declarations.note: choice of auxiliary split primes by a Chebotarev argument and extension of relations (86 lines); part of the Greenberg–Wiles lower bound; the write-up must read it.

declarations.name: exists_divStar
declarations.says: Hilbert 90 for finite ideles: for every norm-one adele u of the CM field E there is a finite idele y such that the finite part of u equals y/ȳ.
declarations.reference: Hilbert's Theorem 90 for the quadratic extension E/E⁺, applied place by place (e.g. J.-P. Serre, Local Fields, Ch. X)
declarations.relation: special case
declarations.note: the idelic form for the norm-one finite adeles of a CM field: u = y/ȳ with y a finite idele (integrality at almost all places included).

declarations.name: mem_integralU1_of_snd_eq_one
declarations.says: A norm-one adele with trivial finite part is integral of every level S.

entries.known_result: Local Tate duality in degree 1, as an upper bound for orthogonal groups of cocycles

declarations.name: IsPotCrys.relIndex_dvd_of_orthogonal
declarations.says: Local duality: L, L' potentially crystalline, perfectly paired by b into ℤ_ℓ(1), Γ → G_ℓ an open embedding, A the image of Z_f(L) in V = L/ℓ^m. If A and S consist of continuous cocycles whose cup products with H bound in ℚ̄_ℓ^×, then [S : S∩A] divides [Z_f(L') : H∩Z_f(L')].
declarations.reference: local Tate duality: J.-P. Serre, Galois Cohomology (1997); J. S. Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems (2nd ed. 2006)
declarations.place: Serre, Galois Cohomology, II §5.2 Thm 2 and §5.7; Milne, ADT, I 2.3, 2.8
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: only an inequality (an index divides an index) for orthogonal groups of cocycles in a potentially crystalline setting, not perfectness of the pairing or the Euler characteristic formula. Places from the file header; REFERENCES.md lists both works as work found, no place given, so the places are unchecked.

declarations.name: exists_perfect_pairing
declarations.says: Let R be a discrete valuation ring, finite and free over ℤ_ℓ, and L a lattice over R. For some ℤ_ℓ-linear form f on R, the map φ ↦ f ∘ φ is a bijection from Hom_R(L, R) onto Hom_{ℤ_ℓ}(L, ℤ_ℓ).
declarations.reference: the trace form and the inverse different, J.-P. Serre, Local Fields, Ch. III

declarations.name: SUnit.dirichlet_unit_theorem
declarations.says: Dirichlet's S-unit theorem: for a finite set S of finite places of K, the S-unit group is finitely generated of rank #S + (number of infinite places) − 1.
declarations.reference: Dirichlet's S-unit theorem (e.g. J. Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, 1999)
declarations.relation: the theorem
declarations.note: finite generation and rank #S + r₁ + r₂ − 1 for S a finite set of finite places; the file header classes it as textbook.

declarations.name: exists_sup_idelesUnitOff_eq_top
declarations.says: For finite sets R, R' of finite places there is a finite S ⊃ R, meeting R' only inside R, such that every finite idele is a principal idele times a unit outside S.
declarations.note: from the finiteness of the class group and the choice, in every ideal class, of an integral ideal prime to a given finite set of primes.

declarations.name: isClosedEmbedding_galois_restrict
declarations.says: For K ⊂ L ⊂ Ω with Galois groups Γ and Γ', a homomorphism φ : Γ' → Γ compatible with the actions on Ω is a closed embedding onto the subgroup fixing L, of index [L:K] (both 0 if infinite).
declarations.reference: infinite Galois theory (J. Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, Ch. IV §1)

declarations.name: isOpenEmbedding_galois_restrict
declarations.says: For K ⊂ L ⊂ Ω with L/K finite and Galois groups Γ and Γ', a homomorphism Γ' → Γ compatible with the actions on Ω is an open embedding.

declarations.name: IsRelAffine.baseChange
declarations.says: Relative affineness of a map of set-valued functors is stable under base change (pull-back squares).

declarations.name: IsRelAffine.comp
declarations.says: A composite of relatively affine maps is relatively affine.

declarations.name: Comparison.IsBijective.trans
declarations.says: Bijective comparison maps of cohomology compose: if two comparisons are bijective and a compatible square commutes, the composite comparison is bijective.

declarations.name: piAbFunctor.lift
declarations.says: Given natural transformations N→F_i for each index i, the natural transformation from N to the pointwise product of the functors F_i having these as components.

entries.known_result: Descent of torsion étale cohomology along v-covers, with excision, transfer and limits

declarations.name: HV.map_comp
declarations.says: Pull-back on cohomology computed on test rings is functorial: (u∘s)* = s*∘u* … in the stated order.

declarations.name: baseChangeOf.ext
declarations.says: Two elements of the base-change functor are equal when their underlying points and ring maps agree (extensionality).

declarations.name: relFreeAb.prod
declarations.says: For subfunctors U ⊂ V and W ⊂ X, the map ℤ[V × X]/ℤ[U × X ∪ V × W] → ℤ[V]/ℤ[U] ⊗ ℤ[X]/ℤ[W] sending [(x,y)] to [x] ⊗ [y].

declarations.name: relFreeAb.restrict
declarations.says: For subfunctors U and W' ⊂ W of V, the map ℤ[W']/ℤ[U ∩ W'] → ℤ[W]/ℤ[U ∩ W].

declarations.name: IsComparableRing.id
declarations.says: Comparability of a ring map passes to the identity of its target ring.

declarations.name: IsTest.pi
declarations.says: A product of any family of test rings (IsTest) is a test ring.

entries.known_result: Bound for the odd part of a twisted Tate–Shafarevich group of an abelian CM field

declarations.name: exists_detecting_points_cocycles
declarations.says: For a number field E inside ℚ(ζ_N) and a prime l there is a finite set S of elements of Gal(Q̄/E), with #S ≤ y²⁰ whenever N ≤ y and l ≤ y², such that every cocycle with values in O/lⁿ(−e) that is unramified outside l (a Selmer class with no local condition imposed above l) and vanishes on S is zero, for all n, e and every l-adic integer ring O.
declarations.note: proved by ray class group generators and a crude count via Minkowski's bound (file header); no published source given; the write-up must read it or cite an effective Chebotarev-type argument.

declarations.name: exists_length_shaOdd_le
declarations.says: For a CM field E in ℚ(ζ_N) and t ≥ 1 there is an integer 1 ≤ X ≤ 2^{4(N+t+3)^27}·h_E (h_E the class number) such that, for every prime l, every 0 ≤ e < t, every n, and every characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring O over ℤ_l with finite residue rings containing the roots of unity of order exp((ℤ/N)^×), the odd part of the Tate–Shafarevich group with coefficients O/lⁿ(−e) has length at most v_O(X).
declarations.reference: B. Mazur, A. Wiles, Class fields of abelian extensions of Q, Invent. Math. 76 (1984); C. Greither, Class groups of abelian fields, and the main conjecture, Ann. Inst. Fourier 42 (1992)
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: The published results give the order of odd isotypic parts (via the main conjecture); here only an upper bound by one explicit integer of size at most an explicit constant times h_E, uniform in l (including l = 2), proved without the main conjecture (Stickelberger annihilation and the Kolyvagin–Rubin bound; small primes by a crude count of ray class generators). Place from the file header; REFERENCES.md: Greither compared, place confirmed; Mazur–Wiles work found, no place given.

declarations.name: IsBesselFunction.enorm_besselS_mul
declarations.says: A Bessel function has the same norm at sy as at y, for s in the Bessel subgroup S.

declarations.name: IsBesselFunction.enorm_integral_besselS_mul
declarations.says: Integrals of a Bessel function translated by s in the Bessel subgroup have the same norm as untranslated: ‖∫β(y)W(sgy)dμ‖ = ‖∫β(y)W(gy)dμ‖.

declarations.name: ascConv_heisenbergMeasure_eq_besselHaar
declarations.says: The measure Shape.besselHaar on 𝖴, viewed on G₁, equals the convolution η₀∗⋯∗η_{ϱ−1} of the measures of the floors.
declarations.reference: header of ComplexPlace: A. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction; S. Helgason, Groups and Geometric Analysis
declarations.note: at ℂ, Haar measure of the unipotent radical of the proof's shape is the product of the Heisenberg floor measures (14 lines); a decomposition of Haar measure in Bruhat coordinates tailored to the shape; the write-up must read it.

declarations.name: exists_chart_ascConv_cellLaw
declarations.says: For each j there is a measurable chart g from (ℂ)^j to G₁, equal to the Weyl element w_j(p) (with the boost on the top floor beyond ϱ), such that integration against the ascending convolution of the cell laws equals integration over (ℂ)^j against the product of the cell densities.
declarations.note: an integration formula for the Weyl part of the big cell (9 lines, using the cell densities); the write-up must read it.

declarations.name: HCParam.HasGap.paramAddRho_lt_iff
declarations.says: For a parameter with a gap, the entries of λ + ρ are ordered as the entries of l.

declarations.name: dsCoeff_eq_flenstedJensen
declarations.says: Independence of the splitting: for a parameter l = 2λ of some gap, g in U(diag ε) and a block diagonal matrix a such that a⁻¹g has positive definite hermitian part, ψ_λ(g) is the normalised integral HCParam.flenstedJensen at (a, a⁻¹g).
declarations.reference: M. Flensted-Jensen, Discrete series for semisimple symmetric spaces, Ann. of Math. 111 (1980)
declarations.note: independence of Flensted-Jensen's integral representation from the splitting; the proof (3 lines here) rests on invariance lemmas of the folder; the write-up must read them.

declarations.name: dsCoeff_inv
declarations.says: For a parameter λ of gap h and g in U(diag ε), ψ_λ(g⁻¹) is the complex conjugate of ψ_λ(g).

declarations.name: dsCoeff_of_mem_maxCompactU
declarations.says: For a parameter λ of gap h and k in K = U(diag ε) ∩ U(n), ψ_λ(k) = m_Λ(k), the product of principal minors of weight Λ = λ + ρ − 2ρ_c.

declarations.name: norm_dsCoeff_le_pow
declarations.says: For a parameter l = 2λ of gap h, a natural number c ≤ h and g in U(diag ε): |ψ_λ(g)| ≤ (2/‖g‖)^c, with the operator norm.
declarations.note: from the decay bound |ψ_λ|²|det a_g|^c ≤ 1 below.

declarations.name: norm_dsCoeff_sq_mul_det_pow_le_one
declarations.says: For l = 2λ of gap h, a natural number c ≤ h and g in U(diag ε): |ψ_λ(g)|²·|det a_g|^c ≤ 1, where a_g is the block diagonal part of g.
declarations.reference: M. Flensted-Jensen (1980); B. Sun, Matrix coefficients of cohomologically induced representations, Compositio Math. 143 (2007), Thm 1.1 (header of the family)
declarations.note: a decay bound for the lowest K-type coefficient whose constant does not depend on the parameter (29 lines); not identified with a published statement; the write-up must read it.

declarations.name: SmoothU.continuous
declarations.says: A smooth function on U(diag ε) is continuous.

declarations.name: one_le_cast_card
declarations.says: A non-empty finite index set has at least one element: 1 ≤ #n.

declarations.name: IsHolOfWeight.mul
declarations.says: Products of holomorphic functions of weights u and v are holomorphic of weight u + v.

declarations.name: IsHolOfWeight.sum
declarations.says: Finite linear combinations of holomorphic functions of weight u are holomorphic of weight u.

declarations.name: IsJointHarmonic.swap
declarations.says: A joint harmonic P for (σ, ε, ε', γ, γ', l, l') is, with rows and columns exchanged, a joint harmonic for (−σ, ε', ε, γ', γ, l', l).

declarations.name: IsMatch.swap
declarations.says: If l, l' match for the data (σ, ε, ε', γ, γ'), then l', l match for the swapped data (−σ, ε', ε, γ', γ).

declarations.name: FockDualPair.IsJointHighest.isPreJointHarmonic
declarations.says: A polynomial jointly highest of the lowest K-type weight for both actions is a pre-joint harmonic.

declarations.name: IsMatch.unique
declarations.says: For matching parameters l, l' (IsMatch), any two polynomials P, Q satisfying FockDualPair.IsPreJointHarmonic are proportional: P = cQ for some complex number c.
declarations.reference: uniqueness of joint harmonics (R. Howe, Transcending classical invariant theory, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2 (1989))
declarations.relation: special case
declarations.note: uniqueness up to a scalar only for matched parameters with large gaps, on Fock space (26 lines).

declarations.name: stdAddChar_half
declarations.says: For a CM field E and x in the adeles, the standard character satisfies ψ((x + x̄)/2) = ψ(x).

declarations.name: idemAdele
declarations.says: The idempotent adele with component 1 at the finite places in S, and 0 at the other finite places and at all infinite places.

entries.known_result: self-duality of a number field in its adeles, strong approximation, and the Poisson inequality

declarations.name: IsDualFamily.sum_le_of_fourier
declarations.says: One-sided Poisson summation on the adeles of E: let F ≥ 0 be integrable and lower semicontinuous at the points of a finite set T ⊂ E. If S bounds all finite sums of |∫ ψ(−ξx)F(x) dx| over ξ in E, then ∑_{t∈T} F(t) ≤ S.
declarations.reference: Poisson summation on the adeles: J. Tate, Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (1950), in Cassels–Fröhlich ch. XV
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: a one-sided inequality Σ_{t∈T} F(t) ≤ S for non-negative integrable F lower semicontinuous at the points of a finite set T, with S a bound for the finite sums of Fourier coefficients, for totally complex E; not the equality. Place from the file header; REFERENCES.md: compared, place confirmed (not re-checked by us).

declarations.name: Space.exists_isUnitary_formTranslation
declarations.says: The space of forms of weight κ on a positive definite V carries an inner product for which right translation is unitary.
declarations.note: average an inner product over the finitely many classes.

declarations.name: eval_heckePoly
declarations.says: The Hecke polynomial at w evaluated at x ≠ 0 is x^n times the reversed evaluation at x⁻¹.

entries.known_result: Landherr's Hasse principle for hermitian forms, and weak approximation for unitary groups

declarations.name: Space.exists_eq_move
declarations.says: Landherr's theorem for spaces with a point: over stably unramified E (StablyUnram), any two spaces V, W with the same signs differ by a rational change of coordinates a and moving the point by some g in G.
declarations.reference: Landherr's Hasse principle for hermitian forms: W. Landherr, Äquivalenz Hermitescher Formen über einem beliebigen algebraischen Zahlkörper, Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg 11 (1936) 245–248; M. Kneser, Lectures on Galois cohomology of classical groups, TIFR 47 (1969)
declarations.relation: special case
declarations.note: only for adelically unimodular spaces of equal signature over a CM field containing the roots of unity of order 5040, stated for spaces with a point (W = a⁻¹Vg); proved from Hasse's norm theorem instead of Hasse–Minkowski. Place from the file header; the file is among those whose citations were not part of the authors' check (REFERENCES.md).

declarations.name: Space.weak_approximation
declarations.says: Weak approximation for U(J): for a finite set S of finite places, a neighbourhood O of 1 in G and g in G, some rational γ has γg = hu with u in O and h in G_f trivial at S.
declarations.reference: weak approximation for unitary groups (M. Kneser, TIFR 47 (1969); V. Platonov, A. Rapinchuk, Algebraic Groups and Number Theory, 1994)
declarations.relation: special case
declarations.note: for U(J) of a space over a stably unramified CM field, in the form that Γ times the elements trivial at a finite set S is dense in G; proved with a Cayley transform and a norm-one scalar (header).

entries.known_result: A prime in a long window (weak form of the Siegel-Walfisz theorem)

declarations.name: exists_prime_modEq_one_log_mem
declarations.says: Let M > 0 be a multiple of 4 and A a natural number. For all large W, every k ≥ 2 with M^k ≤ W^A and every U in [W, W^A], there is a prime p ≡ 1 (mod M^k) with U ≤ log p ≤ U + W.
declarations.reference: H. L. Montgomery, R. C. Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I. Classical Theory, Cambridge 2007 (the Siegel–Walfisz theorem)
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: Siegel–Walfisz gives ψ(x; q, a) = x/φ(q) + O(x exp(−c√log x)) uniformly for q ≤ (log x)^A; here only one prime p ≡ 1 mod q is found, for moduli q = M^k ≤ W^A and log p in the window [U, U+W] with U ≥ W (so q ≤ (log x)^A at x = e^U); no count. The header says the proof starts from a small zero-free disc at 1. Place from the file header; REFERENCES.md: compared, place confirmed (not re-checked by us).

entries.known_result: Zero density for quadratic twists by mean values over real characters

declarations.name: exists_entireL_quadTwist_ne_zero
declarations.says: Let β > 1/2, y > 0, and a a unit mod N such that every prime d ≡ a (mod N) satisfies d ≡ 7 (mod 8) and is prime to N. Then for some prime d ≡ a (mod N), no L̃(s, ξ·(·/d)) with ξ a character mod N vanishes in re s ≥ β, |im s| ≤ y.
declarations.reference: M. Jutila, On mean values of Dirichlet polynomials with real characters, Acta Arith. 27 (1975) 191–198 (zero density for quadratic twists)
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: Jutila's theorem is a zero-density estimate on average over real characters; the Lean statement only extracts one prime d in a residue class whose twists have no zero in a box right of the line re s = β. The header says the proof is a three-lines argument with a smoothed mean square of Jacobi-symbol sums, i.e. not a quotation of Jutila. REFERENCES.md: work found, no place given.

entries.known_result: the class number of an imaginary quadratic field of prime discriminant is odd

declarations.name: isAlgebraic_of_padic
declarations.says: If a complex number x satisfies |ι(x)|₂ ≤ c, with one bound c, for every field isomorphism ι from ℂ onto the algebraic closure of ℚ₂, then x is algebraic over ℚ.
declarations.note: if x were transcendental, automorphisms would move ι(x) to arbitrary transcendental values, contradicting boundedness.

declarations.name: CMLattice.exists_galConjugate
declarations.says: For d a prime ≡ 7 mod 8, a CM datum C and an automorphism σ of ℂ over K = ℚ(√−d), there is a CM datum C' for the same d with a₁(C') = σ(a₁(C)).
declarations.reference: the conjugate of an elliptic curve with CM by 𝒪_K under Aut(ℂ/K) again has CM by 𝒪_K, and it is uniformised by a lattice (J. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, VI.5)
declarations.note: plus the normalisation of the datum.

declarations.name: unitsModule
declarations.says: The multiplicative group Ω^×, written additively, as a discrete module with its continuous action of Γ.

entries.known_result: Global class field theory, covering Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether, reciprocity, existence and norms

declarations.name: artinMap_locIdele
declarations.says: The global Artin map sends the idele with the single component x at v to the local Artin symbol Art_v x.
declarations.note: in this formalisation the global Artin map on finite ideles is the product of the local symbols, so this is immediate.

declarations.name: artinMap_surjective
declarations.says: The global Artin map from the finite ideles of the number field K to the abelianisation of its absolute Galois group Γ is surjective.
declarations.reference: Artin reciprocity (global class field theory): J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory (v4.03, 2020); J. Tate in Cassels–Fröhlich (1967), ch. VII
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: only surjectivity of the Artin map from the finite ideles onto Gal(K̄/K)^ab; the kernel (K^× times the connected component / norms) is not stated here.

entries.known_result: Greenberg–Wiles formula, as a lower bound for the dual side

declarations.name: SplitPlaces.hasFewCocycles_of_central
declarations.says: Let K be totally complex, s auxiliary primes for l^r (r ≠ 0), N and U (SplitPlaces), indexed by ι, with Frobenii φ_i; V finite, l^r-torsion, U-fixed; z central modulo U, fixing l-power roots of unity, z − 1 onto V. If U fixes each l^r-th root, fixed by all φ_i, of a U-fixed N-unit, the trivialised cocycles unramified outside N and s are finite in number, at most (#V)^{#ι+1}.
declarations.reference: the Greenberg–Wiles formula: H. Darmon, F. Diamond, R. Taylor, Fermat's Last Theorem (1995; 2007 text); A. Wiles, Ann. of Math. 141 (1995); J. S. Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems (2nd ed. 2006)
declarations.place: DDT Thm 2.18–2.19; Wiles Prop. 1.6; Milne ADT I 4.10, 5.1
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: only a lower bound for the dual side, under the hypothesis of a central element z with z − 1 onto V; the dual Selmer group is replaced by relations among values on tame inertia at auxiliary split primes, and no local duality is used: the count of trivialised cocycles unramified outside N and the auxiliary primes is at most (#V)^{#ι+1}. Places from the file header; REFERENCES.md: Milne work found, no place given; the other works were not part of the check.

declarations.name: SplitPlaces.card_trivialised_of_isHigmanProjective
declarations.says: Let V be finite, l-torsion, U-fixed, with Higman's property, z − n injective on V, and let U fix zr/rⁿ whenever r^l is an N-unit and all φ_i fix r. Trivialised cocycles number at most (#V)^{#ι+1}, exactly so if K is totally complex and z = n on μ_l.
declarations.note: the counting core of the Greenberg–Wiles lower bound (67 lines), using Higman's property of V; no published statement of this shape is cited.

declarations.name: IsTameGeneratorFor.exists_apply_eq_nsmul
declarations.says: Let A lie over v ∤ m, γ satisfy IsTameGeneratorFor, V be killed by m, and f : G → V be locally constant and additive on inertia. For τ in inertia, f(τ) is a multiple of f(γ).
declarations.note: tame inertia is procyclic modulo the wild part, so f is determined by f(γ).

declarations.name: AutChar.HasWeight.apply_det_eq_prod
declarations.says: Let μ have weight e and tame part ψ, trivial outside finitely many distinct places w_i. For k in the stabiliser K₀ of the standard lattice, μ(det k) = ∏_i ψ_{w_i}(det(k mod w_i)).

declarations.name: IsLocalGalois.of_finite
declarations.says: A finite extension k' of a local field k is local; there are e, f with ef = [k':k], q' = q^f and ord_{k'} = e·ord_k; and #(𝒪'/n) = #(𝒪/n)^{[k':k]} for every natural number n.
declarations.reference: J.-P. Serre, Local Fields, Ch. I–II (finite extensions of local fields)

declarations.name: IsClosedClass.comap
declarations.says: If a property P of functors C → Ab holds for 0 and, in short exact sequences whose first term has P, holds for the middle term iff for the last, then N ↦ P(ΦN) has the same two features, for Φ exact.

declarations.name: IsRelAffine.preimage
declarations.says: The inclusion of the preimage of a relatively affine open subfunctor under any map is relatively affine.

declarations.name: ellAdicPull.comp
declarations.says: Pull-back on the ℓ-adic (inverse-limit) cohomology is functorial: pulling back along α then β equals pulling back along the composite.

declarations.name: IsProperOver.baseChange

entries.known_result: Discrete series character on the compact Cartan by orbital integrals, and the formal degree

declarations.name: Orbital.harish_chandra_degree_and_orbital
declarations.says: Harish-Chandra: for λ of gap 500n³+10n⁵ and signature (p,q), deg_λ = ∏_{λ_j<λ_i}(λ_i−λ_j)/∏_{i<n} i!; for x in the torus with distinct entries, (−1)^{pq} Σ_{σ∈S_n} ∫_G e_λ(g⁻¹(x∘σ)g) dg = p!q!·conj χ(x), χ the character of U(n) of highest weight λ−ρ.
declarations.reference: Harish-Chandra, Discrete series for semisimple Lie groups II: explicit determination of the characters, Acta Math. 116 (1966), with part I, Acta Math. 113 (1965); A. Knapp, Representation Theory of Semisimple Groups (1986)
declarations.place: Harish-Chandra II, Thm 16 (with I, Thm 3); Knapp, Thm 12.7
declarations.relation: special case
declarations.note: only for U(p,q) and Harish-Chandra parameters with a large gap (500n³ + 10n⁵), for the explicit coefficient of the lowest K-type: the formal degree as Weyl's dimension polynomial, and the stable sum of elliptic orbital integrals as p!q! times the conjugate of the compact character, exact in the compact dual measure. Places from the file header; the file is among those whose citations were not part of the authors' check (REFERENCES.md).

declarations.name: lintegral_cayleyDensity_skewColumnEquiv
declarations.says: For J = 1, integrating Cayley's density cayleyDensity over the coordinates θ of row and column k₀, the complementary block η being fixed, gives 2πⁿ/(n−1)! times the density of η in size n−1; both sides are divided by 2πⁿa/(n−1)!, a > 0.
declarations.reference: L. K. Hua (1963), ch. III (integration over sphere fibres; the volume of U(n))
declarations.note: a calculus computation (23 lines).

declarations.name: dsCoeff_eq_holMinors
declarations.says: Holomorphic discrete series: order o with signs +1 first, w K-dominant, w_i+γ ≤ w_j for ε_i = 1, ε_j = −1, γ > 500n³+A+n+1, λ_i = w_i + (n+1)/2 − i with i the rank in o. Then λ has gap 500n³+A and ψ_λ = holMinors ε w on U(diag ε).
declarations.reference: Harish-Chandra, Representations of semisimple Lie groups IV–VI, Amer. J. Math. 77 (1955), 78 (1956); A. Knapp (1986) (highest coefficient of the holomorphic discrete series)
declarations.relation: special case
declarations.note: for products of U(p,q) and large gaps (γ > 500n³ + A + n + 1): the coefficient ψ_λ of the highest vector is the product of principal minors; the bounded domain is replaced by functions on the group extending holomorphically to G·B. REFERENCES.md: Harish-Chandra work found, no place given.

entries.known_result: A cusp form is large only away from the cusps (Siegel's argument)

declarations.name: exists_near_max
declarations.says: Let F ≠ 0 be rapidly decreasing, automorphic of level ς = −ς̄, Im Φ_wς ∈ (0,c], c ≥ 1, holomorphic of weight in [−B,B], B ≥ 2, gap 1. Some z has F(z) ≠ 0, |F| ≤ 2|F(z)|, and |F(g)| ≥ |F(z)| implies Space.firstMinimum(g) ≥ (Bc)^{−½}.
declarations.reference: Siegel's argument that a cusp form is large only away from the cusps: C. Poor, D. Yuen, Linear dependence among Siegel modular forms, Math. Ann. 318 (2000); M. Eichler, Math. Ann. 213 (1975)
declarations.relation: weaker form
declarations.note: for unitary groups over a CM field, highest components of vector weights and forms of rapid decay, with half the supremum in place of an attained maximum, and with an explicit lower bound (Bc)^{−1/2} for the first minimum (the depth) at near-maximal points. Place from the file header; the file is among those whose citations were not part of the authors' check (REFERENCES.md).

declarations.name: IsUnitaryRep.exists_innerProductSpace
declarations.says: For a representation π on X with invariant positive definite hermitian form B as in IsUnitaryRep, there are a complex inner product space H and a linear isomorphism j : X → H with ⟨jx, jy⟩ = B(x,y).
declarations.note: a positive definite invariant hermitian form makes X a pre-Hilbert space.

entries.known_result: Lowest K-type and Casimir value determine a discrete series coefficient; analytic vectors

declarations.name: HCParam.IsKHighest.norm_apply_le_of_mem_filtration
declarations.says: Let l have some gap, IsUnitaryCasimirGe hold, x be K-highest of weight ν, |ν_a| ≤ L. For y in M_s (GlModule.filtration) and any matrix X: Xy ∈ M_{s+1} and ‖Xy‖ ≤ (n+1)⁴(L+1+s)‖X‖‖y‖, with ‖X‖ the operator norm.
declarations.reference: method of the growth of the compact Casimir along the filtration; header sources: R. Parthasarathy, Represent. Theory 19 (2015), Thm 1.1; Hotta–Parthasarathy (1974); Schmid (1975); Vogan–Zuckerman (1984), Prop. 6.1; Nelson, Analytic vectors (1959)
declarations.note: an explicit linear-growth bound for the Lie algebra action along the filtration generated by a K-highest vector (16 lines), the key estimate behind the rigidity result that the lowest K-type and the Casimir value determine the coefficient; the write-up must read it.

declarations.name: IsMatch.exists_isJointHarmonic
declarations.says: If the parameters l, l' match for T (IsMatch), then there is a joint harmonic polynomial Φ in the sense of IsJointHarmonic: nonzero and highest for both lowest K-types Λ and Λ'.
declarations.reference: joint harmonics in the Fock model (R. Howe, Transcending classical invariant theory, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2 (1989); J.-S. Li, Duke Math. J. 61 (1990); A. Paul, J. Funct. Anal. 159 (1998))
declarations.relation: special case
declarations.note: existence of a joint harmonic only for matched parameters with large gaps, for real unitary dual pairs on Fock space. REFERENCES.md: Paul compared, place confirmed (no place in this file's header); Howe and Li work found, no place given.

declarations.name: Lift.DiagTensor

declarations.says: A Galois lattice L over O, crystalline on Γ', with finite sets U_i of integers containing its Hodge–Tate jumps at every embedding γ of O with γ(ζ) = θ(ω(i)), for each letter i (ω(i) the Teichmüller lift).

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Ambient

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Functional
declarations.says: A_inf-linear maps W(C^♭) ⊗ L → B_dR.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Hom.wittMap
declarations.says: For an equivariant map F: L → L', the map 1 ⊗ F: W(C^♭) ⊗ L → W(C^♭) ⊗ L'.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.ainfLattice

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.forms

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.formsOfType

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.fracSpan
declarations.says: The x ∈ W(C^♭) ⊗ L multiplied into the A_inf-span of 1 ⊗ L by some non-zero element of A_inf.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.frobGroup_smul_smul
declarations.says: m·(r x) = (m r)·(m x) for m ∈ ℤ × Γ, r ∈ A_inf, x ∈ W(C^♭) ⊗ L.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.frobKisinAinf

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.jumpBound

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.jumpMultiplicity

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinAinf

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinLocAinf

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.letterOp

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.letterPart

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.letterProj

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mulZeta
declarations.says: Multiplication by ζ on L, as an equivariant endomorphism.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.semilinearAct

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.valueAt

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.valueFieldPoints
declarations.says: For an A_inf-submodule Q of W(C^♭) ⊗ L, the S-submodule of x ∈ Q with μ(x) ∈ 𝒦_0 for every equivariant form μ.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.wittMap
declarations.says: For an O-linear F: L → L', the W(C^♭)-linear map 1 ⊗ F.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.Letter

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.Letter.stepBack

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.LetterRoot
declarations.says: The elements ζ of O with ζ^(p^f − 1) = 1.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.letterFrob

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.letterTeich

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.stdExponent

declarations.name: Lift.TateTwist.smallPart_spec
declarations.says: Artin–Schreier–Witt over the tilt: for M = W(C^♭) ⊗ Z/p^m(1) and S = W(𝔪^♭)·(1 ⊗ 1): p^m kills M, φ − 1 is onto M, φd − d ∈ S ⇒ d ∈ Z/p^m(1) + S, S ∩ Z/p^m(1) = 0; and L(hv − v) ∈ S for h near 1 when ρ is trivial mod p^m near 1.

declarations.says: O is a discrete valuation ring (in particular an integral domain), as a class.

declarations.name: Lift.relLength_le_of_relations
declarations.says: L, L' Z_p-submodules of V with p^t L in L'. If any m+1 elements x_j of L with p x_j in L' have a combination sum a_j x_j in L' with some a_j = 1, then L/(L cap L') has length <= t m.
declarations.note: Induction on t: each layer (L cap p^-1 L')/(L cap L') is an F_p-space of dimension <= m.

declarations.name: Lift.relLength_trans
declarations.says: For Z_p-submodules L, L', L'': if L/(L cap L') has length <= m and L'/(L' cap L'') has length <= n, then L/(L cap L'') has length <= m + n.

declarations.name: PadicIntegerRing
declarations.says: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_l: a DVR of characteristic 0, finite free over Z_l, with finite quotients by nonzero ideals (a class).

declarations.name: QuotSpan
declarations.says: The quotient ring O/aO.

declarations.name: addVal_prod
declarations.says: Over a DVR the normalised valuation of a finite product is the sum of the valuations.

declarations.name: cocycleRels
declarations.says: For rho: Gamma -> M_n(O), the set of matrix-valued finitely supported relations [gh] - [g] - rho(g)[h], one per pair (g,h): obeying them is the 1-cocycle identity c(gh) = c(g) + rho(g) c(h).

declarations.name: comp_mem_obeying
declarations.says: Reducing a function z in Z (functions Gamma -> O^n) modulo a gives an (O/a)^n-valued function obeying every linear relation satisfied by all of Z.

declarations.name: comp_mem_obeying_iff
declarations.says: phi o c obeys the relations R iff phi kills sum_gamma f(gamma) c(gamma) for every f in R (unfolding).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: exists_matrix_addVal_det_le_length
declarations.says: O a DVR, a != 0, aO^n in L in O^n. There are a square matrix M with rows in L and a submodule S of (O/a)^n whose annihilator in O^n is exactly L, with v(det M) <= length S.
declarations.reference: elementary divisor theorem over a PID/DVR
declarations.note: Smith normal form plus duality of finite-length O/a-modules.

declarations.name: fittingIdeal
declarations.says: The zeroth Fitting ideal of R^iota/N: the ideal of R generated by the determinants of square matrices all of whose rows lie in N.
declarations.reference: D. Eisenbud, Commutative Algebra (1995), ch. 20

declarations.name: fittingIdeal.exists_cost_le_relLength
declarations.says: O a DVR, p != 0, p Phi(O^n) in N in R^iota, V a module of functions G -> O/p. Some K >= N contains Phi(v) whenever every linear Psi: O^n -> O/p with Psi o z in V kills v, and some c in O with v(c) <= length(formsMod / V) satisfies c Fitt(K) in Fitt(N).
declarations.note: 'Dividing by a finite-length submodule costs its length in Fitting ideals'; Noetherian induction, one uniformiser per added element. Elementary in method but not a textbook statement: the write-up should prove it (short).

declarations.name: fittingIdeal.sup_smul_top_le
declarations.says: For an ideal I: Fitt(N + I R^iota) is contained in Fitt(N) + I (expand determinants row by row).

declarations.name: fittingIdeal.triangle
declarations.says: If for each j in a finite ordered set I, r_j v_j lies in N plus the span of the v_i (i in I, i < j), then prod_j r_j multiplies Fitt(N + sum_j R v_j) into Fitt(N).
declarations.note: Iterates: r v in N implies r Fitt(N + Rv) in Fitt(N).

declarations.name: formsMod
declarations.says: The O-module of functions g -> Psi(z_g) on G, for O-linear maps Psi: O^n -> O/p vanishing on Phi^-1(N).

declarations.name: length_ker_le_addVal_det
declarations.says: For a square matrix M over a DVR O and p in O, the kernel of M on (O/p)^n has O-length at most v(det M) (uniformiser has valuation 1).
declarations.note: Smith normal form.

declarations.name: length_le_of_le_map
declarations.says: If T' is contained in the image f(S) of a submodule S under a linear map f, then length T' <= length S.

declarations.name: length_mono
declarations.says: Length of modules is monotone under inclusion of submodules.

declarations.name: length_obeying_relationsOn_le
declarations.says: O a DVR, Z a finitely generated O-module of functions Gamma -> O^n (n >= 1): the functions Gamma -> B^n obeying all linear relations of Z have length <= rank(Z) * length(B).
declarations.note: Such functions factor through a module of rank <= rank Z, so they form a submodule of Hom(O^rank Z, B).

declarations.name: mapRel
declarations.says: Apply a ring homomorphism e: O -> O' entrywise to a finitely supported matrix-valued function on Gamma.

declarations.name: mem_obeying
declarations.says: c obeys R iff sum_gamma f(gamma) c(gamma) = 0 for every f in R (unfolding).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: mem_obeying_cocycleRels
declarations.says: c obeys the cocycle relations of rho iff c(gh) = c(g) + rho(g) c(h) for all g, h (unfolding).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: mem_of_forall_form_eq_zero
declarations.says: O a DVR, p != 0, p Phi(O^n) in N. If every O-linear map O^n -> O/p vanishing on Phi^-1(N) vanishes at v, then Phi(v) in N (duality over O/p).

declarations.name: nsmul_quot_eq_zero
declarations.says: If a divides l^M then l^M kills O/aO.

declarations.name: obeying
declarations.says: For a set R of finitely supported matrix-valued f on Gamma, the submodule of functions c: Gamma -> B^n with sum_gamma f(gamma) c(gamma) = 0 for all f in R.

declarations.name: relEval
declarations.says: For a finitely supported f: Gamma -> M_n(O), the linear map c -> sum_gamma f(gamma) c(gamma) from functions Gamma -> B^n to B^n.

declarations.name: relLength
declarations.says: Relative length of submodules S, T: the length of S/(S cap T).

declarations.name: relLength_add_length_inf
declarations.says: length(S/(S cap T)) + length(S cap T) = length(S).

declarations.name: relLength_bot
declarations.says: The relative length of S with respect to 0 is the length of S.

declarations.name: relLength_comap
declarations.says: relLength(S, f^-1 T') = relLength(f S, T') for a linear map f.

declarations.name: relLength_eq_length_map_mkQ
declarations.says: relLength(S, T) is the length of the image of S in M/T.

declarations.name: relLength_iInf_le
declarations.says: relLength(S, T_1 cap ... cap T_k) <= sum_i relLength(S, T_i).

declarations.name: relLength_ker
declarations.says: relLength(S, ker f) = length f(S).

declarations.name: relLength_le_of_inj
declarations.says: If f maps S into S' and x in S with f(x) in T' implies x in T, then relLength(S, T) <= relLength(S', T').

declarations.name: relLength_mono
declarations.says: relLength(S, T) is monotone in S and antitone in T.

declarations.name: relationsOn
declarations.says: The linear relations of Z: finitely supported f: Gamma -> M_n(O) with sum_gamma f(gamma) z(gamma) = 0 for every z in Z.

declarations.name: smul_quot_eq_zero_of_dvd
declarations.says: If a divides p, then p kills O/aO.

entries.known_result: header: part of Poincaré series along a Bessel subgroup, unfolding; unipotent strong approximation (see Lib.Adelic.Poincare.BesselSubgroup). This file holds the proof's vocabulary of shapes, Bessel subgroups and frames, plus Kronecker products, parabolic, unitriangular and Levi subgroups

declarations.name: FI.level
declarations.says: Level function on the basis (e_1..e_ϱ, basis of V_ϱ, e*_1..e*_ϱ): level i−1 for e_i, ϱ on the middle block, 2ϱ−(i−1) for e*_i; block triangularity for it = preserving the isotropic flag ⟨e_1⟩ ⊂ … ⊂ ⟨e_1..e_ϱ⟩.
declarations.note: Lean indices are 0-based: Fin ϱ → i, middle → ϱ, last block i → 2ϱ − i.

declarations.name: Filling.scaleAt
declarations.says: The diagonal matrix with entry p at the index k₀ and 1 elsewhere.

declarations.name: Shape
declarations.says: Shape of a hermitian space V = (ϱ hyperbolic planes ⟨e_j, e*_j⟩) ⊕ X₀ ⊕ ⟨z⟩: the number ϱ, a finite index set κ of a basis of X₀ (rank k = |κ|), and a distinguished index k₀ ∈ κ.

declarations.name: Shape.BesselIndex
declarations.says: The index set of the basis (e_1, …, e_ϱ; basis of V_ϱ = X₀ ⊕ ⟨z⟩; e*_1, …, e*_ϱ) of the whole space of a shape.

declarations.name: Shape.Form
declarations.says: Square matrices over R indexed by the basis of V_ϱ = X₀ ⊕ ⟨z⟩, used as Gram matrices T on V_ϱ.

declarations.name: Shape.Form.G
declarations.says: The unitary group U(V) of the whole space V with Gram matrix splitGram(T) (ϱ hyperbolic planes plus T).

declarations.name: Shape.Form.besselU
declarations.says: The unipotent group 𝖴 ⊂ U(V): elements block upper triangular for the levels with identity diagonal blocks (unipotent radical of the stabiliser of the isotropic flag ⟨e_1⟩ ⊂ … ⊂ ⟨e_1..e_ϱ⟩).
declarations.note: The unipotent part of a Bessel subgroup in the sense of Gan–Gross–Prasad.

declarations.name: Shape.Form.besselU0
declarations.says: The subgroup 𝖴⁰ of 𝖴 of the elements fixing every vector of the frame (e_1, …, e_ϱ, z).

declarations.name: Shape.Form.frameGram
declarations.says: For a matrix γ on V with Gram matrix J: Z(γ) = (h(f_j, γf_l))_{j,l}, the submatrix of Jγ on the frame f = (e_1, …, e_ϱ, z).

declarations.name: Shape.Form.splitGram
declarations.says: The Gram matrix of V: ϱ hyperbolic planes pairing e_j with e*_j (identity blocks), and T as the middle block on V_ϱ.

declarations.name: Shape.MiddleIndex
declarations.says: The index set κ ⊔ {z} of the basis of V_ϱ = X₀ ⊕ ⟨z⟩.

declarations.name: Shape.besselFrame
declarations.says: The positions of the frame (f_1, …, f_n) = (e_1, …, e_ϱ, z) in the basis of V.

declarations.name: Shape.indexX₀
declarations.says: The position in the basis of V of the j-th basis vector of X₀.

declarations.name: Shape.k
declarations.says: The rank k = |κ| of X₀.

declarations.name: Shape.middleGram
declarations.says: For N ∈ R: the Gram matrix on V_ϱ that is the identity on X₀ and −N at z (block diagonal).

declarations.name: Shape.n
declarations.says: The number n = ϱ + 1 of vectors of the frame (e_1, …, e_ϱ, z).

declarations.name: Shape.r
declarations.says: The rank r = 2ϱ + k + 1 of the whole space V.

declarations.name: Shape.top
declarations.says: The last position of the frame, that of z.

declarations.name: Shape.z
declarations.says: The position of z in the basis of V.

declarations.name: SplitIndex
declarations.says: The disjoint union of ϱ indices, a middle index set μ, and ϱ further indices (basis of hyperbolic planes around a middle space).

declarations.name: agreeWithOneOn
declarations.says: For a relation r on indices (with r(i,j) ⇒ r(i,k) or r(k,j)), the subgroup of u ∈ GL_n(R) with u_{ij} = δ_{ij} whenever r(i,j).

declarations.name: blockHom
declarations.says: The homomorphism from the block upper triangular subgroup (for a level function) of GL_n(R) to GL of the level-a block: g ↦ its diagonal block of level a (Levi projection).

declarations.name: conj_mem_unitriangular
declarations.says: If d ∈ GL_n(R) is block upper triangular and u is block unitriangular for the same levels, then d⁻¹ud is block unitriangular (the unipotent radical is normal in the parabolic).

declarations.name: det_eq_one_of_unitriangular
declarations.says: A matrix Z with Z_{ab} = δ_{ab} whenever level(b) ≤ level(a) has determinant 1.

declarations.name: eStar
declarations.says: The position of the basis vector e*_a, in the last block of a split index set.

declarations.name: exists_GL_mul_inclMatrix
declarations.says: Over a field, a matrix b with linearly independent columns extends to an invertible matrix u with u·ι = b (columns ι(j) of u are the columns of b).

declarations.name: frameImage
declarations.says: The columns of γ at the frame positions: the image γf of the frame f = (e_1, …, e_ϱ, z).

declarations.name: frameMatrix
declarations.says: The square submatrix of γ ∈ U(V) on the rows and columns of the frame (e_1, …, e_ϱ, z).

declarations.name: hyperbolicGram
declarations.says: The Gram matrix [[0,0,1],[0,T,0],[1,0,0]] of hyperbolic planes indexed by σ around the middle form T.

declarations.name: inclMatrix_mulVecLin_injective
declarations.says: The inclusion matrix of an injection of index sets defines an injective linear map.

declarations.name: kroneckerPi
declarations.says: The Kronecker (tensor) product ⊗_s A_s of a finite family of matrices: entry at (β, α) is ∏_s A_s(β_s, α_s).

declarations.name: kroneckerPi_mul
declarations.says: Mixed-product property: ⊗_s (A_s B_s) = (⊗_s A_s)(⊗_s B_s).

declarations.name: kroneckerPi_one
declarations.says: The Kronecker product of identity matrices is the identity.

declarations.name: leadingMinor
declarations.says: The leading principal minor D_l(Z): the determinant of the upper-left l × l submatrix of Z.

declarations.name: levi
declarations.says: For a labelling τ of the indices, the Levi subgroup of GL_k(W) (W a local ring): matrices g with g_{ij} = 0 whenever τ(i) ≠ τ(j).

declarations.name: parabolic
declarations.says: The subgroup of GL_n(R) of matrices block upper triangular for a level function lev (a standard parabolic subgroup).

declarations.name: wave
declarations.says: The function c ↦ exp(c − c̄) = exp(2i·Im c) on ℂ, a unitary additive character of ℂ.

entries.known_result: Kisin modules of a Kummer chart inside A_inf: Galois action trivial modulo the variable, Hodge–Tate weights read off (only upper bounds); analogue of Wach-module statements (Berger 2004 §III; Wach 1996)

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Hom.comp_wittMap_mem_forms
declarations.says: Pulling back an equivariant form on W(C^♭) ⊗ L' along 1 ⊗ F, F: L → L' equivariant, gives an equivariant form on W(C^♭) ⊗ L.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Hom.map_mem_kisinAinf
declarations.says: 1 ⊗ F maps the A_inf-Kisin module of L into that of L'.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Hom.wittMap_letterProj
declarations.says: 1 ⊗ F commutes with the letter projections.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Hom.wittMap_mem_frobKisinAinf
declarations.says: 1 ⊗ F maps φ^l(M) of L into φ^l(M) of L'.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.S_smul
declarations.says: Scalars from S act on W(C^♭) ⊗ L through A_inf.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.ainfLattice_eq_span_basis
declarations.says: The A_inf-span of 1 ⊗ L is spanned by 1 ⊗ e_l for a Z_p-basis (e_l) of L.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.apply_eq_of_mem_fracSpan
declarations.says: Two A_inf-linear functionals with the same values on 1 ⊗ e_l (a Z_p-basis) agree on the saturation fracSpan.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.basisValues
declarations.says: The B_dR-linear map sending a functional μ to the vector (μ(1 ⊗ e_l))_l of its values on a chosen Z_p-basis of L.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.comp_letterProj_mem_forms
declarations.says: Composing an equivariant form with a letter projection gives an equivariant form.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.conjForm
declarations.says: The conjugate of a functional μ by g ∈ Γ: x ↦ j(g)⁻¹·μ(g x).

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.exists_span_formsOfType_mod_pred
declarations.says: For O a domain and L potentially crystalline: modulo forms of type u − 1, the forms of type u at the letter i are spanned over Q̄_p by at most Σ_{γ(ζ) = θ(ω(i))} jump_γ(u) of them.
declarations.reference: L. Berger, Limites de représentations cristallines, Compositio Math. 140 (2004), §III; N. Wach, Bull. SMF 124 (1996)
declarations.note: the authors' analogue for Kisin modules inside A_inf of statements on Wach modules; only upper bounds on weights (header)

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.finrank_wittFq
declarations.says: W(F_{p^f}) is free of rank f over Z_p.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.form_gal_smul
declarations.says: An equivariant form μ satisfies μ(g x) = g μ(x) for g in the Galois monoid of the chart and x in fracSpan.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.formsOfType_subset_pred_of_notMem
declarations.says: If n is not an allowed jump in U_i, every form of type n at the letter i is of type n − 1.
declarations.note: corollary of exists_span_formsOfType_mod_pred

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.frobEUnit_pow_smul
declarations.says: Powers of the unit φ^a(E) of W(C^♭) act as the powers of φ^a(E).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.frobEUnit_smul
declarations.says: The unit φ^a(E) of W(C^♭) acts as φ^a(E).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.gal_smul_letterProj
declarations.says: Elements of the chart's Galois monoid commute with the letter projections.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.gal_smul_mem_letterPart
declarations.says: Elements of the chart's Galois monoid preserve each letter part.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.letterProj_mem_letterPart
declarations.says: The letter-i projection lands in the letter-i part.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.letterProj_mk_mem_ainfLattice
declarations.says: The letter projection of 1 ⊗ t lies in the A_inf-span of 1 ⊗ L.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mem_letterPart_iff_letterProj
declarations.says: x lies in the letter-i part iff its letter-i projection is x.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mem_letterPart_iff_mulZeta
declarations.says: x lies in the letter-i part iff ζ acts on x as the Teichmüller lift ω(i).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mk_one_mem_ainfLattice
declarations.says: 1 ⊗ t lies in the A_inf-span of 1 ⊗ L.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.phi_pow_smul_letterTeich
declarations.says: φ^l maps the Teichmüller lift of i⁻¹ to that of (i^(p^l))⁻¹.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.phi_pow_smul_mem_letterPart_iff
declarations.says: φ^a x lies in the letter-i part iff x lies in the part of the letter a steps before i.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.smul_letterProj
declarations.says: If m ∈ ℤ × Γ sends ω(i)⁻¹ to ω(i')⁻¹, then m intertwines the letter-i projection with the letter-i' projection.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.smul_mem_ainfLattice
declarations.says: ℤ × Γ preserves the A_inf-span of 1 ⊗ L.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.smul_mem_fracSpan
declarations.says: ℤ × Γ preserves fracSpan.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.sum_letterProj
declarations.says: The letter projections sum to the identity.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.valueAt_comp_wittMap
declarations.says: valueAt commutes with pulling back along 1 ⊗ F.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.valueAt_frobEUnit_zpow_smul
declarations.says: valueAt_a μ (φ^b(E)^n x) = φ^(−a)(φ^b(E))^n · valueAt_a μ (x) for n ∈ ℤ.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.wittMap_mem_ainfLattice
declarations.says: 1 ⊗ F maps the A_inf-span of 1 ⊗ L into that of 1 ⊗ L'.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.zTauUnit_smul
declarations.says: The unit zτ of W(C^♭) acts as zτ.
declarations.note: unfolding

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting); also part of: theta kernels of unitary dual pairs (Lib/Weil/DualPair/KernelDecay)

declarations.name: AutChar.spaceChar
declarations.says: For a character a of [U(1)] = U(1)(E)\U(1)(𝔸) and k ∈ ℕ, the Hecke character x ↦ a(x/x̄)·υ(x)^{−k} of E (υ the splitting character).

declarations.name: G.det
declarations.says: The determinant, as a homomorphism from the adelic unitary group of signs s to the norm-one adeles {x : x x̄ = 1} of E.

declarations.name: G.onHom
declarations.says: The homomorphism U(S)(𝔸) × U(T)(𝔸) → U(Hom(S,T))(𝔸), (g, h) ↦ (x ↦ h x g⁻¹) on n′×n matrices.

declarations.name: Space.IsThetaFunctional.comp
declarations.says: Transport of theta functionals: composing a theta functional of V with a (semi)linear isometry that carries rational vectors to rational vectors, intertwines Heisenberg operators and keeps the vacuum of norm 1 gives a theta functional of V₁.

declarations.name: Space.add_apply
declarations.says: (f + f′)(x) = f(x) + f′(x), data read as functions x ↦ θ(ϱ(x)f).
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: Space.apply_vecAtPoint_add
declarations.says: Quasi-periodicity under rational vectors: for γ ∈ E^n with image γ′ in adelic coordinates of V, β(γ′, x)·f(γ′ + x) = f(x), where f(x) = θ(ϱ(x)f).
declarations.note: Invariance of the theta functional.

declarations.name: Space.dataInner
declarations.says: The inner product ⟨c, c′⟩ = ∫_{𝔸^n} c̄ c′ on the data space 𝒮(V), conjugate-linear in the first variable.

declarations.name: Space.dataInner_eq_quotMean
declarations.says: Isometry of the theta map: ⟨f, f′⟩ equals the mean over 𝔸^n modulo the rational vectors of conj(f(x))·f′(x), data read as functions f(x) = θ(ϱ(x)f).
declarations.reference: A. Weil, Sur certains groupes d'opérateurs unitaires, Acta Math. 111 (1964)
declarations.note: Part of the theory of the invariant theta functional (orthogonality for the Heisenberg group, Stone–von Neumann); proved in Lib/Weil/Construction/ThetaFunctional.

declarations.name: Space.dataInner_rho_of_vacElem
declarations.says: Vacuum coefficient: ⟨vac, ϱ(y)vac⟩ = e(y) for every adelic vector y, e the vacuum function.

declarations.name: Space.ext_of_vacElem
declarations.says: Two bounded linear maps on 𝒮(V) that agree on all vectors ω(g)ϱ(y)vac (g fixed, y adelic) are equal.

declarations.name: Space.finHeisOp
declarations.says: For a finite adelic vector x, the finite Heisenberg operator ψ(½c₀ȷαᾱ·x*x)·ϱ(αx) on 𝒮(V).

declarations.name: Space.hasSum_dataInner
declarations.says: Poisson-type sum: for f, f′ ∈ 𝒮(V), Σ_{γ rational} ⟨f′, ϱ(γ)f⟩ converges to θ(f)·conj(θ(f′)).
declarations.reference: A. Weil, Sur certains groupes d'opérateurs unitaires, Acta Math. 111 (1964)
declarations.note: Fourier inversion on 𝔸^n/E^n with the theta isometry (Lib/Weil/Construction/ThetaFunctional); a Poisson summation formula in Heisenberg form.

declarations.name: Space.hom
declarations.says: For hermitian spaces S, T the space Hom(S,T), with rational Gram matrix J_T ⊗ J_S^{−T} and adelic frame x_T ⊗ x_S^{−T}.

declarations.name: Space.integrated
declarations.says: The bounded bilinear map (v, f) ↦ v ⊗ f = ∫ v(y) ϱ(y)f dy, v in the Fock space of the real places, f ∈ 𝒮(V), y over real vectors in Fock coordinates.

declarations.name: Space.norm_apply_le
declarations.says: |f(x)| ≤ ‖θ‖·‖f‖ for every adelic x.

declarations.name: Space.projOn
declarations.says: For a set S of finite places, the projection P^S on 𝒮(V): the mean over y ∈ Ô^n of the finite Heisenberg operator at the part of y above S ∪ S̄.

declarations.name: Space.ratMap
declarations.says: For a matrix i over E and spaces V, V′ with adelic frames x, x′, the adelic matrix x⁻¹ i x′.

declarations.name: Space.smul_apply
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: Space.vacElem
declarations.says: The vacuum of 𝒮(V): the Gaussian at the real places times the twisted lattice function at the finite places.

declarations.name: Space.zero_apply
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: WeilData.upsilonU1
declarations.says: The splitting character υ restricted to the norm-one ideles: a character of U(1)(𝔸) trivial on U(1)(E).

declarations.name: detFin
declarations.says: For g in the finite adelic unitary group, det(1, g) as a norm-one adele.

declarations.name: finCoord
declarations.says: For an adelic vector y, the finite adelic vector α⁻¹·y_f (α the finite idele of the Weil data).

declarations.name: finVec
declarations.says: For a finite adelic vector x, the adelic vector with finite part αx and real part 0.

declarations.name: homSigns
declarations.says: For sign vectors s on n and s′ on n′, the sign vector (i, j) ↦ s′(i)s(j) on n′ × n (signs of Hom(S,T)).

declarations.name: matToVec
declarations.says: A matrix read as the function (i, j) ↦ x_{ij} on pairs of indices.

declarations.name: pairChar
declarations.says: For characters a, b of [U(1)], the character (g, h) ↦ a(det h)·b(det g)⁻¹ of U(S)(𝔸) × U(T)(𝔸).

declarations.name: pairTheta
declarations.says: The theta kernel θ^{S,T}_{a,b}(f)(g, h) = θ(ω_{a,b}(g,h)f), f ∈ 𝒮(Hom(S,T)), θ the theta functional of Hom(S,T).

declarations.name: pairWeil
declarations.says: The Weil representation of the unitary dual pair: (g, h) ↦ a(det h)·b(det g)⁻¹·ω(x ↦ h x g⁻¹) on 𝒮(Hom(S,T)), with splitting characters a, b.

declarations.name: rankTwist
declarations.says: For a character a of [U(1)] and an index set of size n, the character a·υ^{⌊n/2⌋}.

declarations.name: realCoord
declarations.says: The archimedean part of an adelic vector y in Fock coordinates: (2π·Im τ(ȷ))^{1/2}·y_{i,τ}, indexed by infinite places τ and coordinates i.

declarations.name: realVec
declarations.says: The additive map ℂ^{Φ×n} → 𝔸^n multiplying the coordinates at τ by (2π·Im τ(ȷ))^{−1/2} and putting 0 at the finite places.

declarations.name: vecToMat
declarations.says: A function y on pairs of indices read as the matrix (y(i,j)).

entries.known_result: Part of: Schrödinger and mixed models of the Weil representation, action of parabolic subgroups (see Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw); this file: splittings along isotropic subspaces, Levi and unipotent radical, adapted points, zero term and mixed model

declarations.name: G.mat_preserves_stdForm
declarations.says: An element g of the adelic unitary group G(s) preserves the standard form: g*·ε·g = ε.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Space.Splitting
declarations.says: A Witt splitting V = (lE^p ⊕ kE^p) ⊥ iV₀ over E: isotropic frames k, l with l*Jk = 1, an isometric embedding i of V₀ orthogonal to both, rk V = rk V₀ + 2p.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.ActsOnFrame.isUnit
declarations.says: If g ∈ G satisfies gk = ka for an adelic p×p matrix a, then a is invertible.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.IsAdapted
declarations.says: g ∈ G is adapted to t ∈ GL_p(𝔸): the matrix g⁻¹(l t*⁻¹, kt, ι) has orthonormal columns at every infinite place and integral entries at every finite place.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.IsAdapted.omega_projOn_of_isMixedLaw
declarations.says: If g is adapted to t, T obeys the mixed-model Heisenberg law, and u = ω(g)P^S f, then T(t*⁻¹αx)u equals P^S T(t*⁻¹αx′)u (x′ the part of x off S ∪ S̄) if x is integral on S ∪ S̄, and 0 otherwise.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.comp
declarations.says: Composite splitting: from V over V₀ (rank p) and V₀ over V₁ (rank q), the splitting of V over V₁ with frames (k, ik′), (l, il′) and embedding ii′.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.exists_eq_radicalElt_mul_levi
declarations.says: Levi decomposition of the parabolic: if g ∈ G satisfies gk = ka, then g = n(c,b)·m(a, g₀) with n(c,b) in the unipotent radical, m(a, g₀) in the Levi subgroup GL_p × G(V₀), and g₀ the restriction of g to V₀.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.frameAt
declarations.says: For g ∈ G and t ∈ GL_p(𝔸), the adelic matrix g⁻¹(l t*⁻¹, kt, ι) with three column blocks.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.gram_frameAt
declarations.says: The Gram matrix of g⁻¹(l t*⁻¹, kt, ι) for the standard forms is (hyperbolic block) ⊕ (standard form of V₀).

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.iAdelic
declarations.says: The embedding i in standard coordinates: ι = x⁻¹ i x₀ (x, x₀ the adelic points of V, V₀).

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.iCoord
declarations.says: The coordinate map ε₀ι*ε sending la + ιw + kb to w.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.isContPeriodic_along_k
declarations.says: For f ∈ S(V), b ↦ f(ιy + kb) is continuous on 𝔸^p and periodic under E^p.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.isMixedLaw_mixedTerm
declarations.says: Heisenberg action in the mixed model: (ϱ(la + ιw + kb)f)[x] = ψ(½ȷ b*(2x + a))·ϱ(w)(f[x + a]) for x, a, b ∈ 𝔸^p, w an adelic vector of V₀.
declarations.note: From the translation laws of the zero term.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.kAdelic
declarations.says: The isotropic frame k in standard coordinates: x⁻¹k.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.lAdelic
declarations.says: The isotropic frame l in standard coordinates: x⁻¹l.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.lCoord
declarations.says: The coordinate map k*ε sending la + ιw + kb to a.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.levi
declarations.says: The Levi embedding GL_p(𝔸) × G(V₀) → G(V), (m, g₀) ↦ the element with k ↦ km, ι ↦ ιg₀, l ↦ l m*⁻¹.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.levi_conj_radicalElt
declarations.says: m(a,g)·n(c,b)·m(a,g)⁻¹ = n(g c a*, a b a*): the Levi subgroup normalizes the unipotent radical.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.levi_mem_Γ
declarations.says: If a ∈ GL_p(E) and g₀ is rational for V₀, then m(a, g₀) is rational for V.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.levi_mul_kAdelic
declarations.says: The Levi element m(a, g) sends the isotropic frame k to ka.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.mixedTerm_zero
declarations.says: The mixed-model slice at 0 is the zero term.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.radicalElt
declarations.says: The unipotent element n(c,b) of the parabolic: k ↦ k, ι ↦ ι + kc*ε₀, l ↦ l − ιc − k(ȷ⁻¹b + ½c*ε₀c), for adelic c (n₀×p) and b (p×p, hermitian part used).

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.realMatrix
declarations.says: The archimedean part of an adelic matrix as one complex matrix, block-diagonal over the infinite places.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.realMatrix_orthonormal
declarations.says: If A is ortho-integral, its archimedean block matrix has orthonormal columns.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.realVec_realMatrix_mulVec
declarations.says: Placing (realMatrix A)y among the adelic vectors equals A applied to the placed vector y.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.symm
declarations.says: The splitting obtained by exchanging the isotropic frames k and l.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.zeroTerm
declarations.says: The zero term (constant term) along k: the bounded map S(V) → S(V₀) with (ev f)(y) = mean of f(ιy + kb) over b ∈ 𝔸^p/E^p.
declarations.note: Defined as a choice from exists_zeroTerm, which proves (via uniqueness of the invariant theta functional) that this mean is given by a bounded map into S(V₀); the write-up must state that existence.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.zeroTerm_rho_kAdelic
declarations.says: The zero term is invariant under Heisenberg translations along k: ev(ϱ(kx)f) = ev(f).

declarations.name: Space.gram_at_point_eq_map
declarations.says: (x⁻¹A)*·ε·(x⁻¹B) equals the image in adelic matrices of A*JB, for E-matrices A, B (x the adelic point of V).

declarations.name: Space.ratMap_mulVec_vecAtPoint
declarations.says: The rational map between spaces in standard coordinates commutes with placing vectors at the adelic points.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: hypSum
declarations.says: The orthogonal sum of the hyperbolic space of rank 2p and V₀.

declarations.name: splittingOfGram
declarations.says: The splitting whose l, k, i are the three column blocks of an E-matrix M with M*JM the Gram matrix of (hyperbolic) ⊥ V₀ and matching ranks.

entries.known_result: Part of: commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n and the Eichler commutation relation (known result stated in Lib/General/LinearAlgebra/ColumnLattices); this file: Hecke operators at split places of unitary groups, Hecke polynomials, eigenforms

declarations.name: FinPlace.IsSplit.star
declarations.says: If w is split (w ≠ w̄) then so is w̄.

declarations.name: Gf.supportedOn_star
declarations.says: The subgroup of G_f supported at w̄ equals that supported at w (the unitary group sees w and w̄ together).

declarations.name: HasHeckePolyAt
declarations.says: At the split place w, f is K_w-fixed, each Hecke operator T_{w,j} acts on f by a scalar t_j, and P = Σ_j (−1)^j q_w^{j(j−1)/2} t_j X^{n−j}.

declarations.name: IsEigenform
declarations.says: f is an eigenform for the system of polynomials P: f ≠ 0 and at almost all places w of prime norm, w is split and f has Hecke polynomial P(w) there.

declarations.name: IsSphericalWith
declarations.says: y is spherical at w (fixed by the part of K₀ at w, w̄) and the Hecke polynomial operator at every X ∈ ℂ acts on y by the scalar p(X).

declarations.name: IsSphericalWith.smul
declarations.says: Scalar multiples of a vector spherical with polynomial p are spherical with p.

declarations.name: IsUnitary.le_span_hecke_eigenvectors
declarations.says: Spectral theorem for Hecke operators: in a unitary representation of G_f, a finite-dimensional subspace spherical at a conjugation-stable set of split places and stable under all T_{w,j} there is spanned by joint eigenvectors.
declarations.note: Finite-dimensional spectral theorem for a commuting family closed under adjoints (T_{w,j}* = T_{w̄,j}), using heckeSplit_comm and heckeSplit_adjoint.

declarations.name: apply_liftResidue_eq
declarations.says: On vectors of level (levelOf H, χ), the lift of a residue family acts like any element of K₀ with the same reductions.

declarations.name: exists_heckeSplit_eq_smul
declarations.says: At a split place w, for each polynomial system p there are scalars t_i such that every y spherical with p satisfies T_{w,i}y = t_i y.
declarations.note: The Hecke polynomial determines the individual eigenvalues (linear algebra in the coefficients).

declarations.name: heckePolyEval
declarations.says: For a sequence t_i in a complex vector space and X ∈ ℂ, Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−X)^i q^{i(i−1)/2} t_i, q the norm of w.

declarations.name: heckePolyOp
declarations.says: The Hecke polynomial at w as an operator: X ↦ Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−X)^i q^{i(i−1)/2} T_{w,i}.

declarations.name: heckePolyOp_adjoint
declarations.says: For a G_f-invariant pairing B, σ-semilinear in the first variable, on spherical vectors B(H_w(X)y, z) = B(y, H_{w̄}(σX)z).

declarations.name: heckeSplit
declarations.says: The Hecke operator T_{w,j} at a split place w: the operator of the double coset of diag(ϖ1_j, 1) in GL_n(E_w), acting through the identification U(n)(E_w × E_w̄) ≅ GL_n(E_w).

declarations.name: heckeSplit_comm
declarations.says: Commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n: for split places w, u and v spherical at both, T_{w,i}T_{u,j}v = T_{u,j}T_{w,i}v.
declarations.reference: T. Tamagawa, On the zeta functions of a division algebra, Ann. of Math. 77 (1963); Gelfand's trick
declarations.relation: special case: the operators T_{w,j} at split places of unitary groups (GL_n(E_w)) acting on spherical vectors; proved by Gelfand's trick (transpose-inverse)
declarations.note: Different places commute trivially; same place uses IsBiInvariant.heckeFun_comm (Lib/General/LinearAlgebra/ColumnLattices).

declarations.name: heckeSplit_dual
declarations.says: If ϖ is a uniformizer and i + j = n, then π(central ϖ at w)·T_{w̄,i}v = T_{w,j}v on spherical v.

declarations.name: heckeSplit_mem_levelSpace
declarations.says: For v spherical at w and of level (K, χ) with K ≤ K₀, T_{w,j}v is again of level (K, χ).

declarations.name: heckeSplit_mem_of_heckePolyOp
declarations.says: If a subspace N contains the Hecke polynomial operators at all X, it contains each T_{w,i}.
declarations.note: Polynomial interpolation.

declarations.name: isSphericalWith_of_heckeSplit
declarations.says: A spherical y with T_{w,i}y = t_i y for all i is spherical with the Hecke polynomial Σ(−X)^i q^{i(i−1)/2} t_i.

declarations.name: jumps
declarations.says: For a weight κ and an embedding σ of E, the multiset over 1 ≤ j ≤ N of j − 1 − λ_j if σ is in the CM type at its place, else λ_j + N − j, where λ_j = κ₂ + Σ_{j≤h<N} κ₁(h) (the Hodge–Tate weights attached to κ at σ).

declarations.name: levelRep
declarations.says: For φ: S → ∏ GL_n(k_{w_i}) normalizing H and fixing χ, the representation s ↦ π(lift of φ(s)) of S on vectors of level (levelOf H, χ).

declarations.name: levelSpace_le_sphericalAt
declarations.says: If a finite set S of places contains neither w nor w̄, every vector fixed by the elements of K₀ trivial at S is spherical at w.

declarations.name: levelSpace_levelOf_apply
declarations.says: On vectors of level (levelOf H, χ), k ∈ K₀ with reductions x ∈ H acts by χ(x).

declarations.name: liftResidue
declarations.says: For distinct places w_i, none conjugate to another or to itself, a chosen element of K₀ supported above the w_i and their conjugates with prescribed reductions s_i ∈ GL_n(k_{w_i}).

declarations.name: liftResidue_mem_supportedOn
declarations.says: The chosen lift is supported above the places w_i.

declarations.name: map_heckePolyOp
declarations.says: A σ-semilinear map intertwining the actions at w carries H_w(X) to H_w(σX).

declarations.name: map_heckeSplit
declarations.says: A σ-semilinear map intertwining the actions of the group supported at w commutes with T_{w,j}.

declarations.name: maxCompactAt
declarations.says: The subgroup of K₀ of elements whose components away from w and w̄ are 1.

declarations.name: mem_sphericalAt_iff
declarations.says: v is spherical at the split place w iff it is fixed by GL_n(O_w) acting through U(n)(E_w × E_w̄) ≅ GL_n(E_w).

declarations.name: reduceFamily_liftResidue
declarations.says: The chosen lift of a residue family s has reductions s at the places w_i.

declarations.name: sphericalAt
declarations.says: The vectors of a representation of G_f spherical at w: fixed by all elements of K₀ whose components away from w and w̄ are 1.

entries.known_result: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz with multiplicity (Alon 1999; Ball-Serra 2009) - but New uses none of it directly: the used declarations are this file's definitions of Schur (dual Weyl) modules, Weyl lattices, Fischer/Fock pairing (part of: standard basis theorem for Schur modules, see Lib.GLn.SchurModule.MinorBasis)

declarations.name: FitsRanks
declarations.says: Branching condition at every place tau: |n_tau| <= |n'_tau| and the column multiplicities kappa_tau(h) vanish for |n_tau| < h < |n'_tau|.

declarations.name: MatrixPoly
declarations.says: The polynomial ring R[y_{a,i}] in matrix variables, rows a in m, columns i in N.

declarations.name: PolyRep.rowPos
declarations.says: A fixed numbering of the rows at the place tau: a chosen bijection n_tau -> {0, ..., |n_tau| - 1}.

declarations.name: WeylIndex
declarations.says: The index set of the standard basis of the Schur module: families, over the places tau, of standard fillings (tableaux) of the shape given by kappa_tau with entries in n (same n at every place).

declarations.name: diagramWeight
declarations.says: The highest weight of the column multiplicities kappa: its value at (tau, i) is the sum of kappa_tau(h) over i < h < N_tau (row lengths of the diagram with kappa_tau(h) columns of height h).

declarations.name: fockPairing
declarations.says: The Fischer (Fock) pairing on polynomials <P, Q> = P(d)Q(0): monomials are orthogonal and <x^d, x^d> = d!.
declarations.reference: E. Fischer's inner product; e.g. R. Howe, Perspectives on invariant theory (1995)

declarations.name: fockPairing_monomial
declarations.says: The Fischer pairing of a y^alpha with g equals alpha! a (coefficient of y^alpha in g), alpha! the product of the factorials of the exponents.

declarations.name: highestPoly
declarations.says: The highest weight vector: product over places tau and heights h < N_tau of the leading principal h x h minor of the block-tau variables raised to kappa_tau(h).

declarations.name: hookNumber
declarations.says: The integer <f, f> = f(d)f(0) for f the highest weight vector highestPoly (Fischer norm of the highest weight vector).
declarations.note: Name refers to its evaluation by hook lengths (Lib/GLn/SchurModule/Hook).

declarations.name: jet
declarations.says: The pairing of a polynomial P with a formal power series F: P(d)F(0) = sum_d d! P_d F_d.

declarations.name: jet_mul_X
declarations.says: jet(f X_i, F) = jet(f, dF/dX_i).

declarations.name: linSubst
declarations.says: Linear change of variables for an m x sigma matrix z: the algebra map R[X_sigma] -> R[X_m], X_b -> sum_t z_{tb} X_t.

declarations.name: minor
declarations.says: For an h-tuple I of rows, the determinant of the h x h matrix of variables y in rows I and the first h columns.

declarations.name: nablaBasis
declarations.says: Standard basis element of the Schur module: for a family i of standard fillings, the product over tau of the minor products (bideterminants) of i_tau in the rows of block tau.

declarations.name: nablaFam
declarations.says: The Schur (dual Weyl) module of prod_tau GL(n_tau): polynomials in the row-coloured matrix variables that are semi-invariant of weight diagramWeight under upper triangular matrices acting on columns.
declarations.reference: induced module H^0(lambda); J. C. Jantzen, Representations of Algebraic Groups (2003), part II

declarations.name: permArray
declarations.says: For maps e_tau from rows to N, the 0/1 array whose entry at row (tau, a), column i is 1 iff e_tau(a) = i.

declarations.name: rankAt
declarations.says: |n_tau|, the number of rows at the place tau.

declarations.name: rowSubst
declarations.says: For matrices z_tau of size n'_tau x n_tau, the algebra map f -> f(z y): y_{(tau,b),i} -> sum_a z_tau(b, a) y_{(tau,a),i}.

declarations.name: schur
declarations.says: The Schur matrix S_kappa(z) of z = (z_tau), z_tau of size n'_tau x n_tau: row i holds the coordinates of b'_i(z y) in the family b_j(y) prod_tau det(y_tau)^{d_tau}; for square z the matrix of the polynomial representation of GL on the Schur module.
declarations.note: Coordinates are chosen (invFun): meaningful only when the expansion exists (e.g. under FitsRanks); d from schurDetExp.

declarations.name: schurDetExp
declarations.says: d_tau = kappa_tau(|n_tau|) if |n_tau| < |n'_tau|, else 0: the determinant power split off when restricting from rank n' to rank n.

declarations.name: tableauPoly
declarations.says: For a filling T and a row map e, the product over the columns of T of the minors whose rows are the e-images of the column entries (a bideterminant).

declarations.name: toPoly
declarations.says: The linear map from coordinate vectors to polynomials xi -> sum_i (G xi)_i b_i, G the Gram matrix of Weyl's lattice and b_i the standard basis.

declarations.name: weylEval
declarations.says: For an array y over R, the vector (b_i(y))_i of values of the standard basis polynomials at y.

declarations.name: weylGramOver
declarations.says: The integer Gram matrix G of Weyl's lattice (coefficients of the kernel f(y^T x) = sum G_ij b_i(x) b_j(y)) mapped into the ring R.

declarations.name: weylKernel
declarations.says: For an array y, the polynomial x -> f(y^T x), f = highestPoly, taken blockwise with the first |n_tau| columns of y: the reproducing kernel of the Schur module.

entries.known_result: Rallis inner product formula by doubling (Weil's convergent range; rapidly decreasing forms); also: critical Hecke L-values of CM fields as squared norms of theta lifts from U(1) (Shimura 1975; Yang 1997; Harris-Li-Skinner 2005); rank-one unramified doubling sum as Euler factor; sharpness of level data

declarations.name: IsConjKernelPair
declarations.says: A pair of functions k(false), k(true) on the real unitary group G_infinity that are complex conjugate to each other and are both cusp kernels of order 0 (kernels defining discrete-series types of automorphic forms).

declarations.name: IsConjKernelPair.form_mem_rapidFunctions
declarations.says: Automorphic forms of type k(d), for a conjugate cusp kernel pair k, are rapidly decreasing.
declarations.note: Direct application of the rapid decay of forms of cuspidal type (Lib/Adelic/CuspForms).

declarations.name: IsEdgeFamily
declarations.says: Hypothesis bundle for a family of theta lifts between discrete-series types: k, k' conjugate cusp kernel pairs, the characters a(i, n), a(i, n') have weights gamma, gamma' independent of i with equal tame parts, and (k d, k' d, harmonic polynomial vector of Phi) is an edge for the real Weil representation of the pair.
declarations.note: Authors' packaging ('edge', 'arrow', 'staircase' in Lib/Weil/Lift) of global theta lifts between discrete-series types (J.-S. Li).

declarations.name: IsEdgeFamily.exists_lift_eq_realConv
declarations.says: Along an edge family with polynomial P, for every polynomial Q there is a compactly supported alpha on G_infinity such that the theta lift with datum Q at infinity equals the real convolution by alpha of the lift with datum P, uniformly in i, S, T, the modulus and the finite datum.
declarations.note: Content from the edge property (Lib/Weil/Lift/Edge): other harmonic polynomials give convolutions of the same lift.

declarations.name: IsEdgeFamily.isArrow_modDatum
declarations.says: Along an edge family, the theta datum with harmonic polynomial P at infinity and any finite part Psi mod m lifts forms of type k(d) on S to forms of type k'(d) on T, and the swapped kernel descends forms of the conjugate types from T to S.
declarations.note: Global theta lifts preserve discrete-series types; content from Lib/Weil/Lift/Edge (cf. J.-S. Li, Theta lifting for unitary representations with nonzero cohomology).

declarations.name: IsEdgeFamily.petersson_descent_eq
declarations.says: Along an edge family with polynomial P, each polynomial Q has a constant kappa, independent of spaces and finite data, with <z, conj(Q-lift of y-bar)>_T = kappa <P-descent of z, y>_S (adjointness of lift and descent up to kappa).

declarations.name: Modulus.flipScalar
declarations.says: The scalar matrix u-bar/u in the finite adelic unitary group of rank n, where u is alpha times the chosen idele generating the modulus m.

declarations.name: cosetRep
declarations.says: For a coset gamma of the subgroup of G_f integral at the places A, the component above A cup A-bar of a chosen element of gamma (a representative supported at A).

declarations.name: cosetTerm
declarations.says: The term rho(g)<y', R(g)y> of a coset gamma, g = cosetRep(gamma), R right translation on forms and rho the vacuum matrix coefficient b(det g)^-1 conj(Delta_f(g^-1))^{-M}.

declarations.name: exists_conj_modKernel_eq_swap
declarations.says: Reversal of a pair: conj(theta^{S,T}_{a,b}[D,P](g,h)) = c theta^{T,S}_{b,a}[D',P'](h, g u), with D' the finite Fourier transform of D-bar, P' the signed transpose of P-bar, u = flipScalar, |c|^2 = N(m)^{-nm} and c independent of D, P, g, h.
declarations.note: A Weil-representation computation (change of polarisation / partial Fourier transform at the finite places dividing m).

declarations.name: exists_hasSum_vacuumCoeff_at_place
declarations.says: Rank-one unramified doubling sum: for nu with trivial tame part at w, w-bar and k > 1, over representatives supported at w, w-bar of U(1)(A_f) modulo the elements integral at w, the vacuum coefficients for (2k, nu upsilon^k) sum to prod_{u in {w, w-bar}} (1 - eps_u q_u^{-k})/(1 - nu~(pi_u)^{-1} q_u^{-k}).
declarations.note: Rank-one case of the unramified computation of the doubling zeta integral (cf. Piatetski-Shapiro-Rallis 1987; Li 1992), done here by a direct coset sum; eps = realZetaCoeff, nu~ the base change of nu.

declarations.name: exists_modKernel_flip_line
declarations.says: For a sign u, S of rank n and k integral: there are an additive character psi of O_E/m and c with |c|^2 = N(m)^{-n} such that theta^{<-u>,S}_{1,b}[D,P](k,h) = c theta^{S,<u>}_{a',upsilon}[D^,P'](h, k u_m) for all P, D, h (D^ the psi-Fourier transform, P' = flipPoly P).
declarations.note: Line case of the reversal of a pair; Weil-representation computation.

declarations.name: hasSum_partialIntegral_coset
declarations.says: Let f be vacuum at A, Phi_c(g) = <f, omega(g)f> c(g) integrable, G_A integral at B, K_D = K_A cap K_B, t_gamma in G_A representing G_f/K_A. Then sum_gamma rho(t_gamma) int_D Phi_{c(t_gamma .)} = int_B Phi_c (partial integrals over points integral at D, resp. B).
declarations.note: Coset decomposition of an integral (Fubini over G_f/K_A) using the vacuum invariance.

declarations.name: inner_product_formula
