entries.known_result: Theta lift for a definite unitary pair as a class sum on algebraic modular forms; seesaw identity for periods of theta lifts; non-vanishing of theta lifts in large rank; Rallis inner product formula by doubling

declarations.name: IsHCParam.paramsCorrespond_iff
declarations.says: For definite spaces of ranks n < n′, κ fitting and l the (Harish-Chandra) parameter of weight (κ, e_c): l and l′ correspond under the theta matching of parameters for weights (e_a, e_b) iff l′ is the parameter of (κ, e_a).
declarations.note: Combinatorics of parameters (finite check); combinatorial form of the Kashiwara–Vergne highest-weight correspondence for compact dual pairs.

declarations.name: IsSharp.partialIntegral_eq
declarations.says: For finite data F sharp of mass c at level J, φ = v ⊗ F, y right J-invariant, u finite: c ≠ 0 and the integral over g integral off S₀ of ⟨φ, ω(g)φ⟩⟨y′, R(ug)y⟩ equals c ∫_{real x} ⟨v, Ω(x)v⟩⟨y′, R(xu)y⟩ dx.
declarations.note: Factorisation using that the finite matrix coefficient of sharp data is c times an indicator; 'sharp data' is a device of this artifact (Lib/SiegelWeil/RallisInner/SharpData).

declarations.name: Space.height_reindex
declarations.says: The height function of a hermitian space is unchanged when the coordinates are reindexed (by a bijection of index sets).
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: Space.integrable_moderate_mul_forms
declarations.says: For a rapidly decreasing (cusp-kernel) form f on U(S), a bounded form y on U(T), a continuous moderate weight M and map j: z ↦ M(z) f(z) y(j(z) r) is integrable on [U(S)].

declarations.name: Space.periodPairing
declarations.says: The period pairing (f, y) ↦ ∫_{[U(S)]} M(z) f(z) y(j(z) r) dz of forms f on U(S), y on U(T), for a continuous moderate weight M, a continuous map j: U(S) → U(T) and a real point r.

declarations.name: exists_lift_ofAlgForm_eq_smul
declarations.says: Definite pair U(n)×U(n′), n<n′, fitting weights, corresponding parameters l, l′, scale c≠0: there is β with: for every theta kernel at level K and algebraic form φ, the adelic theta lift (joint harmonic ⊗ f) of F_φ equals β[K₀:K]⁻¹ F_{φ′}, φ′ the class-sum lift of φ.
declarations.reference: B. Gross, Algebraic modular forms, Israel J. Math. 113 (1999); Kashiwara–Vergne (1978); Howe, Transcending classical invariant theory, JAMS 2 (1989)
declarations.note: Header: known result (theta lift for a definite unitary pair as a class sum on algebraic modular forms); the constant β is left unspecified; no published statement identified to compare with.

declarations.name: integral_eq_zero_of_lift_eq_zero
declarations.says: Rallis's injectivity of the theta lift in the stable range (step): rk S = n, rk T = m, 2n < m, φ = v⊗F, F sharp at J, y J-invariant rapidly decreasing with zero lift: ∫_{real x} ⟨v, Ω(x)v⟩⟨y′, R(x)y⟩ dx = 0 for every rapidly decreasing y′.
declarations.reference: S. Rallis, Injectivity properties of liftings associated to Weil representations, Compositio Math. 52 (1984); J.-S. Li, Crelle 428 (1992)
declarations.relation: weaker form: concludes only that the integral of the real matrix coefficient against ⟨y′, R(x)y⟩ vanishes (no L-functions), for unitary groups with m > 2n and finite data sharp at a level; injectivity is drawn from it in rallis_inner_product_euler
declarations.note: Proved from the inner product formula of Lib/SiegelWeil/RallisInner/SharpData (other chunk).

declarations.name: rallis_inner_product_euler
declarations.says: Rallis inner product formula (doubling): rk T > 2 rk S, v an edge from type e: there is A ≠ 0 such that for F sharp at J of mass c the lift L by v⊗F is injective on J-invariant forms y and ⟨Ly′, Ly⟩ = A c Σ_γ ρ(γ)⟨y′, R(γ)y⟩ (sum over cosets off S₀).
declarations.reference: S. Rallis, Injectivity properties of liftings associated to Weil representations, Compositio Math. 52 (1984)
declarations.relation: special case: stable range m > 2n (absolutely convergent theta integrals, no regularisation) for unitary groups and finite data sharp at a level, where the doubling integral becomes an explicit coset sum; the real constant A ≠ 0 is not computed
declarations.note: Also yields injectivity of the lift (Rallis's non-vanishing).

declarations.name: seesaw_periods
declarations.says: Seesaw identity (Kudla): for edges S → T and T′ → S′ whose kernels agree up to moderate factors on a spanning set of Fock polynomials, if finite sums of periods of f against lifts of y are proportional to (c_o) at every real translate, so are the sums of periods of y against descents of f.
declarations.reference: S. Kudla, Seesaw dual reductive pairs, in Automorphic forms of several variables (Katata 1983), Progr. Math. 46, Birkhäuser 1984, 244–268
declarations.relation: weaker form: transfers a proportionality of finite sums of weighted periods from lifts to descents under a spanning hypothesis, instead of the equality of the two period integrals; the proof is Fubini
declarations.note: Citation given in the file header only; REFERENCES.md lists Kudla 1984 for other files (work found, no place given).

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: Sat.of_mem
declarations.says: If g ∈ S then u = 1 is saturating for g (u, gu ∈ S and lu + m·gu = 1 with l, m ∈ S).
declarations.note: Trivial.

declarations.name: Sat.v_det_saturatingElem
declarations.says: For b ∈ GL_n(𝔸_f) and the chosen saturating matrix u (uÔⁿ = Ôⁿ ∩ b⁻¹Ôⁿ): at each finite place w, det u and det y have the same valuation for any local saturating y of b_w.
declarations.note: Uniqueness of Λ ∩ b⁻¹Λ up to GL_n(O_w).

declarations.name: chiAdelic
declarations.says: The character x ↦ υ(x)|x|^{−1/2} of the ideles of E, υ the splitting character of the Weil data and |x| the idele norm.

declarations.name: chiFin
declarations.says: The character x ↦ υ(x)|x|^{−1/2} of the finite ideles of E (x extended by 1 at the infinite places).

declarations.name: finMultiplier
declarations.says: For g in the finite adelic unitary group, the multiplier Δ_f(g) of its underlying matrix (finite factor of the normalisation of the Weil representation).

declarations.name: finMultiplier_inv
declarations.says: For g in the finite adelic unitary group, Δ_f(g⁻¹) is the complex conjugate of Δ_f(g).

declarations.name: glMultiplier
declarations.says: For g ∈ GL_n(𝔸_f): Δ_f(g) = υ(det λ)|det λ|^{−1/2}, λ a chosen invertible matrix with λ, gλ integral and lλ + m·gλ = 1 for integral l, m (so λÔⁿ = Ôⁿ ∩ g⁻¹Ôⁿ).
declarations.note: |Δ_f(g)|² is the index [Ôⁿ : Ôⁿ ∩ g⁻¹Ôⁿ] (proved in the same file).

declarations.name: mem_subring_matrix_iff
declarations.says: A matrix lies in M_n(S) iff all its entries lie in S.
declarations.note: Unfolding.

entries.known_result: Part of: theta kernels of unitary dual pairs: functoriality, seesaw, growth, rapid decay (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/KernelDecay)

declarations.name: PairFock
declarations.says: The Fock space for the signs s′_i s_j of Hom(S,T), one factor at every infinite place.

declarations.name: pairHomInf
declarations.says: The homomorphism from real points (x, y) of U(S)×U(T) to the real unitary group of Hom(S,T): z ↦ y_w z x_w⁻¹ at each infinite place w, as one block-diagonal matrix.

declarations.name: pairThetaKer
declarations.says: The theta kernel of the pair (S, T) with characters a, b: the representation ω_{a,b} on 𝒮(Hom(S,T)) with the theta functional of Hom(S,T).

declarations.name: pairWeil_integrated
declarations.says: If a, b have weights γ, γ′, then for real points x, y: ω_{a,b}(x, y)(v⊗f) = (Ω(x,y)v)⊗f, Ω the real Weil representation of the pair of weights γ, γ′.

declarations.name: pairWeil_integrated_all
declarations.says: ω_{a,b}((x,k),(y,k′))(v⊗f) = (Ω(x,y)v) ⊗ (ω_{a,b}(k,k′)f): real and finite components act separately.

declarations.name: pairWeil_integrated_fin
declarations.says: Finite points act on the finite factor only: ω_{a,b}(k,k′)(v⊗f) = v⊗ω_{a,b}(k,k′)f.

declarations.name: pairWeil_integrated_right
declarations.says: ω_{a,b}(1, h)(v⊗f) = (Ω_{γ,0}(1,h)v)⊗f for a real point h of U(T).

declarations.name: realPairWeil
declarations.says: The real Weil representation of the pair with weights γ, γ′ on the Fock space: (x, y) acts by ∏_w (det y_w)^{γ_w}(det x_w)^{−γ′_w} times the Fock operator of z ↦ y z x⁻¹.

declarations.name: realPairWeil_polyVector
declarations.says: For x, y block diagonal (maximal compact subgroups U(p)×U(q), U(p′)×U(q′)): Ω(x,y)v_P = ∏_w (det y⁺)^{γ−q}(det y⁻)^{γ−p}(det x⁺)^{q′−γ′}(det x⁻)^{p′−γ′}·v_Q, Q obtained from P by the linear substitution z ↦ y z x⁻¹ (or its contragredient on negative blocks).
declarations.note: Standard Fock-model formula for the action of the maximal compact subgroup; 22-line computation.

entries.known_result: Part of: theta kernels of unitary dual pairs: functoriality, seesaw, growth, rapid decay (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/KernelDecay); part of: Schrödinger and mixed models (Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw)

declarations.name: IsTargetBounded.isAutFunction_thetaIntegral
declarations.says: For target-bounded data f the theta integral g ↦ ∫_{[U(T)]} θ_{α,β}(f)(g,h) dh is an automorphic function on U(S) (continuous, left invariant under rational points).
declarations.note: Dominated convergence.

declarations.name: ReadsAt.isSchwartzBruhat
declarations.says: If π: 𝔸_f → F (F semilocal) reads the places A and φ is Schwartz–Bruhat on n′×n matrices over F, then x ↦ φ(π(x)) is Schwartz–Bruhat above A.

declarations.name: ReadsAt.isTargetBounded
declarations.says: A local datum v⊗φ with v rapid and φ Schwartz–Bruhat supported on matrices of full rank is target-bounded: |θ_{α,β}(f)(g,h)| ≤ C·ht(g)^B uniformly in h and the characters.
declarations.note: Specialisation (N = 0) of pairTheta_decay_of_onto (KernelDecay, substantial).

declarations.name: ReadsAt.pairWeil_localDatum_of_mem_Kf
declarations.says: For integral finite g, h: ω_{α,β}(g,h)(local datum of φ) = α(det h)β(det g)⁻¹·(local datum of φ(h⁻¹ · g)).

declarations.name: exists_linear_thetaIntegral
declarations.says: There is a linear map Λ on data agreeing with the theta integral on all target-bounded data.
declarations.note: Linear extension from a subspace.

declarations.name: lineTermReal
declarations.says: Real counterpart of the line term: the slice, in the mixed model of the adapted splitting chosen for the two-line expansion, at the point with last coordinates a ∈ ℂ^f and the others 0.

declarations.name: realSlice
declarations.says: The slice of a real datum for (X, V) at the real part of an adelic matrix x: its value in the mixed model of the splitting D, a real datum for (W₁, V).

declarations.name: thetaIntegral_pairWeil
declarations.says: Equivariance of the theta integral: (theta integral of ω_{α,β}(p)f)(g) = (theta integral of f)(g·p₁).

declarations.name: thetaLarge
declarations.says: The theta integral over [U(T)] of the datum v⊗Φ (Φ placed at the ramified places of the tame character 𝔠), both characters being ν⁻¹υ^{⌊n/2⌋}, n = rk S.

entries.known_result: Part of: mixed models of the Weil representation (Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw); tower property (Lib/SiegelWeil/Tower/LargeSideConstantTerm); singular forms governed by coefficients at unimodular indices (Lib/SiegelWeil/SingularForms/SingularForms); this file: archimedean Tate integral of slices, finite slices of framed data, Fourier coefficients under shears

declarations.name: IsEquivariantLift.centreCoeff_shear
declarations.says: For an equivariant lift 𝒟 (Schwartz–Bruhat data at S → automorphic functions, equivariant up to ρ(det)), if mat ν = 1 + (e·ck − ē·B) with kc = 0, then the shear Ψ′ of Ψ ∈ M stays in M and the T-th Fourier coefficient of 𝒟Ψ′ at x equals that of 𝒟Ψ at ν⁻¹x.
declarations.note: From the equivariance law and det(1 + ck) = 1 when kc = 0.

declarations.name: IsEquivariantLift.comp_mul_mem_ker
declarations.says: For an equivariant lift, M ∩ ker 𝒟 is stable under Ψ ↦ Ψ(g·) for g ∈ GL_m at the places S.

declarations.name: IsEquivariantLift.exists_linear_centreCoeff
declarations.says: At each point x, Ψ ↦ (T-th Fourier coefficient of 𝒟Ψ at x) extends to a linear functional L on Schwartz–Bruhat data; shearing Ψ by z along the frame k multiplies LΨ by ψ(tr(T_S z)), T_S = T divided by the inverse-different idele, read at S.

declarations.name: ReadsAt.hasIntegralConductor_psi
declarations.says: If π: 𝔸_f → F reads the components at S, the induced additive character ψ of F has conductor exactly O.

declarations.name: ReadsAt.sourceTerm_localDatum
declarations.says: For an adapted splitting, y = x_f and a Schwartz–Bruhat Φ with Φ(w) = 1_O(w)G(wk | wι) on wk = πy: the mixed-model slice of v⊗Φ at κx vanishes unless y is integral, and then equals c·(real slice of v)⊗(z ↦ 1_O(z)G(πy | z)), c the vacuum factor.
declarations.note: Partial Fourier transform computation in the mixed model.

declarations.name: SplitTameChar.invOnUnits_mul_div_star
declarations.says: For a split tame character (χ, ν) and an idele u that is a unit everywhere, χ⁻¹(u_S)·ν_f(u)/χ⁻¹(ū_S) = 1 (unit law of a tame character).

declarations.name: adaptedFrame
declarations.says: For an adapted splitting, the images under π (reading the places S) of the finite parts of the adelic frame (k, ι, l) and its dual frame, as an integral frame (mutually inverse integral matrices) over F.

declarations.name: coneIntegrand
declarations.says: The integrand of the cone integral at (k, t): ∏_x (t_x/|t_x|)^{2μ(x)}·(∏|t_x|²)^σ times the real slice at t of the datum v moved by the real part of k ∈ the maximal compact.

declarations.name: integrable_coneIntegrand
declarations.says: For adapted splittings along isotropic lines, σ ≥ 1 and a rapid real datum v, the cone integrand is integrable, its integral is a rapid datum, and each weighted moment of the integrand is dominated by an integrable function.
declarations.note: Archimedean Tate-integral convergence estimate via the mixed-model slice bounds.

entries.known_result: Part of: Schrödinger and mixed models of the Weil representation, action of parabolic subgroups (see Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw); this file: names (Schrödinger-model data at a set of places) under products and changes of coordinates

declarations.name: Space.boxProd_name
declarations.says: Names multiply on vacua: for S disjoint from S̄ and Ψ, Ψ′ Schwartz–Bruhat above S, (Ψ⊗vac) ⊠ (Ψ′⊗vac) = Θ⊗vac with Θ(x) = Ψ(x₁)Ψ′(x₂) on the two blocks of coordinates.

declarations.name: Space.boxProd_projOn
declarations.says: Along a splitting of coordinates, the external product respects the vacuum projections above S: P^S f₁ ⊠ P^S f₂ = P^S(f₁ ⊠ f₂).

declarations.name: Space.name_mem_finitePart
declarations.says: Naming any Ψ at any set S of finite places maps the finite part 𝒲_f of S(V) into itself.

declarations.name: Space.name_union
declarations.says: For disjoint S, T with S ∪ T disjoint from its conjugate and Ψ, Ψ′ Schwartz–Bruhat on S, T: (ΨΨ′)⊗f named at S ∪ T equals Ψ⊗(Ψ′⊗f).

declarations.name: Std.map
declarations.says: For a change of coordinates φ (with a twist σ, an isometric ring automorphism of ℂ) compatible with β and the vacua, the continuous σ-semilinear map S(V₁) → S(V), c ↦ σ∘c∘φ.

declarations.name: Std.map_integrated
declarations.says: A change of coordinates commutes with inserting a Fock vector at the real places: D(v⊗f) = (D_∞ v)⊗(Df).

declarations.name: Std.map_name
declarations.says: If the finite part B of a change of coordinates D carries S′-parts to S-parts (and their conjugate closures likewise), D sends Ψ⊗vac named at S to (σ∘Ψ∘B)⊗vac named at S′.

declarations.name: Std.realMap
declarations.says: For a change of coordinates with archimedean part A and twist σ, the σ-semilinear map of Fock spaces v ↦ σ∘v∘A.

declarations.name: Std.starCoordEquiv
declarations.says: For a bijection e, units u_i of a topological ring R with involution τ, the additive homeomorphism x ↦ (u_i·τ(x_{e(i)}))_i.

entries.known_result: header: part of the branching law GL(n+1)→GL(n) and of the contravariant form on Weyl's lattice (see Branching, DeltaForms); this file: Gram norm, Zariski density of U(n), Cartan multiplication (integral, isometric, equivariant, split), submultiplicativity of norms.

declarations.name: PolyRep.coe_weylNormSq
declarations.says: The Gram norm ‖ξ‖² = Re(ξ*Gξ) equals ξ*Gξ as a complex number (G the integer Gram matrix, symmetric).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: PolyRep.star_weylEval
declarations.says: The complex conjugate of the evaluation vector ev_y equals the evaluation vector at the conjugate array ȳ (the basis polynomials have integer coefficients).

declarations.name: PolyRep.weylNormSq_weylEval_permArray
declarations.says: For enumerations e_τ of the rows, the evaluation vector at the permutation array of e (the extremal vector) has Gram norm 1.

declarations.name: weylNormSq
declarations.says: The Gram (contravariant) norm ‖ξ‖² = Re(ξ*Gξ) of a complex coordinate vector ξ of weight κ, G the integer Gram matrix of the Weyl lattice.

declarations.name: weylNormSq_comp_smul
declarations.says: For a multiplicative map σ: ℂ→ℂ, ‖σ∘(tξ)‖² = |σ(t)|²·‖σ∘ξ‖².

declarations.name: weylNormSq_le_mul_of_toPoly_eq
declarations.says: Submultiplicativity of the Gram norm under the Cartan product: if the polynomial attached to ζ (weight κ+κ') is the product of those attached to ξ (weight κ) and η (weight κ'), then ‖ζ‖² ≤ ‖ξ‖²‖η‖².
declarations.note: Proof: the matrix C of products of basis minor products satisfies Cᵀ(G_κ⊗G_κ')C = G_{κ+κ'} (isometric Cartan embedding, proved in the same file), then Cauchy–Schwarz for the positive form G_κ⊗G_κ'.

declarations.name: weylNormSq_nonneg
declarations.says: ‖ξ‖² ≥ 0 (the Gram matrix is positive definite).

declarations.name: weylNormSq_smul
declarations.says: ‖tξ‖² = |t|²‖ξ‖² for t ∈ ℂ.

entries.known_result: header: lemmas on Weyl representations, their Gram form and the highest vector, used to turn algebraic forms into functions on G.

declarations.name: Space.IsStd.std_induction
declarations.says: Induction principle: a property of hermitian spaces V marked standard holds for all of them once it holds for the standard space I_n (signs 1).
declarations.note: Lean bookkeeping

declarations.name: algFormCoeff
declarations.says: For a linear functional L on the coordinate space of weight κ, the map sending an algebraic form φ to the function g ↦ L(ρ(g_∞)⁻¹φ(g_f)) on G = U(ℝ)×U(𝔸_f) (matrix coefficients of algebraic forms).

declarations.name: conj_gramForm
declarations.says: The Gram form is hermitian: conj⟨ξ,η⟩ = ⟨η,ξ⟩.

declarations.name: exists_equiv_decrPosition
declarations.says: For an injective l: n → ℤ there is an enumeration e of n with #{j : l_j > l_a} = e(a) and #{j : −l_j > −l_a} = |n|−1−e(a).

declarations.name: gramForm_highestVector_self
declarations.says: If each l_w is injective, the highest vector v⁺ attached to l is a unit vector: ⟨v⁺,v⁺⟩ = 1.

declarations.name: ofAlgForm
declarations.says: The map φ ↦ F_φ from algebraic forms of weight (κ,e) to functions on G, F_φ(g) = ⟨v⁺, ρ(g_∞⁻¹)φ(g_f)⟩, v⁺ the highest vector for the parameter l.

declarations.name: star_highestVector
declarations.says: The highest vector v⁺ is real (equals its complex conjugate).

declarations.name: weylRep_coeff_eq_prod_weightMinors
declarations.says: The diagonal matrix coefficient ⟨v,ρ(g)v⟩ of the extremal vector v of weight (κ,e) is ∏_τ m(g_τ), m the product of (leading) minors to the powers e_τ + λ(τ,p_τ(i)).
declarations.note: Matrix coefficient of an extremal weight vector as a product of minors (standard).

entries.known_result: header: integral finite adeles of a CM field with 5040-th roots of unity satisfy the adelic-ring axioms; adelic index of a field element is its absolute norm (product formula); saturation, indices, discriminant of an orthogonal complement in a unimodular adelic lattice

declarations.name: Filling.jacobi_perp_discriminant
declarations.says: R in A an adelic pair, J hermitian unimodular, F integral, n primitive with F^H J n = 0 and complementary sizes, N = Gram matrix of (F|p) for J plus c on the p-block. If F is left invertible or [det N] != 0: n^perp lies in the span of F and [det n^H(J + c^-1 J p p^H J) n] i^2 [c]^|rho| = [det N], i = [{y : Fy integral} : R^sigma].
declarations.note: Discriminant of an orthogonal complement in a unimodular lattice, modified by a rank-|rho| block; proof by Jacobi's complementary-minor identity and index computations. Tailored to New/Filling (namespace Filling); [x] = generalised index.

declarations.name: Filling.submoduleIndex_dvd_of_le
declarations.says: For an R-linear map P and submodules: if D lies in P^-1(K) and K' lies in P(M) + K, then [K' : K cap K'] divides [M : D cap M].

declarations.name: exists_isPrimitiveMatrix_mul_fromBlocks
declarations.says: For an adelic pair R in A and a left-invertible matrix m with columns indexed by sigma + tau, there are a in GL_sigma(A), e in GL_tau(A) and z such that m times the block upper-triangular matrix [[a, z], [0, e]] is primitive over R.
declarations.note: Block-triangular saturation, from the valuation-pair property of R.

declarations.name: exists_preimageLattice_eq_colLattice
declarations.says: For an adelic pair R in A and a left-invertible matrix m over A, there is a in GL(A) whose columns span {y : m y integral} over R, with m a primitive over R.

declarations.name: genIndex_algebraMap
declarations.says: Product formula (finite part): for x in a number field E, the generalised index of x in the finite adeles of E equals |N_{E/Q}(x)| (0 for x = 0).
declarations.reference: product formula for number fields, e.g. J. Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory (1999), ch. III
declarations.relation: special case: the finite-adelic half of the product formula, equivalently N((x)) = |N_{E/Q}(x)| for the principal ideal (x)
declarations.note: Header: 'Adelic index of a field element equals its absolute norm (product formula)'.

declarations.name: genIndex_det_conj
declarations.says: For square matrices H, J over A (adelic pair): genIndex(det(J^H H J)) = genIndex(det H) genIndex(det J)^2.
declarations.note: Multiplicativity of the Haar modulus and its invariance under the involution.

declarations.name: genIndex_natCast
declarations.says: For a CM field E and a natural number k: the generalised index of k in the finite adeles of E is (k^{#infinite places of E})^2 = k^{[E:Q]}.

declarations.name: ne_zero_and_le_of_dvd
declarations.says: For natural numbers: if b != 0 and a | b, then a != 0 and a <= b.

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of measure and integration, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: distribHaarChar_GL_eq_det
declarations.says: Let R be a locally compact Polish commutative ring with a compact open subring O forming a valuation pair. Then g ∈ GL_n(R) scales Haar measure on R^n by the same factor as det g scales Haar measure on R: mod_{R^n}(g) = mod_R(det g).
declarations.reference: A. Weil, Basic Number Theory (1967), ch. I
declarations.note: Classical for local fields; here for rings with a Smith normal form, proved by reducing to diagonal matrices.

declarations.name: genIndex
declarations.says: The multiplicative function on R sending a unit a to the inverse of its module (the factor by which x ↦ ax scales additive Haar measure), and non-units to 0; for a local field it is |a|⁻¹.

declarations.name: genIndex_det_eq_one
declarations.says: For V ∈ GL_n(O), O compact open: the inverse module of det V is 1.

declarations.name: genIndex_eq_card
declarations.says: For O a compact open subring and a ∈ O a unit of R: the inverse module of a equals #(O/aO).

declarations.name: genIndex_pos
declarations.says: The inverse module of a unit is positive.

declarations.name: map_restrict_haar_eq
declarations.says: For μ bi-invariant on Z, η left-invariant on G, π: Z → G a measurable homomorphism and O ⊂ Z such that every h ∈ G has a preimage normalising O on both sides: η(K)·π_*(μ|_O) = μ(π⁻¹K ∩ O)·η⁻ (η⁻ the inverted measure), a left-invariant measure.
declarations.note: Uniqueness of Haar measure applied to the push-forward.

declarations.name: map_smul_eq_inv_distribHaarChar_smul
declarations.says: The push-forward of an additive Haar measure ν under x ↦ a·x is mod(a)⁻¹·ν.

declarations.name: measure_le_of_div_mem
declarations.says: For a right-invariant measure ζ on a group: if (for each y ∈ E) there is g with Eg⁻¹ ⊂ K, then ζ(E) ≤ ζ(K).

entries.known_result: header: part of pseudocharacters, Brauer–Nesbitt, Clifford; compact subgroups of GL_n stabilise a lattice (see Lib.GaloisRep.Pseudocharacter.FibreSum); this file: integer rings of finite Galois extensions of ℚ_ℓ, length versus cardinality, stable lattices

declarations.name: CoeffRing
declarations.says: The (directed) set of rings of integers O_L of finite Galois extensions L of ℚ_ℓ inside ℚ̄_ℓ (coefficient rings).

declarations.name: CoeffRing.dvd_iff_norm_le
declarations.says: In O = O_L: x divides y iff |y| ≤ |x|.

declarations.name: CoeffRing.eventually_mem
declarations.says: Every x ∈ ℚ̄_ℓ with |x| ≤ 1 lies in O_L for all sufficiently large L.

declarations.name: CoeffRing.norm_le_one
declarations.says: Elements of O_L have absolute value at most 1.

declarations.name: IsLatticeIn
declarations.says: u: G → M_n(O) is an integral form of r: G → GL_n(ℚ̄_ℓ): there is P ∈ GL_n(ℚ̄_ℓ) with u(g) = P⁻¹r(g)P for all g (a G-stable O-lattice).

declarations.name: IsLatticeIn.charpoly_eq_map
declarations.says: If u is an integral form of r, the characteristic polynomial of r(g) is that of u(g), viewed over ℚ̄_ℓ (so it has coefficients in O).

declarations.name: eventually_exists_isLatticeIn
declarations.says: A continuous representation r of a compact group G on ℚ̄_ℓ^n is conjugate to one with entries in O_L, for every sufficiently large finite Galois extension L of ℚ_ℓ (existence of a stable lattice).
declarations.reference: J.-P. Serre, Abelian ℓ-adic representations and elliptic curves (1968), ch. I
declarations.note: Folklore: Baire's theorem puts r(G) in GL_n of a finite extension, and a compact subgroup stabilises a lattice; the Lean proof uses Auerbach's lemma (CommonEigenvectors) and Baire category.

declarations.name: length_le_of_card_dvd_or_le
declarations.says: For modules X, Y over a complete DVR R with finite residue field (an ℓ-adic integer ring): if #X divides #Y, or #X ≤ #Y with X finite, then length_R X ≤ length_R Y (#X = q^{length X}).

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of topology, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: HasIntegralConductor
declarations.says: The additive character ψ of a semilocal field F has conductor O: ψ is continuous and ψ(tO) = 1 exactly when t ∈ O.

declarations.name: SemilocalField
declarations.says: Axioms met by a finite product of non-archimedean local fields: a locally compact Polish ring with Haar measure, a compact open subring O of volume 1 with Smith normal form (valuation pair), and a topologically nilpotent unit ϖ ∈ O.

declarations.name: TameLocalChar
declarations.says: Tameness datum for a multiplicative character χ of F: a finite ring R, a surjection π: O → R with kernel ϖO, and a primitive character η of R with η∘π = χ⁻¹ on units of O (0 on non-units).

declarations.name: integral_mem_of_isLocallyConstant
declarations.says: If g ↦ f_g is locally constant on a compact space Y with values in a subspace P of functions, then ∫ f_g dμ(g) ∈ P (finite measure μ).

declarations.name: invOnUnits
declarations.says: The function equal to χ⁻¹ on the units of O and 0 elsewhere.

declarations.name: schwartzBruhat
declarations.says: The space of locally constant, compactly supported complex functions on X vanishing outside s (Schwartz–Bruhat functions supported in s).

declarations.name: schwartzBruhat.comp
declarations.says: If φ is Schwartz–Bruhat supported in s, f continuous with a continuous left inverse g mapping s into t, then φ∘f is Schwartz–Bruhat supported in t.

declarations.name: schwartzBruhat.isLocallyConstant_curry
declarations.says: For φ Schwartz–Bruhat and continuous families f(γ, ·) with continuous inverses g(γ, ·), the map γ ↦ (y ↦ φ(f(γ, y))) is locally constant (uniformly in y).

entries.known_result: header: part of Green's characters of GL_n(F_q) and the parabolic-induction ring (see LabelDegree: Green 1955).

declarations.name: IsLabel.scaleRoots
declarations.says: Scaling the roots of a label by a unit a ∈ k^× gives a label of the same degree.

declarations.name: frobenius_conj_pow_injOn
declarations.says: If q = |k| ≡ 1 mod 9, r = 3^{e+1}, ξ a primitive (q^r−1)-th root of unity and l prime, then the q^i-th powers (0 ≤ i < r) of ξ^{l^a} are distinct (ξ^{l^a} has degree r over k).
declarations.note: Elementary number theory (lifting the exponent); tailored to the 3-power degrees used by the proof.

declarations.name: isCentralProj_sum_tupleIdem
declarations.says: Green's orthogonality: for any finite set s of tuples (c_w) of polynomials over the residue fields k_w, Σ_{c∈s} ⊗_w e_{c_w} is a central self-adjoint idempotent of ℂ[∏_w GL_n(k_w)].
declarations.reference: J. A. Green, The characters of the finite general linear groups, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1955)
declarations.relation: special case: Green's characters Ξ_c of squarefree labels are (up to sign) pairwise distinct irreducible characters, stated through their central idempotents

declarations.name: isCentralProj_tupleIdem
declarations.says: Green's irreducibility: for each tuple (c_w), ⊗_w e_{c_w} is a central self-adjoint idempotent of ℂ[∏_w GL_n(k_w)] (equivalently ±Ξ_{c_w} irreducible, or e_{c_w} = 0 when c_w is not a label).
declarations.reference: J. A. Green, The characters of the finite general linear groups, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1955)
declarations.relation: special case: squarefree labels only

declarations.name: labelChar_mul_det
declarations.says: Twisting Green's characters: Ξ_c(g)·χ(det g) = Ξ_{c'}(g) on GL_n(k), where the roots of c' are x_χ times those of c.
declarations.reference: Green 1955
declarations.note: Standard twisting property; follows from the construction of Ξ_c.

declarations.name: reflectionSum_mul_labelIdem
declarations.says: If x_χ is not a root of c and l ≠ 0, then e_c annihilates Σ_h χ(det h)⁻¹·h over the invertible h = 1 + u·lᵀ: the Ξ_c-isotypic part has no vector on which that group acts by χ∘det.

declarations.name: scaleRootsEquiv
declarations.says: For a ∈ k^×, the multiplicative bijection of k[X] scaling the roots of a polynomial by a (inverse: scaling by a⁻¹).

declarations.name: tupleIdem
declarations.says: For a tuple (c_w) of polynomials over the fields k_w, the tensor product ⊗_w e_{c_w} in the group algebra of ∏_w GL_n(k_w).

entries.known_result: Taylor–Wiles freeness at auxiliary primes, up to the orders of the stabilisers

declarations.name: BaseLevel.exists_higman_operator
declarations.says: Taylor–Wiles freeness at auxiliary primes as Higman's criterion up to c: for a finite group Δ embedded in ∏_j GL_n(k_{w_j}), some lattice-preserving operator Ψ on forms of principal level has Σ_{g∈Δ} g⁻¹Ψg = c, c a common multiple of the stabiliser orders.
declarations.reference: Taylor, Wiles, Ann. of Math. 141 (1995); Clozel, Harris, Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations, Publ. IHES 108 (2008); D. G. Higman, Modules with a group of operators, Duke Math. J. 21 (1954) (Higman: suggested by us)
declarations.relation: weaker form: projectivity (freeness) over O[Δ] only up to the integer c, expressed by one Higman operator
declarations.note: REFERENCES.md marks CHT 'compared, place confirmed' for this file together with New/Patching/OnePrimeTie, whose header gives Lemma 3.1.3, §3.4; this file's header gives no place.

declarations.name: BaseLevel.exists_localOps_aeval_hecke
declarations.says: A polynomial in the Hecke operator of IgI (I the pro-Iwahori) applied after a local operator with values in pro-Iwahori-fixed forms is again a local operator.

declarations.name: BaseLevel.localOps
declarations.says: The lattice-preserving operators on forms of principal level that are restrictions of O-combinations of translations by elements of G_f supported at the auxiliary place w_j and its conjugate.

declarations.name: BaseLevel.localOps.commute_heckeAction
declarations.says: Local operators at the auxiliary places commute with the action of the Hecke algebra away from them.

declarations.name: BaseLevel.mem_baseLevel_iff_residueRep_fixed
declarations.says: A form of principal level at the auxiliary places has the base level exactly when it is fixed by ∏_j GL_n(k_{w_j}).

declarations.name: BaseLevel.residueRep
declarations.says: The action of ∏_j GL_n(k_{w_j}) on forms of principal level at the auxiliary places, by translation through lifts; it preserves the integral forms.

declarations.name: BaseLevel.residueRep_mem_localOps
declarations.says: The action of an element supported at the single place w_j is a local operator at w_j.

declarations.name: BaseLevel.residueRep_mulSingle
declarations.says: On forms, the action of the reduction of k ∈ GL_n(O_{w_j}) equals the local representation of k at w_j.
declarations.note: unfolding

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Fontaine's period rings and the fundamental exact sequence (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.PeriodRings.BdR).

declarations.name: Gp
declarations.says: G_p = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p).

declarations.name: OC
declarations.says: O_C, the ring of integers of C_p.

declarations.name: OC.coe_smul
declarations.says: The action of G_p on O_C is the restriction of its action on C_p.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: OC.dvd_iff_norm_le
declarations.says: In O_C, x divides y iff |y| ≤ |x|.

declarations.name: cyclotomicGp
declarations.says: The p-adic cyclotomic character χ: G_p → Z_p^×.

declarations.name: intQpBar
declarations.says: The valuation ring of Q̄_p.

declarations.name: smul_coe_Cp
declarations.says: On Q̄_p ⊂ C_p, the action of g ∈ G_p on C_p restricts to g.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: valuation_intQpBar_le_iff
declarations.says: For x, y ∈ Q̄_p, v(x) ≤ v(y) for the valuation of the valuation ring iff |x| ≤ |y|.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Ax–Sen–Tate theorem and Tate's vanishing of the invariants of C_p(i) (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.TateSen.NearOne).

declarations.name: BdR.exists_sub_mem_of_smul_sub_mem
declarations.says: Tate: invariants of B_dR modulo a B_dR^+-submodule S come from K: if j(g)x − x ∈ S for all g (j of open image, K its fixed field), then x − a ∈ S for some a ∈ K.
declarations.reference: J. Tate, p-divisible groups, Proc. Conf. Local Fields (1967), §3; O. Brinon, B. Conrad, CMI notes (2009), §14
declarations.relation: the theorem in its H^0 form: (B_dR/S)^{G_K} is the image of K, deduced from C_p^{G_K} = K and C_p(i)^{G_K} = 0 for i ≠ 0
declarations.note: header of TateSen/NearOne cites Tate §3, Fontaine–Ouyang 3.3–3.5, Brinon–Conrad §14 (unchecked list, gives places); Tate's theorem is proved there for H^0 only

declarations.name: algebraMap_mem_hodgeFil_one_iff
declarations.says: y ∈ B_dR^+ lies in Fil^1 = tB_dR^+ iff θ(y) = 0.

declarations.name: algebraMap_mem_hodgeFil_zero
declarations.says: B_dR^+ ⊂ Fil^0 B_dR.

declarations.name: hodgeFil
declarations.says: The filtration of B_dR: Fil^n = t^n B_dR^+ for n ∈ ℤ.

declarations.name: hodgeFil_anti
declarations.says: The filtration is decreasing: Fil^(n+1) ⊂ Fil^n.

declarations.name: mem_hodgeFil
declarations.says: x ∈ Fil^n iff x = y t^n with y ∈ B_dR^+.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: mul_mem_hodgeFil
declarations.says: Fil^m · Fil^n ⊂ Fil^(m+n).

declarations.name: tUnit
declarations.says: Fontaine's period t, as a unit of B_dR.
declarations.note: t is built without logarithms (header of PeriodRings/BdR)

entries.known_result: Part of: theta kernels of unitary dual pairs: functoriality, seesaw, growth, rapid decay (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/KernelDecay)

declarations.name: Space.height_sum_le
declarations.says: For the orthogonal sum S ⊕ T, ht(diag(g, h)) ≤ ht(g)·ht(h).

declarations.name: isPrimitiveMatrix_of_liftFn_ne_zero
declarations.says: If Ψ(y) ≠ 0 forces the matrix of entries of y (arranged by e) to be left invertible mod 𝔪, then wherever the adelic lift of Ψ is nonzero that matrix is primitive over O_w at every w | 𝔪.

declarations.name: isProperMap_inl
declarations.says: The block inclusion U(n) → U(n + m), g ↦ diag(g, 1), is a proper map.

declarations.name: modDatum_eq_sum
declarations.says: The modular datum of Ψ is Σ_x Ψ(x)·(modular datum of the indicator of x), x over residue matrices mod 𝔪.
declarations.note: Linearity.

declarations.name: modulusResidue
declarations.says: For a place w dividing the modulus 𝔪, the reduction map O_E/𝔪 → residue field at w.

declarations.name: modulusResidue_reduction
declarations.says: Reducing mod 𝔪 and then to the residue field at w is reduction at w.
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: norm_fromBlocks
declarations.says: The (sup) norm of a block-diagonal matrix diag(x, b) is max(‖x‖, ‖b‖).

declarations.name: pairTheta_modDatum_decay
declarations.says: Rapid decay for modular data: if 𝔪 ≠ (1) and Ψ is supported on matrices left invertible mod 𝔪, the kernel θ of v⊗Ψ satisfies, for each M, |θ(g,h)|·ht(g)^M ≤ C·mom_N(v)·ht(h)^B (some B, N, C) for all g, h and v with finite N-th moment.
declarations.note: From the decay estimate exists_norm_name_le (KernelDecay).

entries.known_result: header: part of the standard basis theorem for Schur modules (see MinorBasis).

declarations.name: diagramWeight_add
declarations.says: The weight λ attached to column multiplicities is additive: λ(κ+κ') = λ(κ)+λ(κ').

declarations.name: diagramWeight_apply
declarations.says: λ(τ,i) = Σ_{i<h<N_τ} κ_τ(h).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: fockPairing_rowSubst
declarations.says: For the Fock form ⟨P,Q⟩ = P(∂)Q(0), substitution by matrices z_τ and by their transposes are adjoint: ⟨p(zy),q⟩ = ⟨p,q(zᵀy)⟩.

declarations.name: fockPairing_star_self_pos
declarations.says: Over a star-ordered domain of characteristic 0, ⟨p̄,p⟩_Fock > 0 for every nonzero polynomial p (positivity of the Fischer inner product).

declarations.name: map_fockPairing
declarations.says: The Fock pairing commutes with ring homomorphisms.

declarations.name: map_jet
declarations.says: The jet (differential operator application) commutes with ring homomorphisms.

declarations.name: map_nablaBasis
declarations.says: The basis minor products are defined over ℤ: their images under a ring homomorphism are the basis minor products over the target.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of commutative algebra (textbook or folklore): absolutely integrally closed rings, normed fields over Q_p, adic separation

declarations.name: IsAIC.exists_pow_eq
declarations.says: In an absolutely integrally closed commutative ring A (every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root) every a in A has an n-th root, n >= 1 (root of X^n - a).

declarations.name: Nat.Coprime.norm_natCast_eq_one
declarations.says: If F is a normed field that is a normed Q_p-algebra and p does not divide n, then |n|_F = 1.

declarations.name: PadicIso
declarations.says: For a prime l, a chosen ring isomorphism iota_l : C -> Qbar_l (algebraic closure of Q_l), carried as a class.
declarations.note: Existence of such an isomorphism needs the axiom of choice (both fields algebraically closed, char 0, of continuum cardinality); the class only records a choice.

declarations.name: PadicPlace
declarations.says: A p-adic place of C: a chosen ring homomorphism iota_p : C -> C_p, carried as a class.

declarations.name: ThePrime
declarations.says: The statement that p is prime, as a class fixing the prime p in scope (a variant of Fact p.Prime).

declarations.name: norm_p_eq_inv
declarations.says: In a normed field F that is a normed Q_p-algebra, |p|_F = 1/p.

declarations.name: norm_p_lt_one
declarations.says: In a normed field F that is a normed Q_p-algebra, |p|_F < 1.

entries.known_result: header: a step of the proof of sharpness of Katz's divisibility for invariant derivatives on a CM formal group: coefficients of substituted p-adic series, bounds by products, lowest terms

declarations.name: HasLargeSplit.mono
declarations.says: If the exponent D is a sum of k exponents alpha_b with r <= prod_b N(alpha_b), the same holds for every r' <= r.
declarations.note: HasLargeSplit N k D r (defined in Lib/General/LinearAlgebra/PartialDerivComm): D = sum of k exponents alpha_b with r <= prod N(alpha_b).

declarations.name: HasLargeSplit.mul
declarations.says: Splits concatenate: if D splits into k parts with product >= r and D' into k' parts with product >= r' >= 0, then D + D' splits into k + k' parts with product >= r r'.

declarations.name: IsCarriedBy
declarations.says: For a power series H over C_p and a weight N on exponents: 'k copies carry H' if every exponent alpha is a sum of k exponents alpha_b with |coeff_alpha H| <= prod_b N(alpha_b).
declarations.note: Ad hoc bookkeeping notion made for the Katz-divisibility step; no literature name.

declarations.name: IsCarriedBy.mul
declarations.says: If k copies carry H and k' copies carry H', then k + k' copies carry H H' (ultrametric inequality on the coefficients of a product).

declarations.name: IsLowestTerm
declarations.says: The power series f has lowest term c z^m for the weight w: f agrees with the monomial c z^m at every exponent d of w-weight <= the w-weight of m.

declarations.name: IsLowestTerm.mul
declarations.says: If f has lowest term c z^D and g has lowest term d z^D' (same weight w), then f g has lowest term c d z^(D+D').

declarations.name: exists_monomial_max_norm_coeff
declarations.says: For finitely many series f_i over C_p without constant term, a series s and an exponent alpha, some exponent e with |e| <= |alpha| satisfies |coeff_alpha(g(f) s)| <= |coeff_alpha(f^e s)| for every series g with integral coefficients.
declarations.note: Truncate at total degree |alpha| and apply the ultrametric inequality to the finitely many monomials.

entries.known_result: header: projective embeddings by linear systems (properness, closed immersions, Segre, affine charts); tensor powers, Segre and Veronese embeddings (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: LineBundle.IsLinearSystem.pi
declarations.says: The tensor product of finitely many linear systems is a linear system (iterated Segre product).

declarations.name: LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.comp
declarations.says: If the linear system L embeds X projectively over S along s and p: Y -> X is a closed immersion, then p*L embeds Y projectively over S along s o p.
declarations.note: IsProjEmbedding: L a linear system, s proper, and points with the same image in S and the same homogeneous coordinates are equal (equivalent to a closed immersion into P^iota_S pulling back O(1), exists_isClosedImmersion).

declarations.name: LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.ext
declarations.says: If L embeds X projectively over S, two morphisms a, b: Y -> X with a*L = b*L (same transition data) and a o s = b o s are equal.

declarations.name: LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.mul
declarations.says: Segre embedding of a tower: if L embeds X over S along s and N embeds S over S' along b, then L (x) s*N embeds X over S' along b o s.
declarations.reference: Segre embedding; e.g. R. Hartshorne, Algebraic Geometry, ch. II

declarations.name: LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.pow
declarations.says: If L embeds X projectively over S, so does its m-th tensor power for m != 0 (Veronese).

declarations.name: LineBundle.pi
declarations.says: The tensor product of the line bundles N_a over a in s (default: all a), on the common refinement of the covers; for linear systems the Segre product.

declarations.name: LineBundle.pow
declarations.says: The m-th tensor power of L, indexed by m-tuples of indices; for a linear system the Veronese system of all monomials of degree m.

entries.known_result: Witt's extension theorem for hermitian forms, unimodular lattices, and the Iwasawa decomposition (First 2015, Cor. 4.9, 4.11) - New uses only this file's adelic Iwasawa decomposition and Fourier coefficients along the centre of a unipotent radical

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.centreCoeff
declarations.says: The Fourier coefficient at the p x p matrix T of a function D on U(W)(A) at g, along the centre of the unipotent radical of the parabolic of an isotropic frame: the mean over adelic M modulo rational matrices of psi(tr T M) D(z(M) g).

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.centreCoeff_rat_mul
declarations.says: For automorphic D and a rational point gamma acting on the isotropic frame by c: the T-coefficient of D at gamma g equals the c^H T c-coefficient at g.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.centreCoeff_sub
declarations.says: For automorphic D, D': F(g) = D(gY) - c D'(g) is automorphic, and along every splitting its T-coefficient at g is that of D at gY minus c times that of D' at g.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.isContPeriodic_radicalCentre
declarations.says: For automorphic D, the function M -> D(z(M) g) on adelic p x p matrices is continuous and periodic modulo the rational matrices.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.iwasawa
declarations.says: Iwasawa decomposition: for g in U(W)(A) there are kappa in the maximal compact K_infinity K_0 and b in GL_p(A), block upper triangular for a given ordering, such that g kappa acts on the isotropic frame k by b and g kappa = (element of the unipotent radical) times (Levi element of (b, u)) for some u.
declarations.reference: Iwasawa decomposition G(A) = P(A) K; e.g. C. Moeglin, J.-L. Waldspurger, Spectral decomposition and Eisenstein series (1995), ch. I
declarations.relation: special case: adelic unitary groups of the proof's hermitian spaces (self-dual lattices, CM field with WeilData), the parabolic of an isotropic frame, with the GL_p Levi part additionally made block upper triangular
declarations.note: Header's citation (First 2015, Cor. 4.9, 4.11; compared, place confirmed) is for Witt's extension theorem, which is used in the proof but is not itself among the declarations New uses.

declarations.name: adaptedHomBasis
declarations.says: The invertible adelic matrix (x^-1)^H (x) 1_p: Kronecker product of the adjoint of the inverse adelic frame x of T with the p x p identity.

declarations.name: isAdapted_homSource
declarations.says: If the splitting A of W' over W is base-adapted, the induced splitting of the Hom space Hom(T, -) is adapted with respect to the Kronecker frame adaptedHomBasis.
declarations.note: Bookkeeping of frames: adapted splittings pass to Hom spaces.

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: Heisenberg.OrthogonalSum.heisOp_tmul
declarations.says: For an orthogonal sum W ≅ W₁ × W₂, the Heisenberg operator of x acts on v⊗w componentwise: ρ(x)(v⊗w) = ρ(x₁)v ⊗ ρ(x₂)w.

declarations.name: Heisenberg.OrthogonalSum.integral_eq_integral_prod
declarations.says: For an orthogonal sum W ≅ W₁ × W₂ (vacuum-normalised Haar measures), ∫_W f dμ = ∫_{W₁×W₂} f(φ(x)) d(μ₁×μ₂).

declarations.name: Heisenberg.OrthogonalSum.measurePreserving_equiv
declarations.says: The isomorphism W₁ × W₂ ≅ W of an orthogonal sum carries μ₁×μ₂ to μ, the Haar measures being normalised by ∫|e|² = 1.
declarations.note: Uniqueness of Haar measure.

declarations.name: Heisenberg.OrthogonalSum.tmul
declarations.says: Tensor product of reproducing spaces for an orthogonal sum: (v₁, v₂) ↦ ∫ v₁(x) ρ(φ(x,0)) (∫ v₂(y) ρ(φ(0,y))vac dy) dx, a bounded bilinear map.

declarations.name: Heisenberg.OrthogonalSum.tmul_vacElem
declarations.says: vac₁ ⊗ vac₂ = vac.

declarations.name: Heisenberg.Rep.left
declarations.says: The restriction of a Heisenberg representation R of W ≅ W₁×W₂ to the first summand: x ↦ R(φ(x,0)).

declarations.name: Heisenberg.Rep.right
declarations.says: The restriction of a Heisenberg representation R of W ≅ W₁×W₂ to the second summand: x ↦ R(φ(0,x)).

entries.known_result: Part of: commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n and the Eichler commutation relation (known result stated in Lib/General/LinearAlgebra/ColumnLattices); this file: the Eichler commutation relation of Hecke polynomials through theta lifts at split places

declarations.name: FinPlace.q_eq_sqrt_sq
declarations.says: q_w = (√q_w)² in ℂ.

declarations.name: heckePolyOp_eq_sum
declarations.says: On a vector spherical at the split place w, the Hecke polynomial operator at X is Σ_U c_X(U)·π(coset representative attached to the subspace U), and similarly at w̄ with inverse representatives.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: hecke_transfer_of_equivariant
declarations.says: Eichler commutation relation (Hecke transfer through the theta correspondence): w split, ranks n of S and n+k of T, a, b unramified, f the vacuum at w, Λ linear with Λ(ω(g,h)f) = π(g)ρ(h)Λf; then Λf is K_w-fixed for π and ρ and P^ρ_w(X)Λf = ∏_{l<k}(1 − q^{l+n/2}χ_S(w)X)·P^π_{w̄}(q^{k/2}χ_Sχ_T⁻¹(w)X)Λf.
declarations.reference: S. Rallis, Langlands' functoriality and the Weil representation, Amer. J. Math. 104 (1982); R. Howe, θ-series and invariant theory, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 33 (Corvallis 1979); T. Tamagawa, Ann. of Math. 77 (1963)
declarations.relation: special case: split places of unitary groups (GL_n at w), unramified characters, the unramified vacuum; an identity of Hecke polynomials obtained by summing over subspaces of the residue space, without the Satake transform
declarations.note: Known result named in the header of Lib/General/LinearAlgebra/ColumnLattices; REFERENCES.md: Howe and Tamagawa 'work found, no place given' for that file; Rallis 1982 not listed for these files.

declarations.name: isSphericalWith_formLift
declarations.says: If f is an arrow e → e′ (w split, ranks n and n+k, a, b unramified, f the vacuum at w) and y is spherical at w with Hecke polynomial p, then its theta lift is spherical with polynomial ∏_{l<k}(1 − q^{l+n/2}χ_S(w)X)·p(q^{k/2}χ_Sχ_T⁻¹(w)X).
declarations.note: Direct application of the Eichler relation (hecke_transfer_of_equivariant, via hecke_transfer_of_pairing) to the theta lift.

declarations.name: isSphericalWith_trivialHecke
declarations.says: At a split place w of norm q, a vector fixed by the whole finite adelic unitary group of rank n is spherical with Hecke polynomial ∏_{l<n}(1 − q^l X).
declarations.note: Count of subspaces of the residue space (q-binomial coefficients).

declarations.name: maximum_principle
declarations.says: If v is a real function bounded above, Σ|a_i| < l, and l·v(g) ≤ Σ|a_i|·v(r(g,i)) for all g, then v ≤ 0 everywhere.

declarations.name: sum_heckePolyCoeff_smul_pairWeil
declarations.says: At a split place w with f the vacuum at w and a, b unramified: the Hecke sum at X over U(T) (resp. U(S)) applied to f equals f named at w by x ↦ trivialHecke(d − rank(x mod w), νX) on integral x, with (d, ν) = (m, frobValue of a) resp. (n, frobValue of b).
declarations.note: The core local computation of the Eichler relation: action of the Hecke coset sums on the unramified Schrödinger vacuum, by counting subspaces; the write-up must present it (classical in substance, cf. Rallis 1982).

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Potentially crystalline representations, Hodge–Tate weights, Weil–Deligne Frobenius (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.Crystalline.RegularityFrobenius).

declarations.name: Lift.InClass.dual
declarations.says: If a Galois lattice Y lies in the class (F, K, U), its twisted dual Y^∨(1) lies in the class with K(s⁻¹, ·) and jumps U(g) replaced by {−u − 1}.
declarations.note: from IsAdmissible.of_pairing and Lift.jump_tateDual

declarations.name: Lift.InClass.of_cyclotomic_pow
declarations.says: A lattice on which Γ acts through χ^c lies in the class with no killing condition and the single jump −c.

declarations.name: Lift.InClass.of_jointly_injective
declarations.says: If F is coarser than 'near 1' and a lattice Y has jointly injective equivariant O-linear maps to finitely many lattices of the class (F, K, U), then Y belongs to that class.
declarations.note: from IsAdmissible.of_jointly_injective and exists_jump_of_jointly_injective

declarations.name: Lift.InClass.tensor
declarations.says: If Y, L are admissible along F with jumps in U, U' at each embedding, so is Y ⊗ L, with jumps in U + U' (no killing condition retained).

declarations.name: Lift.exists_isKilledBy_tateDual_tensor
declarations.says: If j(s) is in inertia, Y and L are potentially crystalline and monic q, r ∈ Z_p[X] kill (s, 0) on Y and L, then some monic e ∈ Z_p[X] of degree ≤ deg q·deg r kills (s⁻¹, 0) on Hom(Y ⊗ L, O(1)).
declarations.note: e is the polynomial whose roots are the products of roots of q and r (inverted)

declarations.name: Lift.jump_tateDual
declarations.says: For L potentially crystalline, the multiplicity of the jump u of L^∨(1) at γ equals that of the jump −u − 1 of L.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Fontaine's period rings and the fundamental exact sequence (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.PeriodRings.BdR).

declarations.name: Ainf.mem_radical_of_not_isUnit
declarations.says: If a ∈ A_inf is not a unit and p does not divide δ, then a lies in the radical of the ideal (p, δ).
declarations.note: O^♭ = A_inf/p is a rank-one valuation ring

declarations.name: associated_smul_of_dvd
declarations.says: If a ∈ A_inf divides g·a for every g ∈ G_p, then g·a and a are associates.

declarations.name: isUnit_WittCFlat_of_not_p_dvd
declarations.says: If p does not divide a ∈ A_inf, then a is a unit in W(C^♭).

declarations.name: not_p_dvd_tau
declarations.says: p does not divide τ in A_inf (θ(τ) = ζ_p − 1 has absolute value > |p|).

declarations.name: theta_smul
declarations.says: θ is G_p-equivariant: θ(g a) = g θ(a).

declarations.name: theta_surjective
declarations.says: θ: A_inf → O_C is surjective.
declarations.reference: J.-M. Fontaine, Le corps des périodes p-adiques, Astérisque 223 (1994)

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Kisin lattice (Breuil–Kisin module) of a crystalline lattice (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.WachKisin.PeriodMatrixFrame).

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.theta_z_dvd_p
declarations.says: For a chart, θ(z) divides p in O_C.

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.z_dvd_of_dvd_E_pow_mul
declarations.says: For a chart and a ∈ A_inf: if z divides E^k a in B^+, then z divides a in A_inf.

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.z_dvd_sub
declarations.says: If g ∈ G_p fixes Λ = W(F_{p^f}) pointwise and y lies in the bicommutant S_B ⊂ B^+, then z divides g y − y in B^+.
declarations.note: Galois action trivial modulo the variable, for the authors' ring S_B; for y ∈ S it is (g − 1)z ∈ zA_inf

declarations.name: Lift.frobE_dvd_iff
declarations.says: φ^n(E) divides a ∈ A_inf iff θ(φ^(−n)(a)) = 0.
declarations.note: ker θ = (ξ) = (E)

declarations.name: Lift.thetaPhiInv
declarations.says: The ring homomorphism θ ∘ φ^(−n): A_inf → O_C.

declarations.name: Lift.thetaPhiInv_smul
declarations.says: θ ∘ φ^(−n) is G_p-equivariant.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of measure and integration (textbook or folklore): ideal zeta sums, codifferent groups, summation over ideals

declarations.name: idealZeta
declarations.says: The ideal zeta sum zeta_R(s) = sum over ideals I of finite index in R of [R : I]^{-s}, for natural s, in [0, infinity]; for R = O-hat_E it is the Dedekind zeta function of E.

declarations.name: idealZeta_intAdeles_pow_le
declarations.says: For a CM field E: if n [E:Q] <= 2^v, then zeta_E(u + v + 4)^n <= 1 + 2^{-u} (zeta_E the ideal zeta sum of O-hat_E).
declarations.note: From zeta_E(s) <= zeta(s)^{[E:Q]} and zeta(s) <= 1 + 2^{2-s}.

declarations.name: isCompact_codifferent
declarations.says: For a CM field E and an invertible finite adele M, the group of conjugation-invariant finite adeles z with psi_f(M z x) = 1 for all x in O-hat is compact.

declarations.name: isOpen_codifferent
declarations.says: For a CM field E and a finite adele M, the group of conjugation-invariant finite adeles z with psi_f(M z x) = 1 for all x in O-hat is open.

declarations.name: le_two_of_pow_le_ofReal
declarations.says: In [0, infinity]: if x^{mu+1} <= 1 + 2^{-e}, then x <= 2.

declarations.name: lintegral_le_idealZeta_mul
declarations.says: Summation over ideals: if zeta_R(mu) <= 2 and almost every x in s lies in a set S(I), I of finite index, with [R:I]^mu f(x) rho(S(I)) <= V, then the integral of f over s is <= zeta_R(mu) V.

entries.known_result: Singular forms are governed by their coefficients at unimodular indices (after Freitag, LNM 1487 (1991); J.-S. Li, Amer. J. Math. 119 (1997)); adelic, unitary, non-holomorphic, singularity from one split place; only the vanishing half

declarations.name: closureIntegers
declarations.says: The ring of adeles of E that are integral at the places of S cup S-bar.

declarations.name: exists_isBaseAdapted_reindex
declarations.says: Reindexing a base-adapted one-plane splitting D of V' over V along a bijection Unit = p gives a base-adapted splitting with the frame k reindexed and the same embedding i.

declarations.name: exists_isBaseAdapted_stage
declarations.says: A base-adapted splitting D of V' over V factors in two stages: for a bijection e: n_1 + q -> p, some base-adapted splitting of V' over V plus q planes, followed by removing these q planes, has the frame of D (reindexed) and its embedding.

declarations.name: freitag
declarations.says: Let f be automorphic on U(W), fixed by integral points on S, radical-invariant along an extra line, det T != 0. If the T-coefficient of f vanishes at all points acting on the frame by gamma on S with delta^-1 gamma^H T gamma unimodular (primitive over the integers at S cup S-bar), it vanishes at all points supported on S cup S-bar.
declarations.reference: E. Freitag, Singular Modular Forms and Theta Relations, LNM 1487 (1991); J.-S. Li, Automorphic forms with degenerate Fourier coefficients, Amer. J. Math. 119 (1997)
declarations.note: Header: 'Known result: singular forms are governed by their coefficients at unimodular indices'; only the vanishing half, in an adelic unitary non-holomorphic setting, proved by induction on the index of a lattice in its dual. Not a literal theorem of the cited works: the write-up must read it.

declarations.name: invDifferentIdele
declarations.says: The idele delta = j kappa kappa-bar, kappa the scaling idele of the WeilData; its finite part is j alpha alpha-bar.

declarations.name: siegelBracket
declarations.says: Siegel's T[gamma] = gamma^H T gamma for a rational matrix T and an adelic matrix gamma, divided by the idele delta = j kappa kappa-bar.

entries.known_result: Tower property for the constant term of a theta lift along an isotropic line, for a lifted character and ramified data (model: Rallis, Compositio 51 (1984) Thm I.1.1; Wu, JNT 133 (2013) Prop. 3.1)

declarations.name: exists_constant_term_thetaLarge
declarations.says: Removing a plane on the large side: for standard data, the constant term along A of the theta integral of a split tame character for (W', V') is gamma times the theta integral for (W, V) with a cone integral as real datum, where |gamma|^2 Pi(e) = C Pi(e+1), e = rk V - rk W/2, C independent of the character.
declarations.reference: S. Rallis, On the Howe duality conjecture, Compositio Math. 51 (1984); C. Wu, Irreducibility of theta lifting for unitary groups, J. Number Theory 133 (2013)
declarations.note: Analogue of Rallis's tower property (header: Thm I.1.1; Wu Prop. 3.1; not part of the authors' check): the literature lifts cusp forms, here a character with ramified data, and the isotropic orbit leaves a Tate integral whose size is a ratio of partial Hecke L-values. The write-up must read it.

declarations.name: lValueProd
declarations.says: For a finite set S of places, a Hecke character nu and a natural number e: (prod_{w in S} Nw)^{e^2} prod_{z=1}^{e} |L^S(z, nu)|^2.

declarations.name: lValueProdInt
declarations.says: For an integer e, Pi(e): lValueProd at e for the character and places of the split tame character if e >= 0, its inverse at -e if e < 0.

declarations.name: lValueProdInt_pos
declarations.note: Uses that the partial Hecke L-values L^S(z, nu), z >= 1, are nonzero for a character of positive weight (HasWeight.L_ne_zero, Lib/ClassField).

declarations.name: pairWeil_stdRowDatum_eq_self
declarations.says: A datum with real part v, the standard row function at the places of the split tame character and the vacuum elsewhere is fixed by the integral finite points k of U(V), when the character on U(V) is nu^-1 upsilon^{floor(rk W/2)}.

declarations.name: rankTwist_eq_mul_of_splitting
declarations.says: For a splitting of W' over W with |b| hyperbolic planes: rankTwist(nu, rk W') = rankTwist(nu, rk W) upsilon^{|b|} (bookkeeping of characters).

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: stdLattice
declarations.says: The standard lattice Ô^ι (Ô the profinite completion of O_E) as an additive subgroup of finite adelic vectors.

declarations.name: stdLattice.finVac
declarations.says: The finite vacuum: x ↦ ψ_f(½c₀ȷαᾱ·x*x) for x ∈ Ô^ι, and 0 otherwise.

declarations.name: stdLattice.half
declarations.says: The number ½ as a finite adele of E.

declarations.name: stdLattice.psi₀
declarations.says: The additive character u ↦ ψ_f(ȷαᾱu) of the finite adeles of E (ψ_f the standard finite character, ȷ, α from the Weil data).

declarations.name: stdLattice.psi₀_apply
declarations.says: psi₀(z) = ψ_f(ȷαᾱz).
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: stdLattice.semichar
declarations.says: The semicharacter sc(x) = ψ_f(½c₀ȷαᾱ·x*x) of finite adelic vectors x (a quadratic function whose polarisation is the Heisenberg bicharacter).

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: Space.finHeisOp_mem_finitePart
declarations.says: The finite part 𝒲_f is stable under the finite Heisenberg operators.

declarations.name: Space.finitePart
declarations.says: The finite part 𝒲_f ⊂ 𝒮(V): the span of the translates of the vacuum under the finite Heisenberg operators (the Gaussian at ∞ tensored with Schwartz–Bruhat functions at the finite places).

declarations.name: Space.isLocallyConstant_rho_finVec
declarations.says: For f ∈ 𝒲_f the map x ↦ ϱ(αx)f on finite adelic vectors is locally constant.

declarations.name: Space.omega_mem_finitePart
declarations.says: The finite adelic unitary group preserves 𝒲_f: f ∈ 𝒲_f implies ω(1,g)f ∈ 𝒲_f for every finite point g.

declarations.name: Space.rho_finVec_mem_finitePart
declarations.says: 𝒲_f is stable under the operators ϱ(αx), x a finite adelic vector.

declarations.name: Space.vacElem_mem_finitePart
declarations.says: The vacuum lies in 𝒲_f.

entries.known_result: Functoriality, seesaw, growth and rapid decay for theta kernels of unitary dual pairs (decay for data supported on full-rank maps at split places, by small shifts along a short isotropic vector)

declarations.name: Space.coordMatrix
declarations.says: For a matrix c over E and an adelic point g, the adelic matrix g⁻¹x⁻¹c, x the frame carrying the form of S to the standard form.

declarations.name: Space.coordMatrix_mul_ne_zero
declarations.says: If c ≠ 0 and M becomes left invertible (transposed) after a ring map φ: 𝔸_f → R ≠ 0, then (g⁻¹x⁻¹c)_f* · M · X_f ≠ 0 for every X ∈ GL_p(𝔸).

declarations.name: Space.exists_short_isotropic
declarations.says: If ht(g) > 2, the lattice L_g of S contains a nonzero isotropic vector x (xᴴJx = 0) whose real coordinates at g have norm ≤ 2/ht(g).
declarations.note: A short vector has hermitian norm an integer of absolute value < 1, hence 0.

declarations.name: exists_norm_name_le
declarations.says: Decay estimate: for Ψ Schwartz–Bruhat above P (P ∩ P̄ = ∅), f₀ ∈ 𝒲_f, there is C with |L(v⊗Ψ⊗f₀)|·H^N ≤ C·mom_{N+A}(v)·ρ^{N+2A} for L = ℓ∘ω(g,h), under growth bounds on L and, if H > 2, short lattice vectors (one isotropic) giving invariances or non-vanishing conditions.
declarations.reference: decay of theta kernels: Kudla–Rallis, A regularized Siegel–Weil formula: the first term identity, Ann. Math. 140 (1994) (by Siegel sets)
declarations.note: The authors' method (small shifts along a short isotropic vector instead of Siegel sets); statement long and technical, ~50-line proof.

declarations.name: name_eq_zero_of_invariant
declarations.says: If a bounded functional ℓ is invariant under ϱ(X z Y*ε) for all adelic z and X_f* y Y_f ≠ 0 whenever Ψ(y) ≠ 0, then ℓ(Ψ⊗f) = 0 (Ψ Schwartz–Bruhat above P, P ∩ P̄ = ∅).
declarations.note: Orthogonality of characters on a compact group.

declarations.name: pairTheta_decay_of_onto
declarations.says: Rapid decay: for Ψ Schwartz–Bruhat above P (P ∩ P̄ = ∅) supported on matrices of full rank (after a ring map φ), every N has B, M, C with |θ_{a,b}(v⊗Ψ⊗vac)(g,h)|·ht(h)^N ≤ C·mom_M(v)·ht(g)^B for all g, h and v with mom_M(v) < ∞.
declarations.reference: Kudla–Rallis, A regularized Siegel–Weil formula: the first term identity, Ann. Math. 140 (1994)
declarations.note: Header: known result (rapid decay of theta kernels); the header's HKS 1996 citation (compared, place confirmed: §1) concerns splittings and seesaw, not decay.

entries.known_result: Part of the Bargmann–Fock model of the oscillator representation of U(p,q) (see Lib/Weil/Fock/OscillatorPair); this file: Gaussian vacuum identities and sign-matrix algebra

declarations.name: beta_mul_realVac
declarations.says: β(y,x)·e(x−y) = e(x)·e(y)·exp(⟨ζ(y), ζ(x)⟩) for the Gaussian e(x) = exp(−|x|²/2) and the holomorphic coordinates ζ of signature ε.
declarations.note: Gaussian identity; it exhibits the reproducing kernel exp⟨ζ(y),ζ(x)⟩.

declarations.name: integrable_exp_mul_realVac
declarations.says: For every real C, u ↦ exp(C‖u‖)·exp(−|u|²/2) is integrable on ℂ^ι for the normalized Lebesgue measure (‖u‖ the sup norm).

declarations.name: norm_realMultiplier_le
declarations.says: The multiplier Δ(u) = conj(det d) of u ∈ U(ε) satisfies |Δ(u)| ≤ ‖u‖^|ι|.

declarations.name: posProj_mul_self
declarations.says: The projection P onto the positive coordinates of ε is a hermitian idempotent, and the sign matrix diag(ε) is hermitian.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: principalMinor_sign_eq_det
declarations.says: The principal minor of u on the negative coordinates of ε equals det(P + (1−P)u), P the positive projection.

declarations.name: signMatrix_eq_posProj_sub
declarations.says: diag(ε) = P − (1 − P), P the projection onto the positive coordinates.
declarations.note: unfolding

entries.known_result: the basis problem in the stable range, as a reproducing formula

declarations.name: letterPoly_highestVector_holomorphic
declarations.says: Kashiwara–Vergne (harmonic highest vectors for (U(p,q), U(n)) give holomorphic vectors): if κ has no column longer than the number of signs c, the highest vector of weight κ in the variables of sign c is a nonzero polynomial whose Fock vector is holomorphic of the explicit (staircase) weight.
declarations.reference: M. Kashiwara, M. Vergne, On the Segal–Shale–Weil representations and harmonic polynomials, Invent. Math. 44 (1978) 1–48; M. G. Davidson, Pacific J. Math. 129 (1987)
declarations.relation: weaker form: one direction only (harmonic highest vectors are holomorphic of explicit weight); no decomposition of the oscillator representation
declarations.note: Header of Lib/Weil/Lift/Staircase gives Kashiwara–Vergne III 6.3, 7.2 and Davidson Prop. 2.2, Thm 2.9; not recorded as checked for this file. 'Holomorphic' = matrix coefficients extend holomorphically (holomorphicData).

declarations.name: linSubst_letterMinor
declarations.says: Substituting the complex-linear part of (u⁻¹, 1) into a minor of the variable matrix with rows of one sign multiplies it by the principal minor of u on the coordinates of that sign.
declarations.note: Multiplicativity of determinants.

declarations.name: prod_letterMinor_mem_holomorphicData
declarations.says: For signature (p,q) and a definite second space of rank n′, the product over infinite places of the d-th power of a p×p minor in the positive columns is a nonzero polynomial whose Fock vector is holomorphic of weight −d on positive and n′ on negative indices.
declarations.note: The scalar-weight (det^d) case of the Kashiwara–Vergne statement above; proved from the general joint-highest-vector lemma of Lib/Weil/Lift/Staircase.

declarations.name: realInner_realPairWeil_eq_holMinorsPi
declarations.says: If the polynomial P (in the variables of sign +1) is scaled under u by ∏_w (principal minor of u_w on +)^ν_w·(on −)^c_w, then its matrix coefficient ⟨v_P, ω(u,1)v_P⟩ equals ⟨v_P,v_P⟩·M_v(u)·conj(M_k(u)), with M the explicit products of powers of principal minors (holMinorsPi).
declarations.note: Explicit matrix coefficient of a holomorphic vector in the Fock model (classical in substance: lowest K-type coefficients of holomorphic discrete series), from the coefficient formula between harmonic polynomials (FockHarmonicCoeff) and Jacobi's complementary minor identity.

declarations.name: realPairWeil_mem_span_pairedDetProd
declarations.says: For Y ∈ GL_{n′}(E) and y in the compact U(n′) at the infinite places, ω(1,y) applied to the product of d-th powers of minors lies in the span of products of determinants of submatrices of the rows of Y (pairedDetProd).
declarations.note: Multilinear expansion of determinants under the linear substitution by y.

declarations.name: reproducing_formula_modKernel
declarations.says: Basis problem in the stable range, as a reproducing formula: for 2n < n′, level 𝔪 = (N) ≠ (1), unramified c, b, Q₀ ≠ 0 holomorphic of dominant weight u with integrable coefficient m, ψ ↦ ∫ψ(xh)m(h)dh on rapid level-N forms is a fixed finite linear combination of pairings with theta kernels θ_{c,b}[1_e, Q_i] to the definite U(n′).
declarations.reference: S. Böcherer, Über die Fourier-Jacobi-Entwicklung Siegelscher Eisensteinreihen, Math. Z. 183 (1983); J.-S. Li, J. reine angew. Math. 428 (1992)
declarations.relation: special case: a unitary-group analogue at a fixed principal level N with unramified characters, stated in dual form (pairing with a holomorphic discrete series coefficient factors through finitely many theta lifts to U(n′)); deduced from the injectivity of the lift by linear duality
declarations.note: Both citations: 'work found, no place given' in REFERENCES.md. The injectivity input (isSharp_modDatum, realConv_eq_zero_of_lift_eq_zero) lives in other files; the write-up must state which injectivity theorem is used.

entries.known_result: Joint harmonics and global theta lifts between discrete series types

declarations.name: IsEdge
declarations.says: Φ (a Fock vector) is an edge e → e′ for the action Ω of U(s)_∞ × U(t)_∞: a half edge (e a cusp kernel, ∫⟨Φ, Ω(x,1)Φ⟩ē(x)dx ≠ 0, theta lifts by Φ⊗f of forms of type e with a level are forms of type e′, lifts by polynomial vectors are convolutions of these), and the same for the swapped pair with ē′, ē.
declarations.note: Authors' vocabulary packaging the global lifting property.

declarations.name: ParamsCorrespond
declarations.says: Harish-Chandra-type parameters l (signs s) and l′ (signs t) correspond: at every infinite place w, l′_w and −l_w match for the standard pair of signs t, s and weights γ_w, −γ′_w.

declarations.name: ParamsCorrespond.isEdge_jointHarmonic
declarations.says: Joint harmonics and global theta lifts between discrete series types: for n, n′ ≥ 1 and corresponding parameters l, l′, the Fock vector of the product of chosen joint harmonics is an edge from the type of l to the type of l′ for the real Weil representation of weights γ, γ′.
declarations.reference: J.-S. Li, Theta lifting for unitary representations with nonzero cohomology, Duke Math. J. 61 (1990); R. Howe, Transcending classical invariant theory, JAMS 2 (1989)
declarations.relation: weaker form: only that theta lifts with joint-harmonic real data carry forms of one discrete-series type (integrable projector kernels, parameters with large gaps) to forms of the corresponding type, in both directions; no Howe duality, no nonvanishing
declarations.note: Same content as isEdge_of_isJointHarmonic plus the existence of joint harmonics for corresponding parameters (Lib/DiscreteSeries/Theta). Header also cites Ichino arXiv 2002.09148, Lemma 7.8 (not checked). Li 1990: 'work found, no place given'.

declarations.name: isEdge_of_isJointHarmonic
declarations.says: Joint harmonics and global theta lifts between discrete series types: if each Φ_w is a joint harmonic with parameters l′_w, −l_w, the Fock vector of ∏_w Φ_w is an edge between the discrete-series types of l and l′ (both directions) for the real Weil representation of weights γ, γ′.
declarations.reference: J.-S. Li, Theta lifting for unitary representations with nonzero cohomology, Duke Math. J. 61 (1990); R. Howe, Transcending classical invariant theory, JAMS 2 (1989)
declarations.relation: weaker form: the lift is shown to carry forms fixed by one projector kernel to forms fixed by the other (large gaps), without Howe duality or nonvanishing
declarations.note: The analytic core (via oscillator pairs, unitarity, integrable discrete-series kernels and Fubini) is in isHalfEdge_of_oscillatorPair, same file.

declarations.name: jointHarmonic
declarations.says: The product over infinite places w of chosen joint harmonic polynomials for signs t, s and parameters l′_w, −l_w (arbitrary where none exists), each in the variables of w.

declarations.name: negIf
declarations.says: −l if the Boolean d is true and l otherwise.

entries.known_result: Part of: Schrödinger and mixed models of the Weil representation, action of parabolic subgroups (see Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw); this file: naming a function at a set of finite places (the Schrödinger model at those places)

declarations.name: Space.integrated_name
declarations.says: Inserting a Fock vector at the real places commutes with naming Ψ at S: v⊗(Ψ⊗f) = Ψ⊗(v⊗f).

declarations.name: Space.name
declarations.says: The linear map Ψ ↦ (Ψ⊗·) from functions on finite adelic vectors to operators on S(V): Ψ⊗f = Σ_y c(y)·ϱ(αy₊)P^S f for coefficients c whose Schrödinger-model function at S is Ψ (P^S the vacuum projection above S).
declarations.note: Defined through a chosen generalized inverse of the Schrödinger combination; meaningful for Ψ Schwartz–Bruhat above S (finite combinations of translated box indicators), arbitrary otherwise.

declarations.name: Space.name_boxIndicator
declarations.says: For S disjoint from S̄, naming the indicator of the vectors integral at S gives the projection P^S.

declarations.name: Space.name_schrodingerAct_boxIndicator
declarations.says: Naming the Schrödinger translate by y of the box indicator gives ϱ(α y₊)∘P^S, y₊ the part of y above S ∪ S̄.

declarations.name: Space.projOn_name_vacElem
declarations.says: If T is disjoint from S ∪ S̄, the projection P^T fixes Ψ⊗vac for every Ψ named at S.

declarations.name: Space.smul_name
declarations.says: c·(Ψ⊗f) = (cΨ)⊗f.
declarations.note: linearity

entries.known_result: Part of: commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n and the Eichler commutation relation (known result stated in Lib/General/LinearAlgebra/ColumnLattices); this file: Hecke operators of GL_n at a place, coset representatives

declarations.name: basicCosetRep
declarations.says: For a subspace U of k_w^n (k_w the residue field), a chosen element of the double coset of diag(ϖ1_j, 1), j = dim U, whose reduction mod w has kernel U.

declarations.name: card_sub_rank
declarations.says: For a matrix x over a field with n columns, n − rank x = dim ker x (rank–nullity).

declarations.name: heckeGL_zero
declarations.says: The Hecke operator T_{w,0} (double coset of the identity) acts as the identity on K_w-fixed vectors.

declarations.name: index_stabilizer_line
declarations.says: Over a field with q elements, the subgroup H of GL_n of matrices whose i-th column vanishes off the diagonal (stabilizer of a line) has index 1 + q + ⋯ + q^{n−1}.

declarations.name: residueOrZero
declarations.says: The map E_w → k_w reducing integral elements and sending non-integral ones to 0.

declarations.name: residueOrZero_coe
declarations.says: On integral elements, residueOrZero is the residue map.
declarations.note: unfolding

entries.known_result: header: part of the standard basis theorem for Schur modules (see MinorBasis).

declarations.name: hookNumber_le
declarations.says: If Σ_τ Σ_{h<N_τ} h·κ_τ(h) ≤ L, then the hook number h_κ is at most (L^L)³.
declarations.note: Crude bound, enough for the heights.

declarations.name: hookNumber_pos
declarations.says: The hook number h_κ = ⟨f̄,f⟩_Fock = f̄(∂)f(0) > 0, f the product of leading principal minors to the powers κ_τ(h).

declarations.name: schur_mulVec_weylEval
declarations.says: Under the size condition, ∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}·S_κ(z)·ev_y = ev_{zy}, with y_τ the first |n_τ| columns of block τ and d_τ the determinant exponent.
declarations.note: Defining property of the Schur matrices (substitution of basis polynomials).

declarations.name: schur_mulVec_weylEval_of_detExp_zero
declarations.says: If the determinant exponents vanish, S_κ(z)·ev_y = ev_{zy}.

declarations.name: sum_tableauWeight_le
declarations.says: Dominance for fillings: for a set A of rows at τ, the number of entries of the filling i_τ in A is at most Σ_{j<|A|} λ(τ,j), with equality forcing all entries of columns of height ≤ |A| to lie in A.

entries.known_result: header: generalised index invariant under the involution; lattice index is the index of the determinant (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: IsIntMatrix.adjugate
declarations.says: The adjugate of a matrix with entries in a subring R has entries in R.

declarations.name: IsIntMatrix.det_mem
declarations.says: The determinant of a matrix with entries in a subring R lies in R.

declarations.name: one_le_genIndex
declarations.says: For an adelic pair R in A (R compact open) and u in R a unit of A, the generalised index genIndex(u) = 1/mod_A(u) = [R : uR] is >= 1.
declarations.note: genIndex(a) = inverse of the Haar modulus of a on (A,+), 0 on non-units (Lib/General/Measure/HaarModulus).

declarations.name: submoduleIndex_colLattice_div
declarations.says: For an adelic pair R in A and M in GL_n(A) with column lattice L = M R^n: [R^n : R^n cap L] / [L : R^n cap L] = genIndex(det M), the inverse Haar modulus of det M.
declarations.reference: module of a linear automorphism equals module of its determinant, e.g. A. Weil, Basic Number Theory, ch. I
declarations.note: Haar modulus of M on A^n is mod_A(det M).

declarations.name: submoduleIndex_colLattice_intVectors
declarations.says: If moreover M has entries in R, then [R^n : M R^n] = genIndex(det M).

entries.known_result: header: charts with etale coordinates on functors of points: lifting criterion, shrinking, products, intersections, atlases (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: EtaleChart.comap
declarations.says: Pull-back of an etale chart: for a monomorphism u: Y -> X of functors on k-algebras and a chart of X whose point is u(y), the chart of Y with the same ring and coordinates and the point y.
declarations.note: An etale chart of X (Lib/General/Geometry/OpenSubfunctors): a k-algebra R with d coordinates making k[x_1..x_d] -> R etale and a point y in X(R) embedding Spec R as an open subfunctor.

declarations.name: EtaleChart.prod
declarations.says: Product chart: for charts of X and Y with rings R_a, R_b, the chart of X x Y on R_a (x)_k R_b with coordinates x_i (x) 1 and 1 (x) y_j.

declarations.name: EtaleChart.restrict
