declarations.says: Restriction of a chart along a map phi from its ring to a finite-type k-algebra R': the chart on R' with transported point and coordinates, provided Spec R' embeds as an open subfunctor.

declarations.name: IsChartCovered.comap
declarations.says: If u: Y -> X is a monomorphism with open image (functors on algebras over a noetherian ring k) and the field-valued points of X are covered by charts with d etale coordinates, the same holds for Y.

declarations.name: IsChartCovered.prod
declarations.says: If X is covered by charts with d etale coordinates and Y by charts with n, then X x Y is covered by charts with d + n (product charts).

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of group theory (textbook or folklore): characters with values in Q/Z, Pontryagin duals of finite abelian groups

declarations.name: Continuous.of_isOpen_ker
declarations.says: A homomorphism from a topological group whose kernel is open is continuous (for the given topology on the target monoid).

declarations.name: QZ.bijective_ofZMod_comp
declarations.says: If n kills the abelian group A, composition with Z/n -> Q/Z (k -> k/n) is a bijection Hom(A, Z/n) -> Hom(A, Q/Z).

declarations.name: QZ.eq_zero_of_forall_hom_eq_zero
declarations.says: Q/Z is a cogenerator: if every homomorphism A -> Q/Z kills a, then a = 0.
declarations.note: Divisibility (injectivity) of Q/Z.

declarations.name: QZ.ofZMod
declarations.says: For n != 0, the homomorphism Z/n -> Q/Z sending the class of k to the class of k/n.

declarations.name: card_hom_QZ
declarations.says: A finite abelian group A has exactly |A| homomorphisms to Q/Z (its Pontryagin dual has the same order).

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of group theory (textbook or folklore): characters of finite-dimensional representations

declarations.name: IsChar.apply_inv
declarations.says: For a character chi of a finite group: chi(g^-1) = conj(chi(g)).

declarations.name: IsChar.comp
declarations.says: The composite of a character with a group homomorphism H -> G is a character (inflation/restriction).

declarations.name: IsChar.isIntegral
declarations.says: Values of a character of a finite group are algebraic integers (sums of roots of unity).

declarations.name: IsChar.mul
declarations.says: The product of two characters is a character (tensor product of representations).

declarations.name: IsChar.star
declarations.says: The complex conjugate of a character of a finite group is a character (of the dual representation).

entries.known_result: header: part of invariant integration on a quotient (Weil's formula), unfolding, unimodularity (see Lib.Adelic.QuotientMeasure.Unimodular); this file: quotient measure by a cutoff of mass one on each orbit, character orthogonality

declarations.name: IsCutoff
declarations.says: A cutoff for the action of (H, ν) on X: a measurable β: X → [0, ∞] with ∫_H β(hx) dν(h) = 1 for every x.

declarations.name: Subgroup.FixesLeft
declarations.says: F on G is left-invariant under the subgroup N: F(γg) = F(g) for γ ∈ N.

declarations.name: Subgroup.qms
declarations.says: The measure on G computing integrals over N\G: μ weighted by a chosen cutoff for counting measure on N.

declarations.name: orbitMeasure
declarations.says: The measure βμ on X for a chosen cutoff β of the action of (H, ν); integrating an H-invariant function against it gives the integral over H\X.
declarations.note: β is chosen by choice; if no cutoff exists the measure is meaningless, so statements carry existence hypotheses.

declarations.name: setIntegral_char
declarations.says: Orthogonality of characters: for ν translation-invariant, M an open subgroup and χ multiplicative (χ(x + y) = χ(x)χ(y)), ∫_M χ dν = ν(M) if χ = 1 on M and 0 otherwise (ν(M) read as 0 if infinite).

entries.known_result: header: part of the adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (see Lib.Weil.DualPair.PairSplitting), and of algebraic Hecke characters, extension of the quadratic character of a CM field (see Lib.ClassField.HeckeCharacter.SplittingCharExists); this file: splitting character and Weil data

declarations.name: WeilData
declarations.says: Weil data on a CM field E with a primitive 5040-th root of unity: ȷ ∈ E with ȷ̄ = −ȷ, Im Φ_w(ȷ) > 0 at every infinite place, (1 − ȷ⁻¹)/2 integral; a finite idele α making Ô self-dual for ψ_f(ȷαᾱ·); a splitting character υ with υ = −1 at uniformisers of places w = w̄.
declarations.note: General vocabulary of the Weil representation over a CM field, but bundled with this proof's normalisations ('stably unramified', the inert sign).

declarations.name: WeilData.j_ne_zero
declarations.says: The element ȷ of the Weil data is nonzero.

declarations.name: WeilData.scaleIdele
declarations.says: The idele with component (2π Im Φ_τ(ȷ))^{−1/2} at each infinite place τ and finite part α.

declarations.name: WeilData.traceOne
declarations.says: The element c₀ = (1 − ȷ⁻¹)/2 of E, an algebraic integer with c₀ + c̄₀ = 1.

declarations.name: upsilon_atUnif_mul_star
declarations.says: For a splitting character υ (υ(x̄) = υ(x)⁻¹, trivial on finite unit ideles) and a finite place w: υ(ϖ_w)·υ(ϖ_{w̄}) = 1.

entries.known_result: Derived completeness for a principal ideal, with Nakayama, finiteness and completed base change

declarations.name: Function.Bijective.map_prod
declarations.says: If S-linear maps f: X → Y, g: X → Z give a bijection X → Y × Z and a functor U from S-modules to sets preserves finite products, then x ↦ (U(f)x, U(g)x) is a bijection U(X) → U(Y) × U(Z).
declarations.note: formal category theory

declarations.name: IsDerivedComplete.baseChange
declarations.says: W a DVR with uniformiser π, X a derived π-complete W-module of finite rank, W derived π-complete, S a derived a-complete W-algebra (a the image of π): then S ⊗_W X is derived a-complete.
declarations.reference: Stacks Project (tags 091N, 091P, 0G1U, 09BA, 0CQY); B. Bhatt, Torsion completions are bounded, JPAA (2019)
declarations.note: derived completeness = bijectivity of (x_n) ↦ (x_n − π x_{n+1}) on sequences; the proof shows by hand that X is, up to π^(2m), a retract of a finite free module (bounded torsion)

declarations.name: IsDerivedComplete.congr
declarations.says: Derived π-completeness is invariant under W-linear isomorphism.

declarations.name: IsDerivedComplete.pi
declarations.says: A product of copies of a derived π-complete module (X^ι) is derived π-complete.

declarations.name: algCompletion.of
declarations.says: The natural map B → B^∧_p from a commutative S-algebra to its p-adic completion, as a natural transformation from the identity functor to p-adic completion.

entries.known_result: Characters with finite image on inertia are potentially crystalline of weight 0

declarations.name: AlgHeckeChar.avatar_frob
declarations.says: If w ∤ ℓ and the algebraic Hecke character θ of E is unramified at w, its ℓ-adic avatar (attached Galois character) takes at a geometric Frobenius at A over w the value ι(θ_w(ϖ_w)), ϖ_w the chosen uniformiser.
declarations.reference: J.-P. Serre, Abelian l-adic representations and elliptic curves (1968), ch. II
declarations.note: follows from the construction of the avatar and local–global compatibility of the Artin map (Lib.ClassField)

declarations.name: AlgHeckeChar.eventually_avatar_frob
declarations.says: For Frobenius elements at all but finitely many places w of E, the ℓ-adic avatar of θ at the geometric Frobenius equals ι(θ_w(ϖ_w)).
declarations.note: the 'all but finitely many' version of AlgHeckeChar.avatar_frob

declarations.name: AvatarCompatAt.sphericalClause_of_unramified
declarations.says: If the local compatibility of θ's avatar holds at w and θ is unramified at w, then at every A over w the avatar is unramified (crystalline above ℓ), has the jump −n(ι⁻¹τ) at τ, and X − ιθ_w(ϖ) kills every geometric Frobenius.
declarations.note: repackaging via isGoodAt_iff

declarations.name: JumpsRelAt.congr
declarations.says: The relation between the Hodge–Tate jumps of r at A and a family J of multisets depends only on J(τ) for the embeddings τ inducing the place w under A.

declarations.name: isFiniteTypeAt_char
declarations.says: Characters with finite image on inertia are potentially crystalline of weight 0: a continuous ℓ-adic character μ with finite image on inertia at A is of finite type at A, has the single jump 0, and X − μ(s) kills every s.
declarations.reference: B. Conrad, Lifting global representations with local properties (preprint 2011)
declarations.relation: special case: the potentially unramified case of the theorem on locally algebraic characters, with in addition the action of Weil elements on D_pcris
declarations.note: authors' check: compared, place confirmed (REFERENCES.md); the period solves Lang's equation for GL_1 in A_inf, no Lubin–Tate theory

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Limits of crystalline representations with bounded weights are crystalline (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.Limit.LocalLimit).

declarations.name: crysCocycles.continuous_comp
declarations.says: For j: Γ → G_p an open embedding, T finite free over Z_p and potentially crystalline, x ∈ Z_f(T) and an additive map q from T to a topological group with values killed by p^m, the map q∘x is continuous.
declarations.note: corollary of crysCocycles.eventually_eq_pow_smul

declarations.name: map_cyclotomicGp_smul
declarations.says: For an additive map f from a Z_p-module to Q̄_p^× with p^n-torsion values, f(χ(g)·x) = g(f(x)): G_p acts on p-power roots of unity through the cyclotomic character.

declarations.name: nsmul_zmodPowToUnits
declarations.says: p^m kills the image of Z_p/p^m in Q̄_p^× (written additively).

declarations.name: pPowMultiples
declarations.says: The subgroup p^m T of T.

declarations.name: zmodPowToUnits
declarations.says: A chosen injective homomorphism Z_p/p^m → Q̄_p^× (choice of a primitive p^m-th root of unity), written additively.

entries.known_result: header: General lemmas of commutative and general algebra (textbook or folklore).

declarations.name: Amax.X
declarations.says: The element X = ξ/p of A_max = (A_inf[X]/(pX − ξ))^∧_p, the image of the variable.

declarations.name: Bcris
declarations.says: Colmez's B_max = B^+[1/μ], B^+ = A_max[1/p]; the period ring over which (potentially) crystalline representations are defined here.
declarations.note: named Bcris in Lean but it is B_max, not Fontaine's B_cris; crystalline-ness is the same for either ring

declarations.name: BdRPlus
declarations.says: B_dR^+, defined as the ξ-adic completion of B^+ = A_max[1/p].
declarations.note: standard definition completes A_inf[1/p] along ker θ; same ring

declarations.name: Lift.AdicBasis.eq_zero_of_coord
declarations.says: In an I-adically Hausdorff module with an adic basis, an element all of whose coordinates vanish is zero.

declarations.name: nsmulRange.map_mem
declarations.says: A linear map sends n-multiples (elements of nX) to n-multiples.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Kisin lattice (Breuil–Kisin module) of a crystalline lattice (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.WachKisin.PeriodMatrixFrame).

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.E_ne_zero
declarations.says: E ≠ 0 in A_inf.

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.associated_E_mul_tau_mu
declarations.says: Eτ and μ are associates in A_inf (μ = τξ and E ~ ξ).

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.associated_smul_E
declarations.says: E and g·E are associates for every g ∈ G_p (ker θ = (E) is G_p-stable).

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.exists_tau_mul_E_eq_mul_epsTilt_pow_sub
declarations.says: For n ≠ 0 there are α, β ∈ A_inf with τE(p^(v_p(n)) + βz) = α([ε]^n − 1).
declarations.note: from lifting_the_exponent

declarations.name: Lift.lifting_the_exponent
declarations.says: Lifting the exponent: for f: A_inf → R surjective, v a non-unit dividing x − 1 with p·f(x − 1)·f(v) | f(x − 1)^p, and n ≠ 0, f(x^n − 1) divides p^(v_p(n)) f(x − 1).
declarations.note: a divisibility form of the folklore lifting-the-exponent lemma

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: IsTightFrame
declarations.says: Elements w_i of E with α⁻¹w_i integral which, taken m_i times, form a tight frame of length M for the CM type Φ: Σ_i m_i σ(w_i)·conj(τ(w_i)) = M·δ_{στ} for σ, τ ∈ Φ.
declarations.note: Used for the frames of the construction; a frame-theory notion applied to the CM embedding.

declarations.name: IsTightFrame.repeat_vectors
declarations.says: Repeating each w_i exactly m_i times turns a tight frame with multiplicities m into one with all multiplicities 1 (same length M).

declarations.name: Space.IsJetConjugate
declarations.says: Predicate: applying the automorphism σ of ℂ to the coefficients of the scaled Taylor series T_t f of the theta function gives T_{t′} f′ with the places of the variables renamed by π⁻¹ (Galois conjugation of theta jets).

declarations.name: Space.VacuumExpansion
declarations.says: Expansion data for F: N^{2fn} finite vectors x_j with δx_j integral (f infinite places, rank n) and m ∈ ℕ with Σ_j m·ℓ(ϱ(αx_j)vac)·ϱ(−αx_j)F = N^{2fn}·ℓ(F)·vac for every linear form ℓ.
declarations.note: A finite-Heisenberg averaging that projects onto the vacuum; device of this artifact.

declarations.name: finiteImage
declarations.says: The finite adelic vector α⁻¹γ attached to γ ∈ E^I (α the idele of the Weil data).

entries.known_result: Part of: Schrödinger and mixed models of the Weil representation, action of parabolic subgroups (see Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw); part of Witt's extension theorem for hermitian forms (see Lib/SiegelWeil/SingularForms/AdaptedHom); this file: Witt decomposition, adapted splittings

declarations.name: IsBaseAdapted
declarations.says: A splitting V′ = (lE^p ⊕ kE^p) ⊥ iV is adapted: the adelic frame (l, k, ι) in standard coordinates has orthonormal columns at every infinite place and integral entries at every finite place.

declarations.name: Space.Splitting.comp_kAdelic
declarations.says: For splittings taken in stages, the isotropic frame of the composite splitting is (k, ι·k′) in standard coordinates.
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: Space.exists_splitting
declarations.says: Witt decomposition: every isotropic frame k (E-matrix with a left inverse and k*Jk = 0) of a hermitian space V over E is the frame of a splitting V = (lE^p ⊕ kE^p) ⊥ iV₀ with l*Jk = 1, V₀ a hermitian space with a standard adelic point.
declarations.reference: E. Witt, Theorie der quadratischen Formen in beliebigen Körpern, J. reine angew. Math. 176 (1937); textbook: W. Scharlau, Quadratic and Hermitian Forms (1985)
declarations.relation: the theorem: for hermitian spaces over a CM field, together with an adelic point on the complement V₀ (obtained from Landherr's theorem and Witt's extension theorem, proved elsewhere in Lib)
declarations.note: Proof uses V.landherr (Lib/Adelic/Landherr) and V.witt (Lib/SiegelWeil/SingularForms/AdaptedHom).

declarations.name: Space.ratMap_mul_toAdele
declarations.says: Compatibility of the rational map between spaces with the adelic points: (x⁻¹ i x₀)(x₀⁻¹ k) = x⁻¹(ik).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: removePlanes
declarations.says: The tautological splitting of (p hyperbolic planes) ⊥ V over V.

entries.known_result: header: part of local-global compatibility at tame level (see LabelCompatibility); this file: fundamental tame characters of inertia, existence of exponents, link with local reciprocity.

declarations.name: IsLabel.root_pow_eq_one
declarations.says: A root x of a label c of degree r over k_w (in an extension K) satisfies x^{q_w^{r!}−1} = 1, and x^{q_w^d−1} = 1 for some 1 ≤ d ≤ r.

declarations.name: IsLabelledAt
declarations.says: Whenever s ∈ inertia at A has tame exponent a, the property P holds for s and the polynomial ∏_x (X − ι(T(x)^a)) over the roots x of the label c (with multiplicity).

declarations.name: IsTameExponent.pow_apply_charName
declarations.says: Tame local reciprocity on units: if s has tame exponent a at A over w and s is the local Artin image of a unit u, then T^a(x_χ) = χ(ū) for every character χ of k_w^× (x_χ the element naming χ).
declarations.reference: Local class field theory, tame case (fundamental characters of tame inertia composed with the local Artin map); e.g. J.-P. Serre, Local Fields (reference suggested by us, not by the authors)
declarations.relation: special case: the unit (tamely ramified) part of local reciprocity, in the fundamental-character normalization of the file

declarations.name: exists_isTameExponent
declarations.says: Every s in the inertia group at A over w has a tame exponent a (s(z)/z ≡ ζ^a for z^{Q−1} a uniformiser, Q = q_w^{f!}), coprime to Q−1 for the chosen tame generator, and some s has exponent 1.
declarations.note: Kummer theory of the tame quotient of inertia (standard).

entries.known_result: pseudocharacters, Brauer–Nesbitt, Clifford, and the fact that compact subgroups of GL_n stabilise a lattice

declarations.name: IsTraceNondeg.twist
declarations.says: Semisimplicity (non-degenerate trace form on the span of the image) is preserved by twisting with a character μ.

declarations.name: charpoly_eq_mul_of_trace_pow_add
declarations.says: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, if tr A^m = tr B^m + Σ_{e∈S} α_e^m for all m ≥ 0, then charpoly(A) = charpoly(B)·∏_{e∈S}(X − α_e).
declarations.note: Power sums determine eigenvalues with multiplicity (Newton's identities).

declarations.name: det_aeval_neg_eq_prod_roots
declarations.says: det q(−A) = ∏ q(−x) over the eigenvalues x of A with multiplicity (algebraically closed field).

declarations.name: twistByChar
declarations.says: The twist g ↦ μ(g)R(g) of a matrix representation R by a character μ.

entries.known_result: header: part of pseudocharacters, Brauer–Nesbitt, Clifford; compact subgroups of GL_n stabilise a lattice (see FibreSum: Taylor 1991, Thm 1; Rouquier 1996).

declarations.name: IsTraceNondeg.comp
declarations.says: Clifford's theorem: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, if r: G → GL_n(k) is semisimple (non-degenerate trace form on its span) and f: H → G has normal image, then r∘f is semisimple.
declarations.reference: A. H. Clifford, Representations induced in an invariant subgroup, Ann. of Math. 38 (1937) (reference suggested by us; the header names Clifford without a work)
declarations.relation: the theorem (restriction of a semisimple representation to a normal subgroup is semisimple), with semisimplicity in the trace-form sense, characteristic 0

declarations.name: IsTraceNondeg.exists_conj_of_trace_eq
declarations.says: Brauer–Nesbitt theorem: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, if r is semisimple, ρ: G → B has semiprime span in a finite-dimensional algebra B and φ: B → M_n(k) is an algebra map with tr r = tr φρ, then r(g)P = Pφ(ρ(g)) for some invertible P.
declarations.reference: R. Brauer, C. Nesbitt, On the modular characters of groups, Ann. of Math. 42 (1941); Curtis, Reiner, Representation Theory of Finite Groups and Associative Algebras (1962) (references suggested by us)
declarations.relation: the theorem in its characteristic-0 form (equal traces of semisimple representations imply isomorphism)

declarations.name: IsTraceNondeg.hasSemiprimeSpan
declarations.says: If the trace form is non-degenerate on the span of r(G), any x in that span with x·r(g)·x = 0 for all g is zero (the span is semiprime).

declarations.name: blockDiagonalAlgHom
declarations.says: The algebra homomorphism ∏_i M_{m_i}(R) → M_{Σm_i}(R) sending a family of square matrices to the block-diagonal matrix.

entries.known_result: Density of algebraic vectors, congruences to supercuspidal types, and limits of eigensystems (Emerton–Paškūnas 2020; Fintzen–Shin 2021); non-archimedean Stone–Weierstrass for modules (Dieudonné 1944; Kaplansky 1950; Prolla). New uses only four small lemmas of the file.

declarations.name: Attached.tendsto_charpoly_coeff
declarations.says: If ρ is attached to the Hecke polynomials P_w, then for every x, ι(P_w) converges coefficientwise to det(X − ρ(x)) along the Frobenii (w,A,s) with s tending to j(x).
declarations.note: From the definition of 'attached' and continuity of ρ; the filter of Frobenii near j(x) is non-trivial by Chebotarev density (Lib/ClassField).

declarations.name: Attached.trace_eq
declarations.says: Chebotarev uniqueness: two representations of the same size attached to the same Hecke system have equal traces at x and y whenever j(x) = j'(y).
declarations.note: Uniqueness of limits along the Frobenius filter; uses Chebotarev density through that filter.

declarations.name: norm_coeff_le_of_mul_monic
declarations.says: Over ℚ̄_ℓ, if R is monic and all coefficients of DR have absolute value ≤ η, then so do all coefficients of D (Gauss's lemma for the Gauss norm).

declarations.name: norm_eq_one_of_continuous
declarations.says: A continuous character of a compact group into ℚ̄_ℓ^× takes values of absolute value 1.

entries.known_result: header: morphisms landing in opens, functions on points, line bundles given by covers and transition functions (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: LandsIn.comp
declarations.says: If t: Y -> X lands in the open U, so does a o t for every a: Z -> Y.

declarations.name: LineBundle.inv
declarations.says: The dual line bundle: the same open cover with transition functions g_ji in place of g_ij.

declarations.name: LineBundle.mul
declarations.says: The tensor product L (x) M: the cover by the intersections U_i cap V_a with products of transition functions; for linear systems the Segre product.

declarations.name: LineBundle.one
declarations.says: The trivial line bundle: the single open set X with transition function 1.

entries.known_result: header: part of Shintani descent for GL_n(F_q), with the lift named (see ShintaniLifting: Shintani 1976; Silberger–Zink 2008, Thm 5.1).

declarations.name: Lift.mul
declarations.says: The Shintani lift is multiplicative for parabolic induction: if F lifts to F' and G to G' (a common Z-virtual character of GL_m(k')⋊Gal(k'/k) descends to both, for every m), then F*G lifts to F'*G'.
declarations.note: Compatibility of Shintani descent with parabolic induction; source not given by the authors.

declarations.name: Lift.one
declarations.says: The unit class function lifts to the unit.

declarations.name: Lift.sub
declarations.says: Lifts are compatible with differences: F−G lifts to F'−G'.

declarations.name: labelChar_X_sub_C
declarations.says: Green's class function of the label X − x_χ is χ∘det in dimension 1 and zero in other dimensions.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Bloch–Kato finite local condition: rank formula and size of its annihilator (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.BlochKato.BlochKato).

declarations.name: IsPotCrys.exists_hodge_basis
declarations.says: Hodge position: for T potentially crystalline with Z_p-basis e and jumps k_i over Z_p, there is a Z_p-linear automorphism N of B_dR^n turning the action of Γ on B_dR ⊗ T into the coordinatewise action and carrying (B_dR^+)^n onto ⊕ t^(−k_i) B_dR^+, given by a Galois-invariant matrix W t^k.
declarations.reference: J.-M. Fontaine, Représentations p-adiques semi-stables, Astérisque 223 (1994), Exp. III; O. Brinon, B. Conrad, CMI notes on p-adic Hodge theory (2009)
declarations.note: the relative position of the lattices B_dR^+ ⊗ T and B_dR^+ ⊗ D_dR is given by the Hodge–Tate weights; a de Rham statement proved here for potentially crystalline T

declarations.name: crysCocycles.eventually_eq_pow_smul
declarations.says: Automatic continuity: for T finite free over Z_p and potentially crystalline, every crystalline cocycle c and every m, c(g) ∈ p^m T for all g with j(g) near 1.
declarations.note: cocycles in Z_f(T) are not assumed continuous; proved from the Hodge basis (IsPotCrys.exists_hodge_basis)

declarations.name: extensionRep
declarations.says: For an R-linear map a: C → Z_f(T), the extension of the trivial module C by T: the representation on T × C with g(x, e) = (gx + a(e)(g), e).

declarations.name: jump_extension_le
declarations.says: For T finite over R and a: C → Z_f(T), and u ≠ 0, the multiplicity of the Hodge–Tate jump u (at γ) of the extension of C by T along a is at most that of T.
declarations.note: the quotient C is trivial, hence of weight 0; uses Tate's vanishing C_p(u)^G = 0 for u ≠ 0

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Potentially crystalline representations, Hodge–Tate weights, Weil–Deligne Frobenius (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.Crystalline.RegularityFrobenius).

declarations.name: IsFiniteTypeAt.aeval_eq_zero_of_roots
declarations.says: At a place A not above ℓ, if r has finite image on inertia near 1 and P kills r(s) for an inertia element s, then every polynomial vanishing at all roots of P kills r(s).
declarations.note: r(s) has finite order, hence is semisimple with root-of-unity eigenvalues

declarations.name: IsPotCrys.isCrystalline_of_inertia_fixes
declarations.says: Fontaine's criterion: if T is potentially crystalline and every s with j(s) in inertia acts trivially on D_pcris(T) (β_{s,0} = 1), then T is crystalline.
declarations.reference: J.-M. Fontaine, Représentations l-adiques potentiellement semi-stables, Astérisque 223 (1994), Exp. VIII
declarations.relation: weaker form: only the direction 'inertia acts trivially on D_pcris ⇒ crystalline' (the converse is IsCrystalline.linearFrob_eq_one), with Colmez's B_max as period ring and Γ any group with j of open image
declarations.note: header of RegularityFrobenius cites Fontaine Exp. VIII 2.3 and Brinon–Conrad 9.1–9.3 (not checked); a Galois descent argument

declarations.name: PolyKillsAt.of_dvd
declarations.says: If the polynomial P kills s at A (on r, or on the linear Frobenius above ℓ) and P divides Q, then Q kills s at A.

declarations.name: isGoodAt_iff
declarations.says: At a place A over a finite place, r is good (trivial on inertia if ℓ is a unit at A, crystalline above ℓ) iff it is of finite type and X − 1 kills every inertia element.
declarations.note: uses IsPotCrys.isCrystalline_of_inertia_fixes and IsCrystalline.linearFrob_eq_one

entries.known_result: Fontaine's period rings and the fundamental exact sequence

declarations.name: BdR
declarations.says: The de Rham period field B_dR = Frac(B_dR^+).

declarations.name: BdR.smul_algebraMap_qpBar
declarations.says: The embedding Q̄_p → B_dR is G_p-equivariant.

declarations.name: Lift.iterate_frobEnd_teichmuller
declarations.says: φ^n([x]) = [x]^(p^n) for x ∈ O^♭.

declarations.name: Lift.teichmuller_mem_wittMaxIdeal
declarations.says: If x ∈ O^♭ is not a unit, its Teichmüller lift [x] lies in the ideal W(𝔪^♭).

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Fontaine's period rings and the fundamental exact sequence (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.PeriodRings.BdR).

declarations.name: BPlus.eq_zero_of_forall_pow_dvd
declarations.says: For a ∈ A_inf, an element of B^+ = A_max[1/p] divisible by (ξ − pa)^n for every n is zero (B^+ is (ξ − pa)-adically separated).
declarations.reference: O. Brinon, B. Conrad, CMI notes on p-adic Hodge theory (2009) (injectivity of B_cris^+ → B_dR^+)
declarations.note: variant with ξ − pa of the separatedness that makes B^+ ⊂ B_dR^+

declarations.name: BdRPlus.isUnit_iff
declarations.says: An element x of B_dR^+ is a unit iff θ(x) ≠ 0 (B_dR^+ is local with residue field C_p).

declarations.name: thetaBdR
declarations.says: θ: B_dR^+ → C_p, projection to B^+/ξB^+ followed by its identification with C_p.

entries.known_result: header: part of abelian schemes: isogenies finite flat, [m]*L = L^{m²}, Cartier, unramified torsion (see Lib.Shimura.AbelianScheme.ThetaFamily)

declarations.name: abbrev
declarations.says: Two class abbreviations named 'abbrev' by the census: AddObj (a commutative group object over a scheme S) and IsIsogeny (a homomorphism of such objects that is finite, flat and surjective).
declarations.note: Census artifact: 'class abbrev AddObj' and 'class abbrev IsIsogeny' were parsed with the name 'abbrev'; the syntactic use by New is probably the keyword 'abbrev', not these classes (New never mentions AddObj or IsIsogeny).

declarations.name: specOver.map
declarations.says: For an R-algebra homomorphism φ: C → D, the induced morphism Spec D → Spec C of schemes over Spec R.

declarations.name: specOver.map_comp
declarations.says: Functoriality: Spec(ψ∘φ) = Spec(φ)∘Spec(ψ) over Spec R.

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: Space.exists_entireTheta_eq
declarations.says: V standard, d ∈ O_E, dd̄ = N ≠ 0: every entire function S on ℂ^{Φ×n} invariant under the normalised (theta-multiplier) translations by −r(d̄γ), for all γ ∈ E^n with α⁻¹γ integral, equals Θ_F for some F in the finite part 𝒲_f admitting vacuum-expansion data for (d, N).
declarations.note: Classical description of theta functions of a given level as Weil translates (Stone–von Neumann / Schur orthogonality for the finite Heisenberg group); no source cited; ~50-line proof.

declarations.name: entireTheta_translate_finiteImage
declarations.says: For standard V, γ ∈ E^n and f: translating f by the finite part α⁻¹γ turns the theta function Θ_f into y ↦ exp(⟨r,y⟩ − ⟨r,r⟩/2)·Θ_f(y − r), r = r(γ) the archimedean image of γ, ⟨z,w⟩ = Σ z̄_i w_i.
declarations.note: Computation with the Heisenberg bicharacter on the adelic sum.

declarations.name: exists_finiteImage_approx
declarations.says: For F ∈ 𝒲_f and a finite adelic vector x there is γ ∈ E^n with α⁻¹γ − x ∈ Ô^n and ϱ(α⁻¹γ)F = ϱ(x)F.
declarations.note: Density of E in 𝔸_{E,f} and local constancy.

declarations.name: realImage
declarations.says: The archimedean image of γ ∈ E^n in Fock coordinates: the complex vector with entry √(2π·Im τ(ȷ))·τ(γ_i) at (τ, i), τ in the CM type.

entries.known_result: Part of: theta kernels of unitary dual pairs: functoriality, seesaw, growth, rapid decay (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/KernelDecay)

declarations.name: exists_pairTheta_flip
declarations.says: Swapping the dual pair: if V′ has signs opposite to V and frame x_{V′}·l = (1, conj(cα/ᾱ))·x_V, then for each b some z with |z| = 1 has θ^{W,V′}_{b⁻¹υ^{rk W}, a′⁻¹υ^{rk V}}(f∘φ)(h, l g) = z·θ^{V,W}_{a′,b}(f)(g, h) for all a′, f, g, h (φ = flip of coordinates).
declarations.note: Uniqueness of the theta functional up to scalar; z not computed.

declarations.name: flipCoords
declarations.says: For a unit c of Ô with c̄c = −1 and signs t′ = −t, the change of coordinates x ↦ (1, cα/ᾱ)·ε_s x* ε_t from Hom(V,W) (signs t′_i s_j) to Hom(W,V) (signs s_j t_i): conjugate transpose with signs.

declarations.name: flipPoly
declarations.says: The ℂ-algebra map on polynomials sending the variable X_{(τ,i,j)} to −s_i t_j·X_{(τ,j,i)} (transposition with signs).

declarations.name: flipSpace
declarations.says: The opposite space of V = (J, x): Gram matrix −J, opposite signs, frame x scaled by the idele (1, c̄ᾱ/α), c a fixed finite idele with c̄c = −1.

entries.known_result: Part of: transfer of Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi periods under a theta lift, one unfolding step (known result stated in Lib/Weil/Periods/UnfoldingStep); this file: gradings by a nilpotent string, degree filtrations

declarations.name: Grading.gradeOf
declarations.says: The grade of a basis index of V graded by a nilpotent string: 0 on the indices of X, and s − 1 − 2i on the i-th vector of the string (0 ≤ i < s).

declarations.name: HasDegreeGe.mul
declarations.says: Degree filtrations are multiplicative: if x has degree ≥ d and y has degree ≥ d′ (for compatible gradings), then xy has degree ≥ d + d′.

declarations.name: gradedBlocks
declarations.says: The block-diagonal matrix with block A on X and block B on the string, reindexed along the given index bijections.

declarations.name: gradedGram
declarations.says: The Gram matrix of X plus a string of length s: identity on X; string vectors a, b with a + b = s − 1 pair to 1, or to −N if a = b.

entries.known_result: Branching GL(n+1)→GL(n) with multiplicity one (Goodman–Wallach 2009, Thm 8.1.1); dual of a Weyl module by Jacobi's complementary minors and the Cartan component (Fulton–Harris 1991, §15.5; Grinberg, Thm 6.4.48); Schur's lemma for U(n). New uses only the cyclicity, the duality and Schur's lemma, not the branching law.

declarations.name: PolyRep.ext_schur_weylEval
declarations.says: Over a field K of characteristic 0 the extremal vector ev (evaluation vector at a permutation array) is cyclic for ∏_τ GL(n_τ,K) acting by Schur matrices S_κ: two linear maps agreeing on every S_κ(g)·ev are equal.
declarations.note: Cyclicity of an extremal weight vector of the Weyl module; proof by substitution (S_κ(squarePart y)·ev = ev_y) and density of evaluation vectors.

declarations.name: exists_dual_isometry
declarations.says: Duality of Weyl lattices: for the complementary weight κ'_τ(h)=κ_τ(|n_τ|−h) there is a unimodular integer matrix J with JᵀG_κJ = G_κ' (Gram matrices), J·ev_e = ev_e' and S_κ(g^{−T})J = ∏_τ det(g_τ)^{−c_τ}·J·S_κ'(g), c_τ = Σ_{1≤i<|n_τ|} κ_τ(i).
declarations.reference: Fulton, Harris, Representation Theory (1991); Grinberg, An Introduction to Algebraic Combinatorics (Jacobi's complementary minors)
declarations.place: §15.5 (FH) and Thm 6.4.48 (Grinberg), as cited in the file header; authors' check: compared
declarations.note: The cited results give the duality S_κ(V)* ≅ S_κ'(V)⊗det^{−c} over ℂ and Jacobi's identity; the integral unimodular isometric form proved here is stronger than the cited statements, so the write-up must read it or find an integral source.

declarations.name: scalar_of_commute_schur
declarations.says: Schur's lemma for the Schur (Weyl) modules under the unitary group: a complex matrix commuting with S_κ(g) for every tuple g of unitary matrices g_τ ∈ U(n_τ) is scalar, i.e. ∏_τ U(n_τ) acts absolutely irreducibly on the module of weight κ.
declarations.reference: Irreducibility of Schur modules S_λ(ℂⁿ) under GL_n(ℂ) and its Zariski-dense subgroup U(n) (Weyl), with Schur's lemma; header of Lib/Adelic/CuspForms/DeltaForms cites Goodman–Wallach, Symmetry, Representations, and Invariants (2009), ch. 5, and Jantzen (2003)
declarations.place: Goodman–Wallach 2009, ch. 5, as cited in the header of Lib/Adelic/CuspForms/DeltaForms (REFERENCES.md: compared, place confirmed, for that file); no theorem number
declarations.relation: the theorem (irreducibility in commutant form, for the external tensor product over the places τ)
declarations.note: Proof in Lean: Zariski density of U(n) in GL_n plus a highest-weight argument through the Fock pairing.

entries.known_result: header: part of the standard basis theorem for Schur (dual Weyl) modules over any ring (see Lib/GLn/SchurModule/MinorBasis: De Concini–Eisenbud–Procesi 1980; Akin–Buchsbaum–Weyman 1982).

declarations.name: PolyRep.HasLeadingTerm.mul
declarations.says: Leading terms (for the column monomial order) multiply: if F has leading term a·x^γ and F' has a'·x^γ', then FF' has leading term aa'·x^{γ+γ'}.

declarations.name: PolyRep.HasLeadingTerm.prod
declarations.says: The leading term of a finite product is the product of the leading terms (degrees add).

declarations.name: PolyRep.HasLeadingTerm.sum
declarations.says: If one summand F_j has leading degree δ_j strictly above the degrees δ_i of all other summands, the sum has leading term that of F_j.

entries.known_result: header: part of local-global compatibility at tame level (see LabelCompatibility).

declarations.name: isUnitary_localFormRep
declarations.says: The representation of GL_N(E_w) (w split) on forms of weight κ on V is unitary for a chosen invariant inner product (forms on a definite unitary group: finite level sets, Petersson-type product).

declarations.name: le_span_isSphericalOff
declarations.says: A finite-dimensional space of forms fixed by the integral points trivial at S and stable under the Hecke operators T_{w,j} at split w with w, w̄ ∉ S is spanned by its Hecke eigenvectors off S.
declarations.note: Simultaneous diagonalization of a commuting family of normal (Petersson-adjoint-closed) Hecke operators.

declarations.name: localFormRep
declarations.says: The representation of GL_N(E_w), N = |n|, on forms of weight κ on V at a split place w, through the identification U(E_w) ≅ GL_N(E_w) and a numbering of n.

entries.known_result: header: part of local-global compatibility at tame level (see LabelCompatibility).

declarations.name: HasParahoricType
declarations.says: Depth-zero parahoric type: each k ∈ GL_n(O_w), block upper triangular mod w (blocks given by b, block 0 = image of e) with block 0 equal to x, sends f to ∏_l χ_l(det k_{l+1})·ψ(det x)·F(x) (χ_l, ψ characters of k_w^×, F a function on GL_ρ(k_w)).

declarations.name: HasParahoricType.hasProductLabel
declarations.says: Type implies label (Frobenius reciprocity): for a label c of degree |ρ| with roots scaled by x_ψ, distinct χ_l with c'(x_{χ_l}) ≠ 0, and F not orthogonal to Green's character Ξ_c, a form with that parahoric type has the product label c'·∏(X − x_{χ_l})^{t_l} (Green's character times χ_l∘det on the blocks).
declarations.note: Combines Frobenius reciprocity for the parahoric with Green's characters (Lib/LocalGL/Green).

declarations.name: HasProductLabel
declarations.says: f has product label at w: c monic squarefree of degree d with c(0) ≠ 0, c·∏(X − x_{χ_l}) separable, d + Σ t_l = n, and f transforms under GL_n(k_w) by Green's character Ξ_c times ∏_l (χ_l∘det on GL_{t_l}) (parabolically induced).

entries.known_result: header: chain rule for power series substitution; jets under linear substitution (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: jet_subst_linearSeries
declarations.says: Chain rule for a linear substitution: for a matrix M, the jet pairing P(d)F(Mz)|_{z=0} equals the jet pairing of the polynomial P(M^T x) with F.
declarations.note: jet(P, F) = P(d/dz)F at 0 (the Fock/Fischer pairing).

declarations.name: map_pderiv
declarations.says: A ring homomorphism applied to the coefficients of a multivariate power series commutes with partial derivatives.

declarations.name: mem_range_seriesToCp
declarations.says: A power series over C_p has all coefficients in the closed unit ball iff it comes from a series with coefficients in O_{C_p}.

entries.known_result: header: functions on ring-valued points of schemes, regularity (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: LandsIn.mono
declarations.says: If a morphism t lands in the open U (t^-1 U is everything) and U lies in V, then t lands in V.

declarations.name: PointFn.IsRegularOn.mono
declarations.says: A function on ring-valued points regular on U is regular on every smaller open V.
declarations.note: Regular on U: for points landing in U its values commute with all ring maps.

declarations.name: PointFn.IsRegularOn.mul
declarations.says: If f is regular on U and g on V, then f g is regular on U cap V.

entries.known_result: header: smooth and unitary representations; averaging projector over a compact subgroup (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: IsSmoothRep
declarations.says: The representation rho of the topological group G is smooth: every vector is fixed by all g in some neighbourhood of 1.

declarations.name: compactMean_mem_levelSpace
declarations.says: For a smooth representation and a compact subgroup H, the mean of rho over H (average of rho(h)x over H) is H-invariant.
declarations.note: compactMean averages rho(a^-1 b)x over (a,b) in H x H; for smooth rho a finite average.

declarations.name: map_compactMean_of_const
declarations.says: If a (semi)linear map phi takes the constant value c on the H-orbit {rho(h)x : h in H}, then phi(mean of x over H) = c.

entries.known_result: header: Auerbach's lemma; Steinitz (embeddings of a countable ring extend to an isomorphism with ℂ); trace-form semisimplicity; common eigenvectors of commuting operators

declarations.name: IsTraceNondeg
declarations.says: For a representation r: G → GL_n(k): the trace form (x, y) ↦ tr(xy) is non-degenerate on the k-span of r(G), i.e. x in the span with tr(x·r(g)) = 0 for all g is 0.

declarations.name: exists_auerbach
declarations.says: Auerbach's lemma: if linear forms ℓ_a (a in a compact space) on a finite-dimensional K-space have no common zero but 0, and a ↦ φ(ℓ_a(v)) is continuous (φ: K → L normed), some ℓ_{S(k)} are the dual coordinates of a basis z with |φ(ℓ_a(z_k))| ≤ 1 for all a, k.
declarations.reference: H. Auerbach (thesis, Lwów 1930); textbook form in P. Wojtaszczyk, Banach Spaces for Analysts (Cambridge 1991)
declarations.relation: the theorem (in the maximal-determinant form: the norm is the supremum of a compact separating family of forms, and the biorthogonal forms are chosen in the family)
declarations.note: Proof in Lean: choose S maximising |det(ℓ_{S(i)}(b_j))| and use Cramer's rule. Unconfirmed guess: Wojtaszczyk II.E.11.

declarations.name: exists_ringEquiv_extend
declarations.says: Steinitz's theorem: for injective ring maps f: K → ℂ and g: K → L from a nonzero countable commutative ring K, with L algebraically closed of the cardinality of ℂ, there is a field isomorphism σ: ℂ → L with σ∘f = g.
declarations.reference: E. Steinitz, Algebraische Theorie der Körper, J. reine angew. Math. 137 (1910) 167–309
declarations.relation: special case: algebraically closed fields of characteristic 0 and transcendence degree continuum (ℂ and L) are isomorphic, by an isomorphism extending a given one of the (countable) images of K
declarations.note: Proof in Lean: transcendence bases over K of equal cardinality, then uniqueness of algebraic closure.

entries.known_result: header: part of adeles of a number field: base change, discreteness and compact quotient, modulus (see Lib.Adelic.Adeles.IdeleHilbert90); this file: fundamental domains and covolumes of adelic lattices, box domains for filtered discrete subgroups

declarations.name: Filling.existsUnique_mul_mem_box
declarations.says: Successive reduction: for injective graded coordinates c on a group G and a subgroup Γ whose elements trivial below degree i shift c_i by elements of L_i (all of L_i occurring), and fundamental domains F_i of L_i, each x has a unique γ ∈ Γ with c(xγ) ∈ ∏_i F_i.
declarations.note: Fundamental domain of a lattice in a filtered (e.g. unipotent) group, by induction on the degree.

declarations.name: Filling.exists_fundamental_domain_im_skew
declarations.says: For a CM field E containing a primitive 5040-th root of unity and nonzero reals t_v: the lattice {(t_v Im Φ_v(s))_v : s ∈ O_E, s̄ = −s} in ℝ^{infinite places} has a measurable fundamental domain of volume ∏|t_v|·|disc E|^{1/4} (= ∏|t_v|·√|disc E⁺|).
declarations.note: Ingredients: i ∈ O_E gives skew integers = i·O_{E⁺}; covolume of O_{E⁺} is √|d_{E⁺}|; E/E⁺ unramified at finite places, so |d_E| = d_{E⁺}². 'Stably unramified' (E ∋ ζ_5040) is the proof's hypothesis on E.

declarations.name: exists_fundamental_domain_classLattice
declarations.says: For t ∈ ((E ⊗ ℝ)^×)^n and m ∈ GL_n(𝔸_f): the lattice {(t_{j,v}Φ_v(x_j)) : x ∈ E^n, mx integral} has a measurable fundamental domain of volume ∏_w|∏_j t_j(w)|² · |det m|_f / volÔ^n, where volÔ = 2^{r₂}/√|disc E|.
declarations.note: Covolume of O_E^n (Minkowski: 2^{−r₂}√|d_E| per copy) rescaled by t and by the index of the lattice defined by m; genIndex(det m) = |det m|_f⁻¹.

entries.known_result: Satake parameters of unitary unramified representations of GL_n come in strings (Tadić 1986; Bernstein 1984); exponents, U-operators and spherical vectors at pro-p Iwahori level (Casselman 1980).

declarations.name: HasRootString
declarations.says: P(dX) = (X−1)(X−q)⋯(X−q^{t−1})·S with S dividing e: the roots of P contain the string d⁻¹, d⁻¹q, …, d⁻¹q^{t−1}.

declarations.name: chain_lemma
declarations.says: Chain lemma: for a nonzero spherical Hecke eigenvector x with Hecke polynomial P in a smooth unitary representation of GL_N(E_w): a root c of P with P(qc) ≠ 0 has |c|² ≥ q^{N−2}; and if P(dX) contains the string (X−1)⋯(X−q^k) times R, then x ⊥ (U − q^k)R(U)y (in the variable dX) for every pro-p-Iwahori-fixed y, U the operator of diag(ϖ,1,…,1).
declarations.reference: Tadić, Ann. ENS 19 (1986); Bernstein, LNM 1041 (1984)
declarations.note: The authors relate it to Tadić's classification of the unitary dual and Bernstein's inequality at segment ends (REFERENCES.md: work found, no place given); the Lean proof is direct, with no classification. The orthogonality part has no cited source.

declarations.name: isRoot_string_of_norm
declarations.says: Strings of Satake roots: for x as above, if P(c) = 0 and |c|²q^k = q^N then c, cq, …, cq^{k−1} are all roots of P.
declarations.reference: Tadić, Ann. ENS 19 (1986); Bernstein, LNM 1041 (1984)
declarations.note: A necessary condition on Satake parameters of unitary unramified representations; consistent with Tadić's classification, proved directly.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Almost acyclicity of the structure sheaf for the v-topology (known result; see Lib.PadicComparison.Descent.AlmostAcyclic).

declarations.name: Comparison.restrict
declarations.says: The comparison datum along a functor φ: C' → C from an abelian-group-valued functor N to N∘φ, with the identity coefficient map (restriction of a cohomological comparison).

declarations.name: PadicTest.twist
declarations.says: For g in G_p = Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p), the endofunctor of p-adic tests (O_C-algebras S) that keeps S and precomposes its structure map O_C → S with the action of g.

declarations.name: tensorWith.mk
declarations.says: For m ∈ M and a functor Φ to S-modules, the natural map of coefficient functors Φ → M ⊗_S Φ, x ↦ m ⊗ x.

entries.known_result: The rank formula for the Bloch–Kato finite local condition and the size of its annihilator

declarations.name: crysCocycles.apply_eq_zero_of_cyclotomicGp
declarations.says: Bloch–Kato's computation of H^1_f for Tate twists: if Γ acts on T (finite free over Z_p) through χ^(−a), a ≥ 0, every crystalline cocycle c vanishes at each s with ρ(s) = 1, provided j(s) is in inertia when a = 0.
declarations.reference: S. Bloch, K. Kato, L-functions and Tamagawa numbers of motives, Grothendieck Festschrift I (1990)
declarations.relation: weaker form: for Z_p(r), r = −a ≤ 0, only the consequence that crystalline cocycles vanish on ker ρ (on inertia if a = 0), instead of H^1_f(Q_p(r)) = 0 for r < 0 and H^1_f = unramified classes for r = 0
declarations.note: unconfirmed guess: Bloch–Kato Example 3.9; Lean derives it from the rank formula crysCocycles.finrank_eq; Γ is any group with j: Γ → G_p of open image, cocycles not assumed continuous

declarations.name: crysCocycles.fg
declarations.says: If j: Γ → G_p has open image and T is finite free over Z_p and potentially crystalline, the R-module Z_f(T) of crystalline cocycles is finitely generated.
declarations.note: corollary of crysCocycles.finrank_eq

declarations.name: crysCocycles.finrank_eq
declarations.says: Bloch–Kato rank formula: for T finite free over Z_p and potentially crystalline with Hodge–Tate jumps J over Z_p, Z_f(T) is finitely generated over Z_p of rank rk T + [G_p : j(Γ)]·#{negative jumps in J} (with multiplicity).
declarations.reference: S. Bloch, K. Kato, L-functions and Tamagawa numbers of motives, Grothendieck Festschrift I (1990); J. Bellaïche, An introduction to the conjecture of Bloch and Kato (2009)
declarations.relation: special case: potentially crystalline (Bloch–Kato: de Rham) Z_p-lattices; stated for the module of crystalline cocycles Z_f rather than H^1_f (rank of cocycles = rank of coboundaries + dim H^1_f, i.e. rk T + dim D_dR/Fil^0), with Colmez's B_max as period ring
declarations.note: header cites BK Prop. 3.8, Cor. 3.8.4 and Bellaïche Prop. 2.8, Thm 2.1; file is in REFERENCES.md's unchecked list (gives places); of the duality only a count of orders mod p^m is proved (header)

entries.known_result: Ax–Sen–Tate theorem and Tate's vanishing of the invariants of C_p(i)

declarations.name: exists_gp_eq_algHom
declarations.says: Every Z_p-algebra map γ (from an algebraic extension inside Q̄_p) to C_p is the restriction of some s ∈ G_p.

declarations.name: localFieldOf
declarations.says: The local field K = Q̄_p^{j(Γ)} cut out by j: Γ → G_p.

declarations.name: nearOne_eq_nhds_one
declarations.says: If j is an open embedding, the filter 'near 1' on Γ is the neighbourhood filter of 1.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Kisin modules: Galois action trivial modulo the variable, Hodge–Tate weights read off (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.WachGamma.Letters).

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.conjForm_mem_forms
declarations.says: If g ∈ Γ normalises Γ' and μ is a Γ'-equivariant form on W(C^♭) ⊗ L, its conjugate x ↦ j(g)⁻¹ μ(gx) is again Γ'-equivariant.

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.pow_smul_gal_sub_mem_span_of_dvd
declarations.says: If d divides g·y − y for every y in the bicommutant S_B, and E^m x = s for some s ∈ S_B (in B_dR), then E^(2m)(g x − x) ∈ B^+·d.
declarations.note: technical step towards 'Galois action trivial modulo the variable'

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.smul_mem_kisinAinf
declarations.says: If g ∈ Γ normalises Γ', then g maps the A_inf-Kisin module M of L (kisinAinf) into itself.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Kisin lattice (Breuil–Kisin module) of a crystalline lattice (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.WachKisin.PeriodMatrixFrame).

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.equivariant_iff_basisValues
declarations.says: In coordinates: for an invertible matrix A with ρ(g)·g(A) = A, a pair of functionals satisfies μ'(1 ⊗ gt) = g μ(1 ⊗ t) iff their value vectors satisfy v(μ')A = g(v(μ)A).

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.exists_functional_extend
declarations.says: Every Z_p-linear f: L → B_dR extends to an A_inf-linear functional μ on W(C^♭) ⊗ L with μ(1 ⊗ t) = f(t).
declarations.note: B_dR is a vector space over Frac(A_inf), hence an injective A_inf-module

declarations.name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinAinf_le_fracSpan
declarations.says: The A_inf-Kisin module M is contained in fracSpan.

entries.known_result: header: part of integral Kuga–Sato models for GU(1, n−1) (see Lib.Shimura.IntegralModel.ModelExistence) and of complex uniformisation of PEL abelian varieties (see Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert); this file: frames determine forms, levels of large norm are neat

declarations.name: IsFrameFor.unique
declarations.says: If x ∈ GL_n(𝔸_f(E)) is a frame for both hermitian matrices β and β' over E (x*βx and x*β'x are scalars in Ẑ^×), and both are positive definite at one complex embedding, then β' = β.
declarations.note: β'/β is a rational scalar in Ẑ^×, so ±1, and positivity gives +1.

declarations.name: classAut_eq_bot
declarations.says: Neatness (Minkowski–Serre lemma): for a CM field E with at least two infinite places, distinct finite places w_i with (2n)^{[E:ℚ]} < ∏ q_{w_i}, and K ⊂ G_f ∩ GL_n(Ô) reducing to 1 mod every w_i: Γ_f ∩ gKg⁻¹ = {1} for all g, Γ_f the rational points of the definite unitary group U(I_n).
declarations.reference: J.-P. Serre, Rigidité du foncteur de Jacobi d'échelon n ≥ 3, Sém. Henri Cartan 13 (1960/61), appendix; H. Minkowski (1887)
declarations.relation: special case: definite unitary groups over CM fields (Γ ∩ gKg⁻¹ is finite, hence trivial), with the explicit condition (2n)^{[E:ℚ]} < ∏ q_{w_i} on the level in place of 'level ≥ 3'
declarations.note: Method: a finite-order element ≡ 1 mod ∏ w_i has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n by a size bound on its coefficients.

declarations.name: heckeAlgebra
declarations.says: The Hecke algebra of the pair (GU⁺_n, K(𝔑)): elements Σ a_g[g] of k[G] supported on GU⁺ whose function Σ a_g 1_{gK(𝔑)} is left K(𝔑)-invariant.

entries.known_result: header: part of complex uniformisation of PEL abelian varieties; Appell–Humbert; finite class number (see Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert)

declarations.name: IsFrameFor.mul_iff
declarations.says: If x ∈ GL_n(𝔸_f(E)) is a frame for β (x*βx = ε·1, ε ∈ Ẑ^×), then for c ∈ E and g ∈ GL_n(𝔸_f(E)): xg is a frame for cβ iff g is a frame for c·1.

declarations.name: IsReflection.conj
declarations.says: A conjugate zJz⁻¹ of a reflection J (in GL_n(ℂ)) is a reflection.

declarations.name: IsSignedFrame.mul
declarations.says: Signed frames are transported: if (x, J) is a signed frame, then (zxg, zJz⁻¹) is one for z ∈ GL_n(E) (acting on J through the embedding Φ_{v₀}) and g a unitary similitude in GU.

entries.known_result: header: part of complex uniformisation of PEL abelian varieties; Appell–Humbert; finite class number (see Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert)

declarations.name: HasGermAt.lift
declarations.says: For a projectively embedded A and a germ class Q at w₀ (closed under analytic functions of finitely many members): if the families of complex points φ, ψ of A have germs in Q at w₀, so does the family of pairs (φ, ψ) in the fibre product.

declarations.name: HolomorphicAt.comp
declarations.says: If a family φ of complex points of X is holomorphic at g(v₀) and g is analytic at v₀, then φ∘g is holomorphic at v₀.

declarations.name: IsJet.congr
declarations.says: The jet of a family of complex points at w₀ depends only on its germ: families agreeing near w₀ have the same jets.

entries.known_result: part of: tower property, constant term of a theta lift along an isotropic line (see Lib.SiegelWeil.Tower.LargeSideConstantTerm): constant term unfolded over orbits

declarations.name: constTermAt_smul_k
declarations.says: For xi != 0, the contribution to the constant term along the isotropic line of the rational vector xi k (k the line of the splitting X) is theta of the line term of f at xi.
declarations.note: Change of variables in the mean over the radical, in the mixed model.

declarations.name: constTermAt_zero
declarations.says: The contribution of x = 0 to the constant term along the line is theta of the source term of f at 0 (unfolding).
declarations.note: unfolding

declarations.name: integral_thetaIntegral_lineRadical
declarations.says: If the theta kernel of f is target-bounded, the constant term at g along the isotropic line of A of the theta integral over [U(V)] equals the integral over h of the sum over rational x of the orbit contributions constTermAt of omega(g,h)f.
declarations.note: Standard unfolding of the constant term (Fubini justified by the boundedness hypothesis).

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: Space.ratVectors
declarations.says: The rational points of V: the additive subgroup of 𝔸^n of vectors x⁻¹y, y ∈ E^n, x the adelic frame of V.

declarations.name: smul_eq_mat_mulVec
declarations.says: The action of g on adelic vectors is multiplication by its matrix.
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: vacuumMeasure
declarations.says: The Haar measure on 𝔸^n image of (real Fock measure) × (lattice measure on finite adeles) under the identification of 𝔸^n with real and finite coordinates.

entries.known_result: Part of the Bargmann–Fock model of the oscillator representation of U(p,q) (known result stated in Lib/Weil/Fock/OscillatorPair); this file: the theta function of a real vacuum datum is entire and determines the datum

declarations.name: Space.entireTheta
declarations.says: For f in the model space S(V) of the adelic Weil representation and y a vector of complex coordinates at the infinite places, Θ_f(y) = θ(ϱ(y)f)·exp(|y|²/2) (y placed among the adelic vectors with finite part zero).
declarations.note: θ is the theta functional, ϱ the Heisenberg action; dividing by the Gaussian vacuum exp(−|y|²/2).

declarations.name: Space.entireTheta_eq_integral
declarations.says: If all signs of V are positive and f is a real vacuum (fixed by the projection that inserts the Gaussian at the real places), then Θ_f(y) = ∫ exp(Σ_p y_p w̄_p)·e(w)·f(w) dw over complex real-place coordinates w, e the Gaussian.
declarations.note: Bargmann-transform type integral formula, obtained from the reproducing identity of the vacuum; used to prove that Θ_f is entire.

declarations.name: Space.eq_zero_of_realVec
declarations.says: An element f of S(V) whose values f(y) = θ(ϱ(y)f) vanish at every adelic vector y with finite part zero is zero.
declarations.note: Proof: invariance of θ under rational translations and density of E in the finite adeles, plus continuity.

entries.known_result: the Bargmann–Fock model of the harmonic (oscillator) representation of U(p,q)

declarations.name: isUnitaryRep_detTwist
declarations.says: Bargmann–Fock model of the oscillator representation of U(p,q): for a continuous homomorphism f: U(ε) → U(ε′) with ‖f(g)‖ ≤ a‖g‖, g ↦ det(g)^γ·ω₀(f(g)) on the Fock space is strongly continuous, of norm O(‖g‖^|C|), and preserves the positive definite form ∫c̄c′.
declarations.reference: G. B. Folland, Harmonic Analysis in Phase Space (1989); M. G. Davidson, The harmonic representation of U(p,q) and its connection with the generalized unit disk, Pacific J. Math. 129 (1987)
declarations.place: Folland ch. 1, 4 (second hand); Davidson §1, Prop. 2.2: place not confirmed
declarations.relation: weaker form: on the L¹ reproducing (Feichtinger-type) space, not the Hilbert Fock space; only preservation of the hermitian form, strong continuity and polynomial norm growth; no unitary completion and no kernel formula
declarations.note: The header says weighted moments replace Schwartz seminorms. The unitarity used downstream is that of the pre-Hilbert form ∫c̄c′.

declarations.name: norm_pairHom_le
declarations.says: For g in U(ε′) and h in U(ε), the ℓ² operator norm of x ↦ h x g⁻¹ on R×C matrices is at most ‖g‖·‖h‖.

declarations.name: pairHom
declarations.says: The homomorphism U(ε′) × U(ε) → U(ε⊗ε′), (g, h) ↦ h ⊗ (g⁻¹)ᵀ, i.e. x ↦ h x g⁻¹ on R×C matrices: the dual pair embedding into the unitary group of the signs ε_r ε′_c.

entries.known_result: Part of: Schrödinger and mixed models of the Weil representation (see Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw); this file: ortho-integral adelic matrices

declarations.name: IsOrthoIntegral.mul
declarations.says: Products of ortho-integral adelic matrices (orthonormal columns at the infinite places, integral at the finite places) are ortho-integral.

declarations.name: IsOrthoIntegral.of_eq_submatrix_mul
declarations.says: If C is ortho-integral and e is injective, then (columns e of A)·C is ortho-integral for ortho-integral A.

declarations.name: IsOrthoIntegral.one
declarations.says: The identity matrix is ortho-integral.

entries.known_result: Part of: transfer of Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi periods under a theta lift, one unfolding step (see Lib/Weil/Periods/UnfoldingStep); this file: finite adelic Bessel groups and coordinates

declarations.name: Grading.J_inv_eq_gradedGram
declarations.says: For a space graded by a nilpotent string with parameter N, the inverse Gram matrix J⁻¹ is the graded Gram matrix with parameter N⁻¹.

declarations.name: Space.gram_xFin
declarations.says: For a hermitian space (J, x), the finite part x_f of the adelic point satisfies x_f* J x_f = 1 over the finite adeles.

declarations.name: Space.ratCoordMatrixFin_snd
declarations.says: The finite rational-coordinate matrix of g_f is the finite part of the rational-coordinate matrix of g.
declarations.note: unfolding

entries.known_result: header: part of the duality of Weyl modules and Cartan component (see Branching); this file: integral isometric Cartan component of a Weyl module tensor a dual Weyl module.

declarations.name: mixedCartan
declarations.says: A chosen integral embedding Δ_l → Δ_kp ⊗ Δ_km (l the mixed weight) of Weyl lattices: integer matrix with integral left inverse, isometric for the Gram forms, sending ev₁ to ev₁⊗ev_{w₀} and intertwining det^{−c}S_l(g) with S_kp(g)⊗S_km(g^{−T}).
declarations.note: Its existence (nonempty_mixedCartanEmbedding: the Cartan component of a Weyl module tensor a dual Weyl module, made integral and isometric) is the substantial input, proved from exists_dual_isometry and the comultiplication matrix.

declarations.name: mixedWeight
declarations.says: The mixed weight l(τ,i) = kp(τ,i) + km(τ,|n|−i) (truncated subtraction): highest weight of the Cartan component of Δ_kp ⊗ Δ_km^∨ up to a determinant power.

entries.known_result: header: part of cyclic base change of prime degree for definite unitary groups (see BaseChangeEigenchar).

declarations.name: IsMatchingPair.mul
declarations.says: Matching pairs for cyclic base change multiply: if (f,φ) match for the idempotent u and level K and (f',φ') match for v and L, with u,v orthogonal self-adjoint idempotents, then (ff', φφ') match for u+v and K∩L.
declarations.note: Matching = twisted-invariant functions agreeing through norms (Labesse's matching of functions, in the authors' elementwise form).

declarations.name: IsRootQuotient.mul
declarations.says: If a·z(γ)* = z(γ) and b·w(γ)* = w(γ) for a unitary γ and commuting data, then (ab)·(zw)(γ)* = (zw)(γ).

entries.known_result: Hilbert 90 for GL_n and norm surjectivity on units, for a cyclic action at congruence level

declarations.name: IsProfiniteRing.eqLocus
declarations.says: If σ is a ring automorphism of a profinite ring R with σ^p = 1 and some element of σ-trace 1, then the subring of σ-fixed elements is profinite (it is a retract via x ↦ Σ_i σ^i(ex)).
declarations.note: Not Hilbert 90 itself; a lemma of the file's setting.

declarations.name: IsTameAtLevel.of_map
declarations.says: The tameness condition (σ^p = 1, σ(m) = m, an element of trace ≡ 1 mod m, freeness away from m) transports along a ring homomorphism f semi-conjugating σ to θ with θ^p = 1.

entries.known_result: header: part of local-global compatibility at tame level (see LabelCompatibility).

declarations.name: galRep_of_parahoric_type
declarations.says: Local-global compatibility on a parahoric eigenspace at split w ∤ ℓ: for lifts s of Art(ϖ) and τ of Art(u) and a nonzero y in the eigenspace with values d_i, in the Galois representation of x the elements s and τ commute, polynomials vanishing at all ι(d_i) kill τ, and ∏(X − ι(θ_i(ϖ)d_i^b)) kills sτ^b (b ≥ 0).
declarations.reference: Taylor, Yoshida, Compatibility of local and global Langlands correspondences, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007); Harris, Taylor (2001)
declarations.relation: weaker form: only consequences for depth-zero parahoric eigenvectors at split places w ∤ ℓ (polynomials killing τ and sτ^b), no local Langlands correspondence

declarations.name: hecke_eq_frob_on_parahoricEigenspace
declarations.says: Iwahori-level compatibility of U-operators and Frobenius: for y pro-p-Iwahori fixed at w ∤ ℓ on which the line stabiliser acts by χ of the top-left entry (χ(u) ≠ 0, χ(u)^{n!} ≠ 1), tr((τ−1)M)·G(U)y = tr(G(s)(τ−1)M)·y for every polynomial G and matrix M, U the Hecke operator of diag(ϖ,1,…,1).
declarations.reference: Taylor, Yoshida (2007); Harris, Taylor (2001)
declarations.relation: weaker form: a trace identity on the τ-nontrivial part at Iwahori level, at split places w ∤ ℓ, instead of the full local-global compatibility

entries.known_result: header: part of Galois representations attached to forms on definite unitary groups (see AvatarCompatibility).

declarations.name: Attached
declarations.says: ρ: H → GL_n(ℚ̄_ℓ) is attached to the Hecke polynomials P_w: ρ continuous and semisimple (non-degenerate trace form), j: H → Gal(Ω/E) open, and for every η > 0, at most Frobenii s at w, det(X − ρ(x)) is coefficientwise within η of ι(P_w) whenever j(x) = s.
declarations.note: An approximate (ℓ-adic limit) form of 'the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius is the Hecke polynomial'.

declarations.name: isRoot_of_isRoot_charpoly
declarations.says: If P(M) = 0, every root of the characteristic polynomial of M is a root of P.

entries.known_result: header: Fourier inversion and uniqueness on a compact abelian quotient via Stone-Weierstrass; means over compact quotients and fundamental domains (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: IsDualFamily.eq_zero_of_coeff
declarations.says: Uniqueness of Fourier coefficients on a compact abelian quotient B/B0 whose characters are a 'dual family' chi_i: a continuous B0-periodic F vanishes if its coefficients mean(chi_i F) vanish for every i with chi_i(a) = c whenever c F(x+a) = F(x) for all x.
declarations.reference: Fourier uniqueness on compact abelian groups, e.g. W. Rudin, Fourier Analysis on Groups (1962), ch. 1
declarations.relation: special case: compact abelian quotient with dual given by a separating family chi_i; plus the remark that coefficients at characters incompatible with a translation relation of F vanish automatically
declarations.note: Proved here from Stone-Weierstrass. IsDualFamily: i -> chi_i an injective homomorphism into unitary characters trivial on B0, with common kernel in B0.

declarations.name: IsDualFamily.zero_apply
declarations.says: In a dual family of characters, chi_0 is the trivial character: chi_0(x) = 1.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of combinatorics (textbook or folklore): averages over finite groups

declarations.name: finMean
declarations.says: The average of a complex function f on a finite group G: (1/|G|) sum_g f(g).

declarations.name: finMean_comp_surjective
declarations.says: For a surjective homomorphism p of finite groups, the average of f o p equals the average of f (all fibres have the same size).

entries.known_result: header: Pontryagin duality for the abelianisation of a profinite group; definitions of algebraic Hecke characters and of the global Artin map (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: artinMap
declarations.says: The global Artin map from the finite ideles of K to Gamma^ab (Gamma = Gal(Omega/K) profinite): a homomorphism chosen so that chi(Art a) = sum_v chi(Art_v a_v) for every continuous Q/Z-valued character chi, Art_v the local Artin maps.
declarations.note: Defined by Hilbert's epsilon: the definition only selects a homomorphism with this local-global compatibility; that one exists (global reciprocity) is class field theory, proved elsewhere or assumed where used.

declarations.name: star_locIdele
declarations.says: For a CM field E, complex conjugation sends the finite idele concentrated at v with component x to the idele concentrated at v-bar with the conjugated component.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of group theory (textbook or folklore): central idempotents act self-adjointly; convolution with them is a contraction

declarations.name: IsCentralProj.self_adjoint
declarations.says: A central idempotent e of C[G] (G finite) acts self-adjointly, B(ex, y) = B(x, ey), for every G-invariant form B on a representation V that is linear in y and semilinear in x for sigma^-1 o conj o sigma, sigma a field automorphism of C.
declarations.note: Central idempotents are sums of e_chi = chi(1)/|G| sum chi(g^-1) g, with cyclotomic coefficients satisfying e(g^-1) = conj e(g); conj commutes with sigma on abelian extensions.

declarations.name: IsCentralProj.sum_norm_conv_le
declarations.says: For a central idempotent e of C[G] and a homomorphism phi: G -> H of finite groups, convolution f -> sum_t e(t) f(phi(t)^-1 s) is a contraction of l2(H, V): sum_s |...|^2 <= sum_s |f(s)|^2.
declarations.note: It is an orthogonal projection (self-adjoint idempotent).

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of linear algebra and matrices, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: exists_contDiff_eventuallyEq
declarations.says: A map from a finite-dimensional real normed space to a real normed space that is analytic at x agrees near x with a globally C^∞ map (multiply by a bump function).

declarations.name: mem_rename_range_mul
declarations.says: If the images of p: κ → ι and q: κ' → ι cover ι, every complex polynomial in the variables ι is a sum of products of a polynomial in the variables p(κ) and one in the variables q(κ').

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of algebraic number theory, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: LocProd
declarations.says: The product ∏_{w ∈ P} E_w of the completions of the number field E at a finite set P of finite places.

declarations.name: mem_O_locProd
declarations.says: An element x of ∏_{w∈P} E_w is integral iff |x_w|_w ≤ 1 for every w ∈ P.
declarations.note: Unfolding.

entries.known_result: The Brauer lift is a virtual character, and cuspidal times Steinberg is induced from a torus (Green 1955, Thm 1; Springer, Sém. Bourbaki 441; Carter 7.4.5). New uses only the naming of characters of F_q^× by field elements.

declarations.name: charName
declarations.says: For a fixed injective character T of the algebraic closure, the group isomorphism χ ↦ x_χ from the multiplicative characters of a finite field k to k^×, inverse to a ↦ θ_a|_k (θ_a built from T with Q = |k|).

declarations.name: charName_pow_eq_one
declarations.says: If χ^M = 1 then x_χ^M = 1.

entries.known_result: Green's characters of GL_n(F_q) and the parabolic-induction ring

declarations.name: IsLabel.map
declarations.says: A label over k stays a label over an extension field K.

declarations.name: labelChar_degree_bounds
declarations.says: Degree of Green's characters (lower bound): for a label c of degree r = |n| over F_q, Re Ξ_c(1) ≥ 0 and the coefficient at 1 of e_c, Ξ_c(1)²/|GL_r(F_q)|, has real part ≥ (1 − r/q)·q^{−r}.
declarations.reference: J. A. Green, The characters of the finite general linear groups, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1955)
declarations.relation: weaker form: only a lower bound derived from Green's degree formula, for squarefree labels
declarations.note: Header gives Green 1955 Thms 2, 9, 12–14; this file's citations were not part of the authors' check.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Characters with finite image on inertia are potentially crystalline of weight 0 (known result; see Lib.PadicHodge.Characters.LocalCharacters).

declarations.name: local_clauses_of_retract
declarations.says: If r'(g)P = P r(φ(g)) for g near 1, P'P = 1, and the open embedding φ is conjugation by c ∈ Aut Ω, then finite type, killing polynomials and (if also PP' = 1) the jumps pass from r' at c⁻¹A to r at A.
declarations.note: transport of the local clauses along a retraction and a conjugation

declarations.name: local_clauses_twist
declarations.says: For r' = μ ⊗ r (μ a character): finite type and goodness (unramified, crystalline above ℓ) pass from r and μ to r', jumps shift by the jump of μ, and if X − c kills s on μ and Q(cX) on r then Q kills s on r'.
declarations.reference: O. Brinon, B. Conrad, CMI notes on p-adic Hodge theory (2009)
declarations.note: tensor compatibility of admissibility, Hodge–Tate weights and Frobenius

entries.known_result: Dwork's trick as an integral crystalline comparison over A_max with a uniform denominator (Kisin 2006 Lemma 1.2.6; Kisin 2008 Lemma 2.2; Bhatt–Scholze 2023 proofs of Prop. 5.3, Thm 7.9)

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.tau_mul_z_dvd_smul_sub
declarations.says: For a Breuil–Kisin chart (z = [π^♭]) and g ∈ G_p fixing Λ = W(F_{p^f}) and θ(z), and y in the chart's bicommutant S_B ⊂ B^+, the element τz divides g·y − y in B^+, where τ = [ε^(1/p)] − 1.
declarations.note: technical step of the authors' Dwork-trick argument; S_B (bicommutant) is the authors' device; for y ∈ W[[z]] it reduces to (g − 1)z = ([ε^a] − 1)z

declarations.name: Lift.Chart.tau_mul_z_pow_dvd
declarations.says: For a chart with Eisenstein series E (E(z) ~ ξ): if τ z^n divides E^h a in B^+, then τ z^n divides a in A_inf.
declarations.note: technical divisibility; uses τ | a ⟺ θ(φ^j a) = 0 for all j ≥ 1, and that E is prime to z and to τ

entries.known_result: header: General lemmas of commutative and general algebra (textbook or folklore).

declarations.name: sum_out_mul
declarations.says: A sum over coset representatives of G/H of a right-H-invariant function is unchanged by left translation of the representatives.

declarations.name: unitsMapNonUnital
declarations.says: For a (not necessarily unital) ring homomorphism f: K → R, the homomorphism of unit groups x ↦ 1 + f(x − 1).

entries.known_result: header: part of Frobenius' dimension formula and irreducibility of the theta group (see Lib.Shimura.ComplexTheta.ThetaDimension)

declarations.name: canonicalMultiplier
declarations.says: For a complex-linear endomorphism b of V: the canonical multiplier x ↦ exp(πi E(bx, x)), E the Riemann form (imaginary part) of the hermitian form B.

declarations.name: normalizedShift
declarations.says: The normalised translation operator on theta functions: the twisted translation by x divided by the canonical multiplier exp(πi E(bx, x)).

entries.known_result: header: part of the Hecke algebra of a pair and its action by correspondences on the base of a tower (see Lib.Shimura.HeckeTower.WildType)

declarations.name: asAlgebraHom_eq_sum_support
declarations.says: An element a = Σ a_g[g] of the group ring k[G] acts on a representation π as Σ_{g ∈ supp a} a_g π(g).
declarations.note: Unfolding.

declarations.name: spanOn.mul
declarations.says: If a is supported on D, b on D', and D·D' ⊂ D'', then ab is supported on D'' (in k[G]).

entries.known_result: header: part of integral Kuga–Sato models for GU(1, n−1) (see Lib.Shimura.IntegralModel.ModelExistence) and of the Eichler–Shimura congruence relation at a split place (see Lib.Shimura.CongruenceRelation.CongruenceStep)

declarations.name: ThetaFamily.IsPointOf.eq_iff
declarations.says: Complex points s, u of a fibre power of the family X, attached to moduli points a, b with their 𝔪-torsion, are equal iff a and b are isomorphic at level K(𝔑) ∩ K(𝔪) (moduli interpretation of the Kuga–Sato fibre powers).
declarations.note: Part of the authors' construction of integral models (Lib/Shimura/IntegralModel); the write-up must read it or cite a moduli-theoretic source.

declarations.name: ThetaFamily.proj
declarations.says: The i-th projection from the fibre power of the abelian-scheme family X to X, as a morphism of schemes.

entries.known_result: header: part of the theta group of an ample line bundle: span of sections, K(L), symmetric theta structures (see Lib.Shimura.ThetaGroup.RigidFibres)

declarations.name: IsSectionLift.comp
declarations.says: Lifts compose: if Φ: H⁰(L) → H⁰(L') is pull-back along f followed by f*L ≅ L', and Θ: H⁰(L') → H⁰(L'') likewise along g, then Θ∘Φ is such a map along f∘g.

declarations.name: IsSectionLift.injective
declarations.says: Along a schematically dominant quasi-compact morphism f, a section lift H⁰(L) → H⁰(L') is injective.

entries.known_result: header: part of the theta group of an ample line bundle: span of sections, K(L), symmetric theta structures (see Lib.Shimura.ThetaGroup.RigidFibres)

declarations.name: IsTranslationLift.mul
declarations.says: If Φ lifts translation by z and Ψ lifts translation by w to sections of L, then ΦΨ lifts translation by z + w (theta-group law).

declarations.name: IsTranslationLift.pow
declarations.says: If Φ lifts translation by z, then Φ^k lifts translation by kz.

entries.known_result: header: part of complex uniformisation of PEL abelian varieties; Appell–Humbert; finite class number (see Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert)

declarations.name: HasThetaCoords.mul
declarations.says: If θ, θ' give theta coordinates of types (B, χ), (B', χ') for line bundles N, M along e, then the products θ_pθ'_q give theta coordinates of type (B + B', χχ') for N ⊗ M.

declarations.name: HasThetaCoords.pow
declarations.says: If θ gives theta coordinates of type (B, χ) for N along e, the monomials of degree m in θ give theta coordinates of type (mB, χ^m) for N^m.

entries.known_result: part of: Siegel-Weil formula in the convergent range (see Lib.SiegelWeil.Formula.SiegelWeilFormula): Lagrangians, zero terms, height bounds

declarations.name: Lagrangian.zeroTerm
declarations.says: The zero term ev_L along a Lagrangian L of the split hermitian space S: the value at 0, in the mixed (Schroedinger) model of a chosen complete splitting with kE^r = L, of a Schwartz-Bruhat datum; the Siegel Eisenstein series is the sum of ev_L over Lagrangians.

declarations.name: sourceTerm_zero
declarations.says: The source term at 0 of a splitting D_1 equals the zero term of its source Lagrangian (unfolding).
declarations.note: unfolding

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: adelicHeis
declarations.says: The Heisenberg datum on 𝔸_E^n with bicharacter β(x,y) = ψ(½ȷ·h(y,x)), h the standard hermitian form of signs s, ψ the standard additive character of 𝔸_E, ȷ the purely imaginary element of the Weil data.

declarations.name: vacuumFn
declarations.says: The adelic vacuum vector: x ↦ exp(−π Σ_{i,τ} Im(τ(ȷ))|x_{i,τ}|²) · ψ_f(½c₀ȷ·x_f*x_f) if the finite part x_f lies in αÔ^n, and 0 otherwise (Gaussian at ∞ times a lattice function at the finite places).
declarations.note: α, c₀, ȷ come from the Weil data of the CM field E.

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: Heisenberg.IsVacuum.norm_le_one
declarations.says: A vacuum e satisfies |e(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.

declarations.name: Heisenberg.Rep.rho_zero_apply
declarations.says: In a Heisenberg representation, ρ(0) is the identity.

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilRep
declarations.says: The Weil representation attached to an action A of G (preserving β and the measure) with trivial cocycle: g ↦ (v ↦ Δ(g)·∫ v(y) ρ(gy)vac dμ(y)).

declarations.name: Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilRep_heisOp
declarations.says: ω(g)ρ(x) = ρ(gx)ω(g).

entries.known_result: Part of the Bargmann–Fock model of the oscillator representation of U(p,q) (see Lib/Weil/Fock/OscillatorPair); this file: the cocycle identity for U(p,q), so the oscillator representation splits over U(p,q), by a complex Gaussian determinant

declarations.name: realAction
declarations.says: The action of the real unitary group U(ε) of signature ε on ℂ^ι by matrices, preserving the bicharacter β and Lebesgue measure, with multiplier Δ(g) = conj(det d), d the negative–negative block of g, and trivial cocycle.
declarations.note: Bundles a theorem: the multiplier Δ satisfies the cocycle identity with trivial cocycle, i.e. the oscillator (Weil) representation splits over U(p,q) with this multiplier; proved by a complex Gaussian integral (determinant) computation inside the definition. The write-up must state this splitting (classical; e.g. Kashiwara–Vergne 1978, Kudla 1994 splitting of metaplectic covers; place not confirmed).

declarations.name: realCoordSum
declarations.says: For a bijection e: ι₁ ⊔ ι₂ → ι compatible with signs (ε∘e = ε₁ ⊔ ε₂), the isomorphism ℂ^ι₁ × ℂ^ι₂ ≅ ℂ^ι as an orthogonal sum of Heisenberg data: β_ε is the product of β_ε₁ and β_ε₂ and the Gaussian vacuum factorizes.

entries.known_result: Part of the Bargmann–Fock model of the oscillator representation of U(p,q) (see Lib/Weil/Fock/OscillatorPair); this file: Fock inner product = Fischer product, polynomials dense, matrix coefficients between harmonic polynomials

declarations.name: denseRange_polyVector
declarations.says: The vectors v_P = P(ζ(x))·exp(−|x|²/2), P a complex polynomial in the holomorphic coordinates ζ, are dense in the Fock space 𝓕 (here the L¹ reproducing space of vacuum coefficients, not the Hilbert Fock space).
