declarations.note: Analogue, for the authors' L¹ reproducing model, of the classical density of polynomials in the Bargmann–Fock space (Bargmann 1961; Folland ch. 1); proof: every v is the integral of v(y)·ϱ(y)e, and ϱ(y)e is a limit of polynomial vectors (Taylor series of the kernel).

declarations.name: realInner_polyVector
declarations.says: For complex polynomials P, Q the Fock inner product ⟨v_P, v_Q⟩ equals the Fischer product (P̄(∂)Q)(0), P̄ the polynomial with conjugated coefficients.
declarations.reference: G. B. Folland, Harmonic Analysis in Phase Space (1989), ch. 1
declarations.note: Classical identity (Fock inner product = Fischer inner product), proved here by induction on P using the creation/annihilation intertwining relations.

entries.known_result: Part of the Bargmann–Fock model of the oscillator representation of U(p,q) (see Lib/Weil/Fock/OscillatorPair); this file: inserting a Fock vector at the real places of an adelic datum

declarations.name: Space.dataInner_integrated
declarations.says: For Fock vectors v, w and f, f′ in S(V): ⟨v⊗f, w⊗f′⟩ = ⟨v,w⟩·⟨Pf, Pf′⟩, where v⊗f = ∫ v(y)ϱ(y)f dy over real vectors y and P is the same operation for the Gaussian.
declarations.note: Orthogonality-relation (Moyal-type) identity for the Heisenberg representation, from the general identity in Lib/Weil/Construction/Model.

declarations.name: Space.theta_integrated
declarations.says: For a Fock vector v and f in S(V): θ(v⊗f) = ∫ v(y)·f(y) dy, f(y) = θ(ϱ(y)f), y over real vectors in Fock coordinates.
declarations.note: θ is continuous linear, so it commutes with the Bochner integral.

entries.known_result: header: part of the duality of Weyl modules (see Branching); this file: integral invariant pairing of opposite weights, giving the values of the functions attached to algebraic forms.

declarations.name: exists_dual_pairing_of_isHCParam
declarations.says: For weights (κ,e) and (κ',e') with Harish-Chandra parameters l and −l there is an invariant integer bilinear pairing A between the two coordinate spaces with: F_η(x,g) = A(η(g), ρ(x)v⁺) for algebraic forms η of the second weight; C·A = h_κ'·1 for an integer matrix C (h the hook number); each A(·,v) = ⟨v',·⟩ with ‖v'‖ = ‖v‖.
declarations.note: Assembled from the duality of Weyl lattices (exists_dual_isometry); the identities for algebraic forms make it partly specific to the forms on unitary groups used by the proof.

entries.known_result: header: part of the standard basis theorem for Schur modules (see MinorBasis).

declarations.name: weylRep
declarations.says: The rational representation of ∏_τ GL(n_τ,R) of weight (κ,e): g ↦ ∏_τ det(g_τ)^{e_τ}·S_κ(g), S_κ the Schur matrix (polynomial representation of highest weight given by κ, twisted by a determinant power).

entries.known_result: header: part of cyclic base change of prime degree for definite unitary groups (weak lift, local matching; see BaseChangeEigenchar: Labesse 2011, Cor. 5.3; Labesse 1999; Arthur–Clozel 1989).

declarations.name: Weight.baseChange
declarations.says: Base change of a weight κ from a CM field E to a Galois extension E': at each infinite place of E' take the column numbers and determinant exponent of κ at the place of E below.

entries.known_result: header: one step of Galois representations for definite unitary groups: degree-n polynomials kill most Frobenius elements and a cocharacter with very different exponents forces rank n (related work: Boston–Lenstra–Ribet 1991; Nekovář 2018; Harris–Taylor 2001, VII.1.8).

declarations.name: AlgHeckeChar.baseChange
declarations.says: Base change ω∘N_{E/K₀} of an algebraic Hecke character ω of K₀ to E; its exponent at an embedding σ of E is that of ω at σ|K₀.

entries.known_result: Local-global compatibility at tame level, away from and at l

declarations.name: Attached.isLabelledAt
declarations.says: Local-global compatibility at tame level: if r is attached to an eigenform f on the definite U(n) (standard space, Weil data) with product label c·∏(X−x_{χ_l})^{t_l} at a split place w, then above w r has finite type, Hodge–Tate jumps of the weight κ, and these polynomials kill the inertia/Weil elements with tame exponents (with det = product of roots away from ℓ).
declarations.reference: Harris, Taylor, The geometry and cohomology of some simple Shimura varieties (2001); Taylor, Yoshida, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007); Barnet-Lamb, Gee, Geraghty, Taylor, Local-global compatibility for l = p, II (2014)
declarations.relation: weaker form: only at split places, for sorted tame Iwahori eigencharacters and depth-zero types induced from a squarefree type and characters of det, stated as polynomials killing Weil/inertia elements, with no local Langlands correspondence
declarations.note: Header gives BLGGT II Thm 1.1; this file is not listed in REFERENCES.md. Reduced by the authors to the spherical case by cyclic base change.

entries.known_result: Galois representations attached to forms on definite unitary groups; and the ℓ-adic avatar of an algebraic Hecke character and its local behaviour (header, second paragraph).

declarations.name: avatarCompatAt_of_stablyUnram
declarations.says: ℓ-adic avatar of an algebraic Hecke character and its local behaviour: for a stably unramified CM field E, the avatar μ of an algebraic Hecke character θ has at every place A over every finite w finite type, Hodge–Tate jumps −n(ι⁻¹τ), and each s of degree m ≤ 1 is Art(x) with ord x = m and X − ιθ_w(x) killing s.
declarations.reference: J.-P. Serre, Abelian ℓ-adic representations and elliptic curves (1968); B. Conrad, Lifting global representations with local properties
declarations.place: Serre 1968, ch. II–III; Conrad, App. B (crystalline case) — as cited in the header; authors' check: compared
declarations.relation: special case: rank one, CM fields that are stably unramified; local behaviour above ℓ read off from the rank-one case of the file's Galois representations rather than from Lubin–Tate theory

entries.known_result: header: part of Galois representations attached to forms on definite unitary groups (see AvatarCompatibility).

declarations.name: HasHeckePolyAt.isMonicOfDegree
declarations.says: The Hecke polynomial at w of a nonzero form f on the unitary group in n variables is monic of degree n.

entries.known_result: header: part of Galois representations attached to forms on definite unitary groups (see AvatarCompatibility: Chenevier–Harris 2013, Thm 3.2.3; Labesse 2011, Cor. 5.3; BLGGT 2014, Thm 2.1.1).

declarations.name: sphericalCompat_std
declarations.says: Galois representations attached to forms on definite unitary groups: for a CM field E with Weil data, every eigenform f on the definite U(n) of the standard form has an attached ℓ-adic representation; if f is fixed by the maximal compact at w, each attached one is unramified (w ∤ ℓ) or crystalline (w | ℓ) at w with the Hodge–Tate jumps of f's weight, and every Hecke polynomial at w kills geometric Frobenius.
declarations.reference: G. Chenevier, M. Harris, Construction of automorphic Galois representations II, Camb. J. Math. 1 (2013); J.-P. Labesse, Changement de base CM et séries discrètes (2011); Barnet-Lamb, Gee, Geraghty, Taylor, Potential automorphy and change of weight (2014)
declarations.relation: weaker form: 'attached' only as an ℓ-adic limit at most Frobenii; at spherical places the Hecke polynomial only kills Frobenius (not equality of characteristic polynomials); only the standard definite form over CM fields with Weil data
declarations.note: The main known theorem of Lib/GaloisRep (named in GUIDE.md). Header places Thm 3.2.3 (CH), Cor. 5.3 (Labesse), Thm 2.1.1 (BLGGT); REFERENCES.md: CH 'work found, no place given', BLGGT 'work found, no place given'.

entries.known_result: header: part of Galois representations attached to forms on definite unitary groups (see AvatarCompatibility).

declarations.name: eventually_notMem_star_notMem
declarations.says: For a finite set S of finite places of a CM field and ℓ ≥ 1, all but finitely many places w satisfy w ∉ S, w̄ ∉ S and w ∤ ℓ.

entries.known_result: header: Fitting ideal bounded by a length over a DVR, through a matrix algebra quotient (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: exists_rows_addVal_det_le
declarations.says: O a DVR with valuation v, psi: A -> M_d(O) a surjective O-algebra map, N an A-submodule of A^iota, p != 0, b < v(p). If the vectors w in ((O/p)^d)^iota killed by N through psi lie in a submodule of length <= b, then some square matrix B with rows in N has v(det psi(B)) <= b.
declarations.reference: Fitting ideals over a DVR (elementary divisors), e.g. D. Eisenbud, Commutative Algebra, ch. 20
declarations.note: Elementary divisors over the DVR plus duality of finite-length modules over O/p, lifted through psi; uses exists_matrix_addVal_det_le_length of FittingDuality.

entries.known_result: header: long exact sequences, four and five lemmas, Cech descent of bijectivity (part of: descent of torsion etale cohomology along v-covers; see Lib.Cohomology.Etale.ContinuityAtlas)

declarations.name: BijectiveUpTo.congr
declarations.says: If bijections a_n, b_n satisfy b_n o f_n = g_n o a_n, then the families f and g satisfy the same first r of the conditions 'f_0 injective, f_0 surjective, f_1 injective, ...'.
declarations.note: Transport of 'bijective in degrees up to r' along isomorphic families of maps.

entries.known_result: header: fixed points of an involution on a finite field; for a stably unramified CM field a place with w-bar = w has norm r^2 with r = 3 mod 4, so a place of prime norm is split

declarations.name: isSplit_of_q_prime
declarations.says: E a CM field containing a primitive 5040-th root of unity, w a finite place of E of prime absolute norm q: then w is split, i.e. w-bar != w (complex conjugation moves w).
declarations.note: If w-bar = w, conjugation induces an involution of the residue field moving i = sqrt(-1), whose fixed field has r elements with r^2 = q; impossible for q prime. 'StablyUnram' = contains a primitive 5040-th root of unity (the proof's fields).

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of commutative algebra (textbook or folklore): jets under renaming of variables

declarations.name: jet_rename
declarations.says: The jet pairing P(d)F(0) of a polynomial P with a power series F is unchanged when both are renamed along an injective map of variables.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of commutative algebra (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: eq_zero_of_forall_pow_dvd
declarations.says: In the pi-adic completion of a commutative ring R, an element divisible by every power of pi is 0 (the completion is pi-adically separated).

entries.known_result: header: holomorphy in several variables, Cauchy estimates, holomorphic parameter integrals (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: norm_sub_le_of_holomorphic_bdd
declarations.says: Schwarz lemma, Lipschitz form: if f from a finite-dimensional complex normed space to a complex normed space is holomorphic with |f| <= B on the open ball of radius r about c, then |f(z) - f(c)| <= (2B/r)|z - c| on that ball.
declarations.reference: Schwarz lemma, e.g. W. Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis, ch. 12
declarations.relation: weaker form: the Lipschitz bound obtained by applying the Schwarz lemma to (f(c + r w) - f(c))/2B on complex lines (constant 2B instead of B since f(c) need not be 0); vector-valued, several variables

entries.known_result: header: reduced closures of points; free finite group actions are etale; Lefschetz local terms of Hecke correspondences as sums over marked pairs (part of: transfer of eigensystems between inner forms of a unitary group, see Lib.Shimura.Transfer.PELDataExistence)

declarations.name: ReducedClosure.proj
declarations.says: For the reduced closure W (a reduced closed subscheme of the product over S of the Z_j, with a dense family of complex points lifting given tuples), the morphism W -> Z_j: inclusion followed by the j-th projection.

entries.known_result: header: functor of points on k-algebras, coefficient functors, points and local terms (part of: half of the holomorphic Lefschetz (Woods Hole) formula, see Lib.Cohomology.PointClass.GaloisRep)

declarations.name: PointsIn.map
declarations.says: Functoriality of points: for a k-algebra map phi: A -> B and an A-valued point y of W over Spec R, the B-valued point y o Spec(phi).

entries.known_result: header: open subfunctors of functors on algebras; etale charts (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: IsOpenSub.preimage
declarations.says: The preimage of an open subfunctor under a natural transformation Y -> X is an open subfunctor of Y.
declarations.note: Open subfunctor: each x in X(A) has an ideal I with phi(x) in V(B) iff phi(I)B = B.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of group theory (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: index_pi_univ
declarations.says: For finitely many groups G_i with subgroups H_i, the index of prod_i H_i in prod_i G_i is prod_i [G_i : H_i].

entries.known_result: header: a tame pair with residually distinct conjugate eigenvalues spans all matrices of a lattice (textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: IsLatticeIn.span_eq_top_of_tame_pair
declarations.says: R: G -> GL_n(Qbar_l) with an O-lattice model u: G -> M_n(O) (O integers of a finite extension of Q_l). If R(gamma)^q = R(phi^-1 gamma phi), R(gamma^{q^n}) = R(gamma) and R(gamma) has an eigenvalue zeta in O with zeta^{q^i} (i < n) pairwise distinct mod the maximal ideal, then u(G) spans M_n(O) over O and u(phi^-n) is scalar.
declarations.note: Folklore argument (eigenline idempotents of u(gamma) by Lagrange interpolation with unit denominators, cyclically permuted by u(phi)); not a textbook statement, about half a page; the write-up must prove it.

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of linear algebra and matrices, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: G.ofMat
declarations.says: For a CM field E and signs s: the element of the adelic unitary group G(E, s) given by an adelic matrix m with m*εm = ε, ε the standard diagonal hermitian form of signs s.

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of linear algebra and matrices, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: norm_mulVec_le
declarations.says: Over an ultrametric normed field, if |M_ij| ≤ c for all entries (c ≥ 0), then ‖Mx‖ ≤ c‖x‖ in the sup norm.

entries.known_result: none named (header: crude bound for the class number by degree and discriminant)

declarations.name: classNumber_le
declarations.says: The class number of a number field F of degree n is at most (2ⁿ|disc F|)^{n+1}.
declarations.reference: Minkowski's bound, e.g. J. Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory (1999), ch. I §6
declarations.note: Crude consequence of Minkowski's bound (every class has an ideal of norm ≤ the bound; count ideals containing an integer).

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of algebraic number theory, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: exists_procyclic_generator
declarations.says: A continuous homomorphism κ from a compact group Γ to ℤ_ℓ^× (values ≡ 1 mod 4 if ℓ = 2) has procyclic image: some γ ∈ Γ is such that every open subgroup containing γ and ker κ is all of Γ.
declarations.note: ℤ_ℓ^× (ℓ odd) and 1 + 4ℤ₂ are procyclic, and closed subgroups of procyclic groups are procyclic.

entries.known_result: header: symmetry of zeros of Dirichlet L-functions from the functional equation, imprimitive characters included

declarations.name: LFunction_one_sub_eq_zero
declarations.says: Functional equation of Dirichlet L-functions (consequence): if L(s, χ) = 0 with Re s ≠ 0 and s ≠ 1, then s is a pole of the gamma factor of χ (where Mathlib sets it to 0) or L(1 − s, χ⁻¹) = 0.
declarations.reference: H. Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory (3rd ed. 2000), ch. 9
declarations.relation: weaker form: only the symmetry of zeros s ↔ 1 − s, χ ↔ χ⁻¹, for every character (imprimitive ones included), off Re s = 0 and the poles of the gamma factor
declarations.note: Uses Mathlib's functional equation for primitive characters (completedLFunction_one_sub) and the nonvanishing of the extra Euler factors off Re s = 0. This is how RH/GRH follow from the zero-free half-plane Re s > 1/2.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of linear algebra (textbook or folklore); part of Green's characters of GL_n(F_q) (see LabelDegree). This file: cuspidal class functions vanish unless the characteristic polynomial is a prime power.

declarations.name: Hall.IsCuspidal.exists_charpoly_eq_pow
declarations.says: Over a finite field k, a cuspidal class function F on endomorphisms (all block averages over block-triangular endomorphisms with two nonzero blocks vanish) is zero at the class of g unless the characteristic polynomial of g is a power of an irreducible polynomial.
declarations.note: The header classes it as folklore; for cuspidal characters of GL_n(F_q) this is the known vanishing off primary classes (Green 1955). Here for class functions on all endomorphisms.

entries.known_result: header: part of Green's characters of GL_n(F_q) and the parabolic-induction ring (see LabelDegree).

declarations.name: root_pow_card_pow_pred_eq_one
declarations.says: A root x of an irreducible P over k with P(0) ≠ 0 satisfies x^{|k|^{deg P}−1} = 1, and |k|^{deg P} ≥ 2.

entries.known_result: header: part of exponents, U-operators and spherical vectors at pro-p Iwahori level; conjugacy in I t I (see Tadic/ChainLemma: Casselman 1980; Haines–Kottwitz–Prasad; Görtz–Haines–Kottwitz–Reuman 2010).

declarations.name: heckeCoset_mem_parahoricEigenspace
declarations.says: For a smooth representation, a uniformiser ϖ and a function χ, the pro-p Iwahori Hecke operator of diag(ϖ,1,…,1) preserves the pro-p-Iwahori fixed vectors on which every integral k fixing the first coordinate line mod ϖ acts by χ of its top-left entry.
declarations.note: Double-coset computation.

entries.known_result: header: part of exponents, U-operators and spherical vectors at pro-p Iwahori level (see Tadic/ChainLemma).

declarations.name: proIwahori_le_blockParahoric
declarations.says: The pro-p Iwahori subgroup of GL_N(F) lies in the block parahoric attached to any block labelling c that is decreasing along the order of indices.

entries.known_result: Shintani descent for GL_n(F_q), with the lift named (Shintani 1976; Silberger–Zink 2008, Thm 5.1). New uses only one unfolding lemma.

declarations.name: evalGL_detChar
declarations.says: The class function attached to χ∘det takes the value χ(det g) at g.
declarations.note: unfolding

entries.known_result: Comparison of simple trace formulas for unitary groups that differ only at real places (Labesse 2011, Thm 5.4; Arthur–Clozel 1989, ch. 1, Lemmas 2.4–2.6); Selberg principle.

declarations.name: Space.exists_trace_eq
declarations.says: Comparison of simple trace formulas: for E ⊇ μ_5040 with an even number of infinite places, a level K, h such that every point of hK has irreducible characteristic polynomial at some finite place, B ≥ 16[E:ℚ](n+1)³ and gap H ≥ 500n³+10n⁵, the trace Σ_i⟨b_i, h·b_i⟩ over an orthonormal basis of K-fixed forms of type e_l (e_l a cusp kernel of order B, l of gap H) is the same for all signatures s and hermitian spaces V.
declarations.reference: J.-P. Labesse, Changement de base CM et séries discrètes (2011); J. Arthur, L. Clozel, Simple algebras, base change, and the advanced theory of the trace formula (1989)
declarations.place: Labesse 2011, Thm 5.4 and its proof; Arthur–Clozel 1989, ch. 1, Lemmas 2.4–2.6 (as cited in the header; authors' check: compared)
declarations.relation: special case: test functions elliptic at a finite place, very regular discrete-series idempotent kernels at the real places, CM fields containing μ_5040; only equality of these Hecke traces across inner forms differing at real places
declarations.note: Convergence by packing, no truncation or endoscopy (header).

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Crystalline comparison: p-adic étale cohomology with good reduction is crystalline (known result; see Lib.PadicComparison.Crystalline.CrystallineClasses).

declarations.name: CrysTest.restrictScalars
declarations.says: Restriction of scalars along S → B, from the category of p-torsion-free p-complete B-algebras (the authors' 'crystalline tests') to the corresponding category over S.

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Congruence relation for the crystalline Frobenius (known result; see Lib.PadicComparison.CrystallineFrobenius.CrystallineCohomology).

declarations.name: ellAdicCohom.transfer
declarations.says: Transfer for a finite Galois covering: if c: W → Y is a covering of proper R-schemes with finite group Δ, then c^*: V^n(Y) → V^n(W) on rational ℓ-adic cohomology over Ω = ℚ̄ is injective and its image contains every Δ-invariant class.
declarations.reference: A. Grothendieck, Sur quelques points d'algèbre homologique, Tôhoku Math. J. 9 (1957) (cohomology of a quotient by a finite group)
declarations.relation: special case: rational ℓ-adic coefficients, covering in the authors' sense (Δ acts over c, c surjective, geometric fibres in characteristic 0 are Δ-torsors), V^n the authors' cohomology computed on test rings (its equality with étale cohomology is neither proved nor used)
declarations.note: image ⊆ invariants is automatic, so c^* identifies V^n(Y) with V^n(W)^Δ; proof uses the transfer map of Lib.Cohomology.Etale.ContinuityAtlas; unconfirmed guess for the classical statement

entries.known_result: Almost acyclicity of the structure sheaf for the v-topology

declarations.name: Comparison.IsBijective.transfer
declarations.says: Formal transfer: for comparisons c: F → G and c': F' → G, maps u: Y → h_B, v: Y → h_B' and a bijection γ: F(B) → F'(B') under which x and γx give the same section of G at each point of Y, if c is bijective along u then c' is bijective along v.
declarations.note: a commutative square of bijections; the file's known result (almost acyclicity of the v-structure sheaf, Scholze diamonds Thm 8.7) is not this declaration

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Hodge–Tate map from Hodge cohomology to p-adic étale cohomology (known result; see Lib.PadicComparison.HodgeTate.HodgeTateVectors).

declarations.name: thickeningOver.proj
declarations.says: The natural map of k-algebras W(R^♭)[1/p]/(ker θ)² → R[1/p] induced by Fontaine's θ, natural in the p-adic test R (the first-order thickening of the generic fibre maps onto it).

entries.known_result: header: Part of: Hodge–Tate map from Hodge cohomology to p-adic étale cohomology (known result; see Lib.PadicComparison.HodgeTate.HodgeTateVectors).

declarations.name: PairH.map
declarations.says: For a map α: N' → N of abelian-group-valued functors on k-algebras, the k-linear pull-back on total Ext groups Ext^*(N∘B, F) → Ext^*(N'∘B, F), where B is (S, M) ↦ B_{S,M}.

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of algebraic geometry, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: IsInfinitesimal.smul
declarations.says: If y is an infinitesimal point of the group object A along ψ: C → C' (it reduces to 0), so is c·y for c in a ring O acting on A.

entries.known_result: Fourier coefficients of theta lifts as periods over stabilisers

declarations.name: period_eq_zero
declarations.says: Fourier coefficients of theta lifts as periods: if Y on U(I_n), n = n₁ + n₂, is continuous, left-invariant under rational points, of level K₀ above T ∪ T̄, and all its theta descents to the split group of n₁ hyperbolic planes (character υ^{n₁}, data vacuum at T ∪ T̄) vanish, then ∫_{[U(I_{n₂})]} Y(h₁u) du = 0 for every h₁.
declarations.reference: P. Walls, The theta correspondence, periods of automorphic forms and special values of standard automorphic L-functions, arXiv:1501.01565 (2015); S. Rallis, On the Howe duality conjecture, Compositio Math. 51 (1984) 333–399
declarations.relation: weaker form: only the consequence 'all descents vanish ⇒ the U(I_{n₂})-period vanishes', from one non-degenerate Fourier coefficient (definite U(I_n) to the split group, unfolded once by Witt's theorem), not the general period formula
declarations.note: Header cites Walls, Prop. 2.1.1; the file is outside the authors' REFERENCES check.

entries.known_result: Frobenius' dimension formula and irreducibility of the theta group

declarations.name: IsAppellHumbert.isCompact_range_norm_thetaShift
declarations.says: For a theta function f of Appell–Humbert data (B, χ) on V/L, the set of values |exp(−B(a, a)/2)·f(a)|, a ∈ V, is compact (the function is L-periodic and continuous).
declarations.note: The file's known result (Frobenius' dimension formula, irreducibility of the theta group) is not among the used declarations.

entries.known_result: header: part of good reduction of unitary PEL abelian varieties, in analytic form (see Lib.Shimura.GoodReduction.ArcReduction)

declarations.name: LatticeForm.sizes
declarations.says: For a valuation v on ℂ and a lattice form B on V/L: the set of size functions x ↦ v((translate of f by x)(0)) on torsion points, for theta functions f of B with a multiplier χ of ample type.

entries.known_result: header: part of integral Kuga–Sato models for GU(1, n−1) with level covers and congruence relation (see Lib.Shimura.IntegralModel.ModelExistence)

declarations.name: PEL.IsGoodAt
declarations.says: A finite place w of E is good for the PEL datum D: w contains neither r nor |T|, and for some prime p and integer b, w ∋ p, β − b; β − b is coprime to β̄ − b; 𝔑 is coprime to w·(p, β̄ − b); and another place v ≠ w contains p and β − b.
declarations.note: Technical condition of the authors' PEL data (β = 1 − β̄, level 𝔑, odd group T, paddings) used for integral models and the congruence relation.

entries.known_result: header: part of moduli of abelian varieties by theta values (theta-null embedding, universal family) (see Lib.Shimura.ThetaModuli.UniversalFamily)

declarations.name: LineBundle.IsHomogCoords.pi
declarations.says: If for each l the functions θ(·, w_l) are homogeneous coordinates for the line bundle M_l along t, then the products ∏_l θ(μ_l, w_l) are homogeneous coordinates for the external tensor product of the M_l (Segre).
declarations.note: Unfolding of the definition.

entries.known_result: header: general lemmas of algebraic geometry; part of moduli of abelian varieties by theta values (see Lib.Shimura.ThetaModuli.UniversalFamily); this file: schematic density of points passes to stalks and fibre products

declarations.name: IsSeparatingFamily.prod
declarations.says: Let S be reduced, locally noetherian, with a dense finite family of points; A, B flat and locally of finite type over S, A reduced. If complex points y_w of B are dense in B (B reduced) and, for each w, points e_w(v) are dense in the reduced fibre product A ×_S T_w, then the points (e_w(v), y_w) are dense in A ×_S B and A ×_S B is reduced.
declarations.note: 'Separating family' = reduced scheme with a dense family of complex points. An EGA IV-type statement on reducedness and density in flat fibre products; the write-up must read it or find a source.

entries.known_result: header: part of moduli of abelian varieties by theta values (theta-null embedding, universal family) (see Lib.Shimura.ThetaModuli.UniversalFamily)

declarations.name: HasProjEmbedding.pi
declarations.says: If an S-scheme W has a closed immersion over S into a finite fibre product of S-schemes each closed in a projective space over S, then W is closed in a projective space over S (Segre embedding).
declarations.reference: R. Hartshorne, Algebraic Geometry (1977), ch. II

entries.known_result: none named (header: general lemmas of algebraic geometry, textbook or folklore)

declarations.name: HasGoodReduction.pow
declarations.says: If the theta data (B, χ) have good reduction at the valuation v with parameter r (ample type, NL^∨ ⊂ L with v(N) = 1, v(r) = 1, r > 1, multiplicative sup norm), then so do (r^j B, χ^{r^j}) for every j.

entries.known_result: header: part of complex uniformisation of PEL abelian varieties; Appell–Humbert; finite class number (see Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert)

declarations.name: ModuliPoint.act
declarations.says: The right action on moduli points: a·(g, α) = (xg, ℓ, (α_i P_i)) for a = (x, ℓ, P), a unitary similitude g ∈ GU⁺ and integers α_i of E acting on the marked points P_i.

entries.known_result: Siegel's formula for representing a number by a hermitian form, and local density bounds

declarations.name: classSum_norm_eq
declarations.says: Siegel's formula (one vector) for the norm form x*x = sum x_i x_i-bar, n >= 3, over a CM field E: for an open level K and K-invariant Schwartz-Bruhat Phi_0 >= 0 and alpha = alpha-bar totally positive, the representation sums converge and their K-class sum equals (class sum of 1) |D_E|^{1/4} prod_v pi^n alpha_v^{n-1}/(n-1)! times the adelic Fourier integral int int Phi_0(x) psi_f(z(x*x - alpha)/2) dx dz.
declarations.reference: A. Weil, Sur la formule de Siegel dans la theorie des groupes classiques, Acta Math. 113 (1965); classical case C. L. Siegel, Ann. of Math. 36 (1935); hermitian: H. Braun, Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg 14 (1941)
declarations.place: Weil 1965, n° 52, Thm 5 (authors' check: compared, recorded in REFERENCES.md for Lib/SiegelWeil/Formula/SiegelWeilFormula, whose Siegel–Weil formula this file specializes; OneVector's own citation was not checked)
declarations.relation: special case: the standard norm form in n >= 3 variables over a CM field with WeilData (enough roots of unity, splitting character, self-dual lattice), any level and test function; singular series left as one adelic Fourier integral, not factored into local densities
declarations.note: Header cites 'Weil 1965, Thm 5 for one vector'; REFERENCES.md confirms Weil 1965 n. 52 Thm 5 only for Lib/SiegelWeil/Formula/SiegelWeilFormula, not for this file. Derived here from the Siegel-Weil formula of that file.

entries.known_result: Strong approximation for isotropic unitary groups (Kneser 1965; Shimura 1964; survey Rapinchuk 2013), in the form of a constancy criterion

declarations.name: IsAutFunction.apply_eq_apply_one
declarations.says: Strong approximation, constancy form: let D be continuous on [U(W)], W split along a line, right invariant under the points supported on S cup S-bar (S nonempty) and under the integral points off S. If invariance under the unipotent radical makes D on the Levi independent of the torus, then D is constant.
declarations.reference: M. Kneser, Starke Approximation in algebraischen Gruppen I, J. reine angew. Math. 218 (1965); G. Shimura, Arithmetic of unitary groups, Ann. of Math. 79 (1964)
declarations.relation: weaker form: a constancy criterion for automorphic functions on U(W) (W isotropic along a line) of the kind strong approximation gives, proved directly with unipotent radicals and rational quasi-reflections; the torus-independence is a hypothesis
declarations.note: Header: 'Known result: strong approximation for isotropic unitary groups'.

entries.known_result: Part of: adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/PairSplitting)

declarations.name: stdLattice.isCompact_stdLattice
declarations.says: The standard lattice Ô^ι is compact in the finite adelic vectors.
declarations.note: Tychonoff.

entries.known_result: Part of: theta kernels of unitary dual pairs: functoriality, seesaw, growth, rapid decay (stated in Lib/Weil/DualPair/KernelDecay)

declarations.name: exists_level_pairWeil
declarations.says: Every f in the finite part of 𝒮(Hom(S,T)) is fixed by K × K′ under the pair Weil representation, for some open subgroups K, K′ of the two finite adelic unitary groups (smoothness).

entries.known_result: A step of the proof of: theta kernels of unitary dual pairs (Lib/Weil/DualPair/KernelDecay)

declarations.name: DescentsVanish
declarations.says: Predicate: all theta descents g ↦ ∫ θ(ω_{a,1}(g,h)f) Y(h) dh of Y from U(V) to U(W) vanish, for all data f equal to their P^S-projection (vacuum at the places of S ∪ S̄).

entries.known_result: Part of: Schrödinger and mixed models of the Weil representation (see Lib/Weil/MixedModel/ZeroTermLaw); this file: smooth compactly supported sections are slices of one rapid vector

declarations.name: MixedModel.exists_section
declarations.says: In a mixed Schrödinger–Fock model, for τ smooth with compact support, u(x) unitary depending smoothly on x, and ξ rapid, there is a rapid Fock vector Φ whose slice at every x is τ(x)·ω₀(u(x))ξ.
declarations.note: Analogue of 'a smooth compactly supported family of Schwartz vectors is one Schwartz vector' in the authors' L¹ model; built by an explicit Fourier-transform integral (about 60 lines). The write-up must give this construction or a source.

entries.known_result: Part of: commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n and the Eichler commutation relation (see Lib/General/LinearAlgebra/ColumnLattices)

declarations.name: AutChar.frobValue
declarations.says: For an automorphic character a of U(1) and rank n, the number χ(ϖ_w)·q_w^{n/2}, where χ(x) = a(x/x̄)·υ(x)^{−n} is the associated Hecke character and ϖ_w the chosen uniformizer at w.
